title: Defensive Tracking Footwork
primarySkill: Defensive tracking footwork
objective: Develop the balanced footwork required to track a moving opponent while remaining able to react safely to changes of direction.
groundSize: Multiple lanes measuring approximately 8 metres long and 3 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 1 – Simple organisation with minimal observation or intervention
setup:
Construct parallel lanes approximately 8 metres long and 3 metres wide.
Place one attacker and one defender at the beginning of each lane.
The attacker begins approximately 1.5 metres in front of the defender and faces the same direction.
Mark a finishing line at the end of each lane.
Ensure neighbouring lanes are separated sufficiently to prevent collisions.
Players work in pairs and alternate attacking and defending roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the attacker moves forward through the lane at approximately 50 per cent speed.
The attacker may change pace and move laterally but must remain inside the lane.
The defender tracks the attacker without making contact, attempting to remain approximately one arm’s length away.
The defender keeps their body square enough to respond in either direction and avoids crossing their feet.
The attacker continues until reaching the finishing line.
The defender earns one point by remaining balanced and within one arm’s length when the attacker crosses the line.
Players walk back outside the lane, exchange roles and repeat.
Complete four to six repetitions in each role.
coachingPoints: Adopt a balanced stance with knees bent, chest upright and weight through the balls of the feet.
Use short, controlled steps rather than long strides when close to the attacker.
Keep the feet moving and avoid planting both feet during the attacker’s change of direction.
Watch the attacker’s hips and trunk rather than reacting only to the head or football.
Maintain enough space to react without allowing the attacker to accelerate freely.
Accelerate when the attacker moves away and shorten the steps when closing.
Avoid crossing the feet during lateral movement.
Keep the head upright to preserve vision and awareness.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders maintain a stable athletic stance.
Whether defenders remain within an effective tracking distance.
Whether players can change direction without crossing their feet.
Whether defenders shorten their stride as they approach the attacker.
Whether players keep their head and eyes up throughout the movement.
Whether the attacker can change pace without the defender becoming upright or unbalanced.

commonErrors.error: Defender stands upright while tracking.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips, bend the knees and keep the chest over the feet.

commonErrors.error: Defender watches the attacker’s feet.
commonErrors.correction: Direct the defender’s eyes towards the hips and centre of mass.

commonErrors.error: Defender crosses their feet when moving sideways.
commonErrors.correction: Use short lateral adjustment steps and keep the feet underneath the body.

commonErrors.error: Defender moves too close and is beaten by one step.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain one arm’s length until the attacker’s movement becomes predictable.

commonErrors.error: Defender takes long strides near the attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the steps before entering tackling distance.

progressions: Allow the attacker to use sharper changes of direction and greater speed.
Introduce a football so the defender must track the ball carrier’s hips rather than follow the football.
Have the coach call a colour at the finishing end that the attacker must move towards.
Reduce the lane width to demand more precise defensive footwork.
regressions: Reduce the attacker to walking speed.
Allow only one pre-planned change of direction.
Increase the lane width and shorten the working distance.
Have the defender shadow the attacker from beside them rather than from behind.
successIndicators: Remain balanced during changes of direction.
Keep their feet active and underneath their body.
Track within an effective defensive distance.
React to the attacker’s hips rather than guessing.
matchApplication: Effective tackling begins before contact. Defenders must track an opponent’s movement, control the closing space and remain balanced enough to react when a ball carrier changes direction, accelerates or attempts to evade. This drill establishes the footwork required to contain an opponent before attempting a legal tackle.

title: Closing Space and Approach Angle
primarySkill: Closing space on an opponent
objective: Teach defenders to close space quickly before approaching under control on an angle that limits the ball carrier’s available escape routes.
groundSize: Triangular working areas approximately 8 metres long and 6 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Create triangular working areas with one starting cone for the defender and two exit gates for the attacker.
Position the defender 6–8 metres directly in front of the attacker.
Place the two exit gates approximately 4 metres apart at the opposite end of the area.
The attacker begins with a football and may attempt to run through either exit gate.
A feeder or coach stands behind the defender and signals which gate is active when required.
Organise players in groups of three: attacker, defender and feeder.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker begins stationary with the football.
On the coach’s signal, the attacker moves towards either exit gate at approximately 60 per cent speed.
The defender accelerates to close the initial space.
When approximately 2–3 metres from the attacker, the defender decelerates and approaches on an angle that directs the attacker away from the centre of the area.
No contact is permitted.
The defender scores one point by forcing the attacker outside the marked gate or causing the attacker to stop, retreat or change direction.
The attacker scores one point by entering the active gate under control.
Players rotate from attacker to defender to feeder after each repetition.
Complete six to eight repetitions per group.
coachingPoints: Accelerate aggressively while the attacker is outside immediate evasion distance.
Decelerate before arriving so the defender can respond to a sidestep.
Approach from slightly inside the attacker’s line to protect the most dangerous space.
Use the boundary or cone line as an additional defender.
Keep shoulders and hips stable rather than lunging towards the football.
Maintain an arm’s-length buffer until the attacker commits to a direction.
Angle the run to reduce two escape options to one.
Finish the approach balanced and ready to tackle, even though contact is not permitted.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders accelerate during the initial closing phase.
Whether defenders decelerate before reaching the attacker.
Whether the approach angle protects the central or dangerous space.
Whether defenders remain balanced when the attacker changes direction.
Whether defenders force predictable movement rather than chasing from behind.
Whether attackers must alter their original path because of the defender’s position.

commonErrors.error: Defender approaches directly and leaves both sides open.
commonErrors.correction: Enter on a slight angle and deliberately protect the most dangerous route.

commonErrors.error: Defender runs at full speed until reaching the attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Begin decelerating 2–3 metres away and shorten the final steps.

commonErrors.error: Defender follows the football rather than controlling space.
commonErrors.correction: Track the attacker’s hips and defend the preferred exit lane.

commonErrors.error: Defender turns their body fully sideways.
commonErrors.correction: Remain square enough to react in either direction.

commonErrors.error: Defender reaches with one hand despite the no-contact rule.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the hands ready but maintain body position and foot movement.

progressions: Increase the attacker’s speed.
Allow the attacker to use a handball fake or baulk.
Move the drill closer to a boundary line and require the defender to force the attacker towards it.
Add a second defender arriving from behind to encourage coordinated closing angles.
regressions: Predetermine the attacker’s exit gate.
Reduce the attacker to jogging speed.
Shorten the starting distance between attacker and defender.
Widen the defender’s protected gate to make the required angle more obvious.
successIndicators: Protect the more dangerous attacking route.
Force the attacker towards a predictable exit.
Finish the approach balanced and ready for legal contact.
matchApplication: Defenders regularly need to close down ball carriers in open play without overcommitting. An effective approach angle can force the ball carrier towards the boundary, away from the corridor or onto their non-preferred side while allowing the defender to arrive under control and complete the tackle.

title: Breakdown Position and Balance
primarySkill: Establishing a balanced breakdown position
objective: Develop the ability to decelerate from a running approach and establish a stable body position from which the defender can move, contain or tackle safely.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 10 metres long and 4 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Mark a starting cone for the defender.
Place a breakdown line 6 metres in front of the starting cone.
Position an attacker approximately 1.5 metres beyond the breakdown line.
Place three coloured movement gates to the attacker’s left, right and rear.
A coach or feeder stands where all gates are visible.
Players work in groups of three and rotate through defender, attacker and feeder roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defender begins at the starting cone in an athletic stance.
On the coach’s signal, the defender accelerates towards the breakdown line.
Before crossing the line, the defender uses several short steps to reduce speed and establish a balanced tackling stance.
The coach calls or points to one of the coloured gates.
The attacker moves two or three steps towards that gate.
The defender reacts and mirrors the movement without making contact.
The repetition ends when the defender reaches the gate beside or in front of the attacker while remaining balanced.
Players reset and repeat three times before rotating roles.
Complete two rotations through each role.
coachingPoints: Begin decelerating before reaching the breakdown line.
Use several short steps rather than one heavy stopping step.
Position the feet slightly wider than shoulder width.
Bend through the knees and hips while keeping the chest upright.
Keep the head up and eyes on the attacker’s hips.
Distribute weight evenly enough to move left, right or backwards.
Keep the hands in front and ready without reaching.
Avoid allowing the knees to collapse inward during deceleration.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender begins decelerating before the marked line.
Whether the final stance permits movement in either direction.
Whether the defender’s knees, hips and feet remain aligned.
Whether the player’s head stays upright.
Whether defenders react from balance rather than lunging.
Whether players can repeat the action without losing technical quality.

commonErrors.error: Defender stops with one long, heavy stride.
commonErrors.correction: Use three or four shorter steps to absorb speed gradually.

commonErrors.error: Feet finish too narrow.
commonErrors.correction: Land with the feet just wider than shoulder width.

commonErrors.error: Weight remains on the heels.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the chest slightly forward and pressure through the balls of the feet.

commonErrors.error: Player bends at the waist and drops the head.
commonErrors.correction: Bend through the knees and hips while keeping the eyes forward.

commonErrors.error: Defender becomes stationary after breaking down.
commonErrors.correction: Keep small adjustment steps active while reading the attacker.

progressions: Increase the defender’s starting speed.
Delay the coach’s movement cue until the defender reaches the breakdown line.
Allow the attacker to select any gate without a coach’s call.
Add a football and permit a handball fake before the attacker changes direction.
regressions: Begin the defender only 3 metres from the breakdown line.
Remove the attacker and have the defender react directly to the coach’s signal.
Predetermine the gate before the defender begins.
Perform the action at walking speed.
successIndicators: Finish with stable foot, knee and hip alignment.
Keep their head upright and vision forward.
React in either direction without slipping or crossing their feet.
Maintain balance throughout the entire approach.
matchApplication: The breakdown position is the transition between closing space and making a defensive decision. A defender who arrives balanced can react to a baulk, contain the ball carrier, apply pressure to a disposal or enter a tackle legally without making reckless high contact.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle

title: Mirror, Contain and Corral
primarySkill: Containing an evasive ball carrier
objective: Teach defenders to remain patient, mirror an opponent and reduce the ball carrier’s space without lunging or attempting premature contact.
groundSize: Squares approximately 6 metres by 6 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Mark multiple 6-metre by 6-metre squares.
Place one attacker with a football and one defender inside each square.
Identify one side of each square as the attacker’s scoring line.
The defender begins approximately 2 metres from the attacker.
Position waiting pairs outside the square, clear of the active area.
The defender may not make contact during the initial version.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker attempts to carry the football across the scoring line.
The attacker may move laterally, retreat, change pace or use a controlled baulk.
The defender mirrors the attacker and attempts to remain between the attacker and the scoring line.
The defender must keep moving their feet and may not reach, hold or make contact.
The defender scores one point by containing the attacker for five seconds or forcing them outside the square.
The attacker scores one point by crossing the scoring line under control.
The repetition stops immediately when either player scores.
Players exchange roles after each repetition.
Complete four to six repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Maintain patience and avoid committing before the attacker has selected a direction.
Keep the hips low and the feet active.
Stay goalside or between the attacker and the protected space.
Move laterally with short adjustment steps.
Give ground when necessary rather than lunging and being beaten.
Reduce the attacker’s space gradually.
Watch the hips and trunk rather than reacting to the football.
Use the square’s side boundary to restrict the attacker’s movement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders remain between the attacker and the scoring line.
Whether defenders maintain active feet throughout the contest.
Whether players lunge when the attacker presents a fake.
Whether defenders can concede a small amount of ground while preserving position.
Whether attackers are forced towards the side of the square.
Whether defenders recognise when the attacker has run out of space.

commonErrors.error: Defender lunges at the first baulk.
commonErrors.correction: Remain patient and move the feet until the attacker commits.

commonErrors.error: Defender reaches instead of moving laterally.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the hands ready and use the feet to maintain position.

commonErrors.error: Defender becomes square and flat-footed.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a low stance with small active steps.

commonErrors.error: Defender retreats too quickly and gives away the scoring line.
commonErrors.correction: Give only the ground required to remain balanced.

commonErrors.error: Defender allows the attacker back into central space.
commonErrors.correction: Angle the body to continue directing the attacker towards the boundary.

progressions: Reduce the square to 5 metres by 5 metres.
Allow the defender to apply a two-handed touch between the shoulders and hips once the attacker commits.
Introduce a five-second time limit for the attacker.
Add a support player outside the square who becomes available for a handball.
regressions: Predetermine the attacker’s first movement direction.
Increase the square to 8 metres by 8 metres.
Reduce the attacker to jogging speed.
Remove the football so the attacker focuses only on movement.
successIndicators: Remain goalside of the ball carrier.
Keep their feet active instead of reaching.
Delay committing until the attacker reveals a direction.
Force the ball carrier towards restricted space.
Contain the attacker without illegal contact.
matchApplication: Defenders often need to corral an opponent while teammates recover defensive position. Remaining patient can prevent the ball carrier from entering the corridor, taking an uncontested shot, drawing a high-contact free kick or escaping through an overcommitted tackle attempt.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle

title: Safe Contact Shape with Tackle Bags
primarySkill: Safe initial tackling contact
objective: Introduce a safe and repeatable body shape for legal tackling contact using stationary tackle bags before players tackle a partner.
groundSize: Contact stations approximately 5 metres long and 4 metres wide.
equipment: Optional mouthguards where required by club policy
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Create several contact stations with one tackle bag at each station.
A holder stands behind each bag in a stable position with feet staggered.
The tackler begins 2 metres in front of the bag.
A coach should be positioned where head placement and body alignment can be observed clearly.
Players rotate through tackler, bag holder and recovery roles.
Under 8 players should use soft shields, walking speed and shoulder placement only.
howTheDrillWorks:
The tackler begins in a balanced stance facing the tackle bag.
On the coach’s signal, the tackler takes two or three controlled steps towards the bag.
The player lowers their centre of gravity by bending through the knees and hips.
The tackler places the near shoulder into the lower half of the bag while keeping the head safely to one side.
The arms wrap around the bag immediately after shoulder contact.
The player takes two short driving steps while the bag holder provides light resistance.
The tackler stops on the coach’s call, maintains balance and releases.
Players reset before repeating from the opposite shoulder.
Complete three to five repetitions on each side before rotating.
coachingPoints: Make contact with the shoulder rather than the head or extended arms.
Keep the head upright and positioned safely to the side of the bag.
Contact below the shoulders and above the knees.
Bend through the knees and hips rather than folding at the waist.
Place the lead foot close enough to create a stable base.
Wrap both arms immediately after the shoulder makes contact.
Drive with short steps instead of launching or leaving the ground.
Stop and release immediately on the coach’s call.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the head remains to the side of the contact point.
Whether the shoulder contacts the legal target area.
Whether the tackler bends through the knees and hips.
Whether both arms wrap after contact.
Whether the feet continue moving without the player launching.
Whether players can perform the technique equally from both sides.

commonErrors.error: Tackler places the head in front of the bag.
commonErrors.correction: Move the head firmly to the side before shoulder contact.

commonErrors.error: Player reaches with the arms before making body contact.
commonErrors.correction: Step close, make shoulder contact and then wrap.

commonErrors.error: Tackler bends at the waist and drops the eyes.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the knees and hips while keeping the chest and eyes up.

commonErrors.error: Player launches from too far away.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the approach distance and place the lead foot closer to the bag.

commonErrors.error: Contact is too high.
commonErrors.correction: Aim the shoulder at the lower half of the bag within the legal tackling zone.

progressions: Allow the bag holder to move slowly forwards or sideways.
Add a football secured against the tackle bag to provide a visual target.
Increase the approach to 3–4 metres while preserving controlled speed.
Finish with the tackler holding the bag stable for two seconds before releasing.
regressions: Begin with stationary shoulder placement and no approach.
Remove the driving steps and rehearse only contact, wrap and release.
Use a lighter hand shield rather than a full tackle bag.
Have the coach physically guide the player’s head and shoulder position at walking speed.
successIndicators: Position the head safely to the side.
Contact with the shoulder inside the legal tackling zone.
Wrap both arms immediately after contact.
Maintain a stable base and active feet.
matchApplication: The drill introduces the body shape used when tackling an opponent from the front or side. Safe head placement, legal shoulder contact and immediate arm wrapping reduce the likelihood of high contact, missed tackles and unsafe collisions.

title: Stationary Wrap and Clamp
primarySkill: Securing a ball carrier with the arms
objective: Teach players to wrap and clamp a stationary opponent securely without using excessive force, lifting, twisting or taking the opponent to ground.
groundSize: Partner stations approximately 4 metres by 4 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Players form pairs matched as closely as practical for size and physical maturity.
One player begins as the stationary ball carrier and holds a football against the torso.
The tackler begins beside the ball carrier with the near shoulder lightly touching the legal tackle area.
Each pair works inside a clearly separated station.
The ball carrier remains upright and provides only light resistance.
The coach establishes a clear release command before the drill begins.
howTheDrillWorks:
The tackler begins with the head safely positioned to the side of the ball carrier’s body.
On the coach’s signal, the tackler wraps both arms around the ball carrier between the shoulders and knees.
The tackler closes the space between their chest and the opponent.
The hands connect or the forearms clamp firmly without pulling the opponent backwards.
The ball carrier attempts to rotate the upper body slightly while keeping both feet grounded.
The tackler uses body connection and arm tension to prevent the rotation for two seconds.
No lifting, slinging, driving or ground contact is permitted.
On the release command, the tackler immediately lets go and steps away.
Players repeat from the opposite side before exchanging roles.
Complete four repetitions from each side.
coachingPoints: Match players appropriately for size, strength and confidence.
Place the head to the side before applying pressure.
Wrap below the shoulders and above the knees.
Close the chest-to-opponent space so the tackle is not dependent on arm strength alone.
Clamp with both arms while keeping the shoulders relaxed.
Keep both feet grounded and the body balanced.
Do not pull, lift, twist or rotate the ball carrier.
Release immediately when instructed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the tackler establishes safe head position before wrapping.
Whether both arms surround the opponent in the legal tackle area.
Whether the tackler closes body space rather than holding with fingertips.
Whether the ball carrier remains upright and balanced.
Whether tacklers avoid lifting, twisting or dragging.
Whether every player releases immediately on command.

commonErrors.error: Tackler holds with the hands only.
commonErrors.correction: Bring the chest closer and wrap with the forearms and upper arms.

commonErrors.error: Arms slide above the shoulders.
commonErrors.correction: Reset the grip lower around the torso.

commonErrors.error: Tackler squeezes while standing upright and distant.
commonErrors.correction: Bend the knees and close the body space.

commonErrors.error: Player pulls the opponent backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain the opponent’s upright position and clamp without dragging.

commonErrors.error: Tackler is slow to release.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce that the drill ends immediately on the release command.

progressions: Allow the ball carrier to make one controlled step before the tackler clamps.
Have the ball carrier attempt a slow handball while the tackler controls the arms.
Begin with the tackler half a step away before entering and wrapping.
Extend the secure hold to three seconds while preserving safe technique.
regressions: Practise the arm wrap around a tackle bag.
Allow the tackler to begin with both arms already positioned.
Remove all resistance from the ball carrier.
Use a standing partner brace in which the ball carrier verbally checks the tackler’s head position.
successIndicators: Wrap with both arms in the legal tackle area.
Prevent controlled rotation without pulling or lifting.
matchApplication: A secure arm wrap prevents opponents from breaking weak tackles or freeing the arms for an effective disposal. The drill teaches players to control an opponent legally without introducing unnecessary force or unsafe ground contact.
relatedDrills: TK-005 – Safe Contact Shape with Tackle Bags

title: Side-On Entry and Head Placement
primarySkill: Safe side-on tackle entry
objective: Develop safe side-on entry technique by coordinating the approach angle, lead foot, shoulder contact and head placement against a slowly moving partner.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 6 metres long and 3 metres wide.
equipment: Optional soft contact vests or shields
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Create multiple lanes approximately 6 metres long.
Place one ball carrier at the start of each lane.
The tackler begins beside and slightly behind the ball carrier.
A coach or safety observer stands outside the lane.
The ball carrier moves in a straight line at walking speed during the first phase.
Players are matched for size and rotate through ball carrier, tackler and observer roles.
No player is taken to ground.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier begins walking through the lane with the football held securely.
The tackler approaches from the side at controlled speed.
The tackler places the near foot close to the ball carrier without stepping across the opponent’s running line.
The near shoulder contacts the ball carrier between the shoulder and hip.
The tackler positions the head behind or to the side of the ball carrier, never across the front of the opponent.
Both arms wrap around the torso.
The tackler matches the ball carrier’s movement for two controlled steps.
The coach calls “release”, and the tackler immediately lets go.
The ball carrier remains upright and continues through the lane.
Players repeat from both sides before rotating roles.
coachingPoints: Approach from an angle that allows shoulder contact without cutting across the opponent’s legs.
Place the near foot close to the opponent to avoid reaching.
Keep the head behind or safely beside the ball carrier.
Contact with the shoulder inside the legal tackling zone.
Wrap both arms immediately after contact.
Match the opponent’s movement rather than jerking them backwards.
Keep the hips low and the chest upright.
Do not lift, rotate, sling or drive the opponent into the ground.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the tackler’s approach remains side-on rather than crossing in front.
Whether the near foot lands close to the ball carrier.
Whether the head remains safely behind or beside the opponent.
Whether the shoulder contacts the legal target area.
Whether both arms complete the wrap.
Whether the tackler moves with the opponent rather than pulling against them.

commonErrors.error: Tackler places the head across the opponent’s front.
commonErrors.correction: Move the head behind the opponent before completing the wrap.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches from too far away.
commonErrors.correction: Place the near foot closer and shorten the final step.

commonErrors.error: Tackler makes contact with extended arms.
commonErrors.correction: Lead with the shoulder and wrap immediately afterwards.

commonErrors.error: Tackler cuts across the ball carrier’s legs.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain the side-on angle and travel parallel to the opponent.

commonErrors.error: Tackler pulls the ball carrier backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Match the ball carrier’s movement and maintain upright control.

progressions: Increase the ball carrier from walking to controlled jogging.
Allow the ball carrier to change pace while remaining in a straight line.
Start the tackler one metre farther behind.
Allow the ball carrier to hold the football on either side of the body.
regressions: Begin with stationary side-on shoulder placement.
Use a tackle bag moving slowly through the lane.
Allow the tackler to walk beside the ball carrier before initiating contact.
Rehearse the lead-foot and head-position sequence without wrapping.
successIndicators: Enter from a safe side-on angle.
Place the near foot close to the opponent.
Keep the head behind or safely beside the ball carrier.
Make legal shoulder contact and wrap both arms.
Maintain the opponent upright and release immediately.
matchApplication: Side-on tackles occur when chasing an opponent, defending along the boundary or closing from an adjacent position. Correct entry prevents head clashes, high contact and dangerous leg contact while improving the defender’s ability to secure the ball carrier.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle
TK-005 – Safe Contact Shape with Tackle Bags

title: Controlled Drive and Release
primarySkill: Maintaining controlled foot drive after tackle contact
objective: Teach tacklers to use short, controlled foot movement to stop an opponent’s momentum while keeping the ball carrier upright and releasing safely.
groundSize: Contact channels approximately 8 metres long and 4 metres wide.
equipment: Optional tackle shields for the introductory phase
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark several straight channels approximately 8 metres long.
Place a start line, contact line and stopping line in each channel.
The ball carrier begins at the start line and moves at approximately 40–50 per cent speed.
The tackler starts 2 metres in front of the ball carrier at the contact line.
A safety observer or coach stands beside each channel where practical.
Players are matched by size and maturity.
The ball carrier remains upright throughout the drill.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier moves forward through the channel with the football.
The tackler closes the final space and establishes a legal shoulder-and-wrap tackle.
After contact, the tackler uses two or three short steps to absorb and stop the ball carrier’s forward momentum.
The tackler keeps the chest close, arms wrapped and head safely positioned.
The tackler must not lift, rotate, sling or drive the ball carrier downwards.
Once forward movement has stopped, the coach blows the whistle.
The tackler immediately releases and steps away.
The ball carrier remains upright, regains balance and returns to the starting line.
Players rotate through ball carrier, tackler and observer roles.
Complete three repetitions from each shoulder.
coachingPoints: Make contact inside the legal tackling zone.
Wrap both arms before attempting to stop the opponent.
Use short, balanced steps rather than one forceful surge.
Keep the feet underneath the body.
Maintain the ball carrier’s upright position.
Keep the head to the side throughout the contact.
Stop driving once the opponent’s forward momentum has been controlled.
Release immediately on the whistle.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether tacklers establish a secure wrap before driving.
Whether the foot movement is short and controlled.
Whether the ball carrier remains upright.
Whether the tackler’s head stays safely positioned.
Whether players stop applying force once momentum is controlled.
Whether the release occurs immediately on the whistle.

commonErrors.error: Tackler attempts to drive before securing the arms.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the shoulder contact and wrap before moving the opponent.

commonErrors.error: Player uses one long step and loses balance.
commonErrors.correction: Use two or three short steps with the feet underneath the hips.

commonErrors.error: Tackler rotates the opponent while driving.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the movement straight and maintain chest-to-opponent alignment.

commonErrors.error: Tackler continues after momentum has stopped.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the action as soon as control is established.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier is pulled towards the ground.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain an upright tackle and remove any downward force.

progressions: Increase the ball carrier’s approach to approximately 60 per cent speed.
Allow the ball carrier to begin one step to either side of the channel’s centre.
Require the tackler to direct the ball carrier safely towards a designated side cone.
Add a controlled disposal attempt after the initial contact.
regressions: Begin with the tackler already wrapped around a stationary partner.
Use a moving tackle bag rather than a partner.
Remove the driving phase and practise only contact, wrap and release.
Reduce the ball carrier to walking speed.
successIndicators: Secure the opponent before applying foot drive.
Stop the opponent’s momentum without lifting or rotating.
Keep both players upright and controlled.
matchApplication: A defender often needs to stop a ball carrier who has forward momentum. Short, controlled steps allow the tackler to complete the tackle and prevent further movement without creating an unsafe sling, lift or forceful ground impact.
relatedDrills: TK-005 – Safe Contact Shape with Tackle Bags
TK-007 – Side-On Entry and Head Placement

title: Ball-and-Arms Lock
primarySkill: Controlling the ball carrier’s arms
objective: Develop the ability to secure a legal tackle that controls the ball carrier’s arms and reduces the opportunity for an effective disposal.
groundSize: Partner stations approximately 5 metres by 5 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Players form size-matched pairs inside separate stations.
One player begins as the ball carrier with the football held at chest or waist height.
The tackler begins immediately beside the ball carrier with no initial momentum.
The ball carrier may attempt a controlled handball but may not run, rotate forcefully or resist at maximum strength.
The tackler must keep the opponent upright.
A coach establishes a maximum two-second working period and a clear release command.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier holds the football in a natural disposal position.
On the coach’s signal, the tackler enters from the side with the head safely positioned.
The tackler wraps both arms around the ball carrier and attempts to include one or both of the opponent’s arms in the tackle.
The ball carrier attempts to complete a controlled handball within two seconds.
The tackler scores one point if the disposal is prevented or clearly affected.
The ball carrier scores one point for completing a legal handball to a nearby target.
No player may lift, sling, pull backwards or take the opponent to ground.
The coach calls “release” after two seconds, regardless of the result.
Players alternate roles after each repetition.
Complete six to eight repetitions per player, varying the football’s starting position.
coachingPoints: Position the head safely before tightening the tackle.
Wrap the torso and arms rather than grabbing at the football.
Close body space so the ball carrier cannot extend the arms freely.
Adjust the wrap according to where the ball is held.
Maintain legal tackle height at all times.
Keep the feet balanced and underneath the body.
Apply enough pressure to control without twisting or forcing the opponent down.
Release immediately at the end of the two-second period.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether tacklers identify the position of the ball and arms before completing the wrap.
Whether players maintain safe head placement.
Whether the tackle prevents arm extension through body connection.
Whether tacklers avoid grabbing the football with one hand.
Whether the ball carrier remains upright and balanced.
Whether contact remains controlled after the disposal is prevented.

commonErrors.error: Tackler wraps only around the waist and leaves both arms free.
commonErrors.correction: Raise or adjust the legal wrap to include at least one arm.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches directly for the football.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the opponent’s body and arms rather than grabbing the ball.

commonErrors.error: Tackler leaves space between the bodies.
commonErrors.correction: Close the chest-to-opponent gap and tighten the forearm clamp.

commonErrors.error: Tackler twists the ball carrier to prevent disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain upright control and remove rotational force.

commonErrors.error: Player continues holding after the ball is released.
commonErrors.correction: End the tackle immediately on the coach’s release command.

progressions: Allow the ball carrier to take one controlled step before contact.
Permit the ball carrier to change the football from one side of the body to the other.
Add a receiver who moves to provide a realistic handball target.
Begin the tackler one metre away and require a controlled side-on entry.
regressions: Begin with the tackler’s arms already loosely positioned.
Have the ball carrier remain completely passive.
Use a tackle bag with a football attached at different heights.
Practise trapping only one arm before attempting to control both.
successIndicators: Include at least one disposal arm in the wrap.
Close body space and prevent free arm extension.
Affect the disposal without twisting or grounding the opponent.
matchApplication: Strong tackles do more than stop movement. Controlling the ball carrier’s arms can prevent a clean handball or kick, create a turnover, produce a holding-the-ball decision or allow teammates to establish defensive structure around the contest.
relatedDrills: TK-007 – Side-On Entry and Head Placement

title: Tracking-to-Tackle Fundamentals
primarySkill: Combining tracking, approach and introductory tackling technique
objective: Integrate the fundamental phases of a safe tackle by requiring defenders to track, close, balance, make legal contact, secure the ball carrier and release under control.
groundSize: Channels approximately 10 metres long and 5 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Construct several channels approximately 10 metres long and 5 metres wide.
Mark an attacker’s starting cone, a defender’s starting cone and a finishing line.
The attacker begins 2 metres in front of the defender with a football.
Position a coach or designated safety observer beside each channel.
The attacker works at 50–60 per cent speed and may make one controlled change of direction.
The defender must complete the sequence without taking the attacker to ground.
Players rotate through attacker, defender, observer and recovery roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the attacker moves towards the finishing line with the football.
The defender tracks from behind and slightly to one side.
The defender closes the initial distance before shortening the steps and establishing balance.
The attacker may make one controlled change of direction inside the channel.
The defender adjusts the approach angle and enters from the side.
The tackler places the head safely behind or beside the ball carrier, makes legal shoulder contact and wraps both arms.
The tackler attempts to include at least one of the ball carrier’s arms in the wrap.
The tackler uses no more than two short steps to stop the attacker’s momentum.
Both players remain upright.
The coach blows the whistle as soon as the tackle is secure.
The tackler releases immediately and both players return outside the channel.
The observer gives one brief technical comment before players rotate.
Complete four to six tackling repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Track the ball carrier’s hips and maintain an effective closing distance.
Accelerate early and decelerate before contact.
Remain balanced when the attacker changes direction.
Enter from the side rather than diving directly into the opponent’s back.
Place the near foot close to the ball carrier.
Keep the head safely behind or beside the opponent.
Make shoulder contact within the legal tackle zone and wrap both arms.
Control the opponent’s momentum without lifting, slinging or grounding.
Release immediately on the whistle.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders maintain balanced tracking footwork before contact.
Whether defenders close quickly but decelerate before tackling.
Whether the approach angle avoids unsafe rear or front-on contact.
Whether the near foot and shoulder arrive close to the opponent.
Whether the head remains safely positioned.
Whether the arms wrap legally and control at least one disposal arm.
Whether the ball carrier remains upright.
Whether the tackler releases immediately on the whistle.

commonErrors.error: Defender chases at one speed and arrives out of control.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate early, then shorten the steps before entering contact range.

commonErrors.error: Tackler dives from behind.
commonErrors.correction: Move to the opponent’s side and establish a safe entry angle.

commonErrors.error: Defender reaches because the final step is too distant.
commonErrors.correction: Place the near foot closer before making shoulder contact.

commonErrors.error: Head moves across the front of the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the head behind or firmly to the side throughout the tackle.

commonErrors.error: Arms wrap loosely and the opponent escapes.
commonErrors.correction: Close the body space and complete a firm two-arm clamp.

commonErrors.error: Tackler rotates or pulls the opponent down.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the tackle upright and stop all force once momentum is controlled.

commonErrors.error: Player fails to release on the whistle.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce immediate disengagement as a non-negotiable safety requirement.

progressions: Increase the attacker to approximately 70 per cent speed.
Allow two changes of direction before contact.
Permit the attacker to attempt a controlled handball after the tackle begins.
Add a support runner whom the ball carrier may use before being secured.
Award the defender two points for legally controlling the ball carrier’s arms and one point for a secure body tackle.
regressions: Predetermine the attacker’s direction.
Reduce both players to walking speed.
Remove the attacker’s change of direction.
Begin the defender beside the attacker rather than behind.
Replace the live ball carrier with a moving tackle bag for players lacking contact confidence.
successIndicators: Track and approach without crossing their feet or losing balance.
Use a safe side-on entry with correct head placement.
Complete legal shoulder contact and a secure two-arm wrap.
Stop the opponent’s momentum while keeping both players upright.
Release immediately when the tackle is complete.
matchApplication: The drill combines the introductory components required for a safe match tackle. Players learn to move from pursuit into a controlled approach, react to evasion, enter legally, secure the ball carrier and finish without dangerous lifting, slinging or unnecessary ground impact.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle
TK-007 – Side-On Entry and Head Placement

title: Legal Tackle Zone Recognition
primarySkill: Recognising and contacting the legal tackling zone
objective: Teach players to identify and consistently make controlled contact between an opponent’s shoulders and knees while avoiding high and low tackle contact.
groundSize: Multiple stations approximately 4 metres by 4 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge with one main teaching point
setup:
Place a soft tackle shield at each station.
Mark the legal tackle zone on each shield between the equivalent shoulder and knee height.
Use a contrasting colour above and below the legal zone to represent prohibited contact areas.
One player holds the shield, one performs the technique and one observes.
The tackler begins approximately 2 metres from the shield.
Rotate roles regularly to minimise waiting.
howTheDrillWorks:
The tackler begins in a balanced stance facing the shield.
The shield holder presents the shield upright and stable.
On the coach’s signal, the tackler takes two controlled steps forwards.
The tackler lowers through the hips and knees while keeping the eyes up.
The near shoulder contacts the marked legal zone.
The tackler positions the head safely to one side and wraps both arms around the shield.
The observer identifies whether the contact was legal, too high or too low.
The tackler releases immediately and resets.
Players perform three repetitions from each shoulder.
Players rotate roles after completing both sides.
coachingPoints: Identify the legal target area before beginning the approach.
Keep contact below the opponent’s shoulders and above the knees.
Lower the body through the hips and knees rather than dropping the head.
Lead with the shoulder rather than reaching with the hands.
Keep the head safely to the side of the contact point.
Place the lead foot close to the target.
Wrap both arms immediately after contact.
Reduce speed whenever accurate contact placement begins to deteriorate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players visually identify the legal tackle zone.
Whether shoulder contact remains inside the marked area.
Whether players lower through the knees and hips.
Whether the head remains safely positioned.
Whether both arms complete the wrap.
Whether players can execute equally from both shoulders.

commonErrors.error: Contact occurs above the marked zone.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips earlier and aim the shoulder through the opponent’s torso.

commonErrors.error: Player dives towards the knees.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the eyes up and target above knee height.

commonErrors.error: Tackler bends at the waist.
commonErrors.correction: Bend through the knees and hips while keeping the chest upright.

commonErrors.error: Hands reach before the shoulder arrives.
commonErrors.correction: Place the lead foot close and make shoulder contact before wrapping.

commonErrors.error: Player closes their eyes before contact.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the speed and require visual focus on the marked target.

progressions: Move the shield slowly forwards or laterally.
Remove the visible markings once players demonstrate consistent accuracy.
Have the shield holder vary their height slightly by bending or standing taller.
Add a football against the shield so the tackler must identify both the legal zone and the ball position.
regressions: Begin with stationary shoulder placement against the shield.
Use hand contact to point to the legal zone before introducing shoulder contact.
Reduce the approach to one step.
Use larger coloured target markings.
successIndicators: Recognise the legal tackle area before contact.
Contact between shoulder and knee height.
Maintain upright head and eye position.
Wrap both arms after shoulder contact.
Avoid high, low or reckless contact.
matchApplication: Players must recognise the legal tackle zone while opponents are moving, changing height and attempting to dispose of the football. Accurate contact placement reduces free kicks, protects both players and improves the likelihood of completing a legal tackle.
relatedDrills: TK-005 – Safe Contact Shape with Tackle Bags
TK-007 – Side-On Entry and Head Placement

title: Front-On Absorb and Wrap
primarySkill: Controlled front-on tackling technique
objective: Teach players to absorb a ball carrier’s forward momentum with a balanced front-on position, legal contact and secure arm wrap.
groundSize: Channels approximately 6 metres long and 4 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark several straight channels approximately 6 metres long.
Position the ball carrier at one end and the tackler approximately 3 metres away.
The ball carrier begins at walking speed before progressing to a controlled jog.
A third player acts as a safety observer.
Match players for size, strength and physical maturity.
Both players must remain upright throughout the drill.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier moves directly towards the tackler at controlled speed.
The tackler maintains a balanced stance and tracks the ball carrier’s hips.
The tackler takes a short adjustment step to avoid rigid, square-on head contact.
The player lowers through the knees and hips while maintaining eye contact with the target area.
The tackler makes legal shoulder-and-chest contact through the ball carrier’s torso.
The head remains safely to one side rather than directly in front.
Both arms wrap around the ball carrier.
The tackler takes one or two short backwards or stabilising steps to absorb momentum.
The tackler stops the ball carrier without lifting, rotating or taking them to ground.
The coach calls “release”, and both players separate immediately.
Players rotate through ball carrier, tackler and observer roles.
coachingPoints: Avoid placing the head directly in front of the oncoming opponent.
Use a small adjustment step to establish safe head and shoulder alignment.
Keep the feet moving as the opponent approaches.
Lower through the knees and hips without dropping the eyes.
Make contact inside the legal tackle zone.
Wrap both arms immediately and close the body space.
Absorb momentum with short steps rather than resisting with locked knees.
Keep the opponent upright and release immediately on command.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether tacklers avoid direct head-to-head alignment.
Whether the adjustment step occurs before contact.
Whether players remain balanced with knees bent.
Whether contact occurs within the legal zone.
Whether momentum is absorbed through controlled foot movement.
Whether the ball carrier remains upright.
Whether the tackler releases immediately.

commonErrors.error: Tackler remains directly square and places the head in front.
commonErrors.correction: Use a small lateral adjustment step and move the head to one side.

commonErrors.error: Player braces with locked knees.
commonErrors.correction: Bend the knees and absorb momentum with short steps.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches from too far away.
commonErrors.correction: Allow the opponent to enter close range before completing the wrap.

commonErrors.error: Tackler falls backwards after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Widen the base and keep the feet active underneath the body.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier is twisted after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the tackle upright and absorb momentum without rotation.

progressions: Increase the ball carrier from walking to 50–60 per cent running speed.
Allow the ball carrier to approach slightly left or right of centre.
Allow a controlled handball attempt during contact.
Require the tackler to identify and control the arm holding the football.
regressions: Begin with a stationary ball carrier.
Use a tackle bag moving slowly towards the tackler.
Start with the tackler’s hands lightly touching the ball carrier.
Remove the football and focus only on safe body alignment.
successIndicators: Move the head away from direct front-on impact.
Establish a balanced and lowered body position.
Secure the ball carrier with both arms.
Absorb momentum without falling, lifting or rotating.
matchApplication: Front-on tackles occur when a defender protects space and a ball carrier runs directly towards them. Correct alignment and momentum absorption allow the defender to stop the opponent safely without high contact, head clashes or uncontrolled collisions.
relatedDrills: TK-005 – Safe Contact Shape with Tackle Bags

title: Rear-Angle Chase Tackle Entry
primarySkill: Converting a chase into a safe side-on tackle
objective: Develop the ability to chase from behind, move safely to the ball carrier’s side and complete a controlled tackle without diving into the opponent’s back or legs.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 12 metres long and 5 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark parallel lanes approximately 12 metres long.
The ball carrier begins 2 metres ahead of the defender.
Place a contact zone between the 6-metre and 10-metre marks.
The ball carrier runs in a straight line at approximately 50–60 per cent speed.
The defender begins slightly offset to the left or right.
A third player observes the contact angle and head position.
No player may be taken to ground.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the ball carrier accelerates through the lane.
The defender pursues from behind and slightly to one side.
The defender accelerates until reaching the ball carrier’s hip line.
Before making contact, the defender reduces speed and moves fully to the opponent’s side.
The defender places the near foot beside the ball carrier.
The head remains behind or beside the opponent rather than pressing into the back.
The tackler makes legal shoulder contact and wraps both arms.
The tackler travels with the ball carrier for no more than two steps.
The coach blows the whistle once control is established.
The tackler releases immediately.
Players rotate through ball carrier, defender and observer roles.
Repeat from both chase angles.
coachingPoints: Chase the ball carrier’s outside hip rather than running directly at the spine.
Accelerate early but control speed before contact.
Move beside the opponent before initiating the tackle.
Place the near foot close to avoid diving.
Keep the head behind or beside the ball carrier.
Make contact above the knees and below the shoulders.
Wrap both arms rather than grabbing clothing or reaching with one hand.
Travel with the opponent instead of dragging them backwards.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders pursue on an angle rather than directly into the opponent’s back.
Whether the defender reaches the ball carrier’s side before contact.
Whether speed is reduced before tackling.
Whether the near foot lands close to the ball carrier.
Whether head position remains safe.
Whether the tackler wraps both arms and keeps the opponent upright.

commonErrors.error: Defender dives into the opponent’s back.
commonErrors.correction: Chase the outside hip and move beside the ball carrier before contact.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches with one arm.
commonErrors.correction: Continue running until close enough to complete a two-arm wrap.

commonErrors.error: Defender clips the opponent’s legs.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the target above the knees and remain alongside the torso.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives at uncontrolled speed.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the final steps and match the ball carrier’s pace.

commonErrors.error: Defender pulls the opponent backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Travel in the same direction and stop force once control is established.

progressions: Increase the ball carrier’s speed to approximately 70 per cent.
Allow the ball carrier one controlled change of direction.
Begin the defender an additional metre behind.
Allow the ball carrier to attempt a handball after contact begins.
regressions: Start the defender level with the ball carrier’s hip.
Reduce both players to jogging speed.
Use a moving tackle bag rather than a player.
Predetermine the defender’s chase side.
successIndicators: Move safely beside the ball carrier before tackling.
Avoid diving, leg contact and direct contact into the back.
Complete legal shoulder contact and a two-arm wrap.
matchApplication: Chase tackles regularly occur after turnovers, loose-ball wins and defensive breakdowns. Moving to the opponent’s side before contact helps prevent dangerous tackles into the back, protects the ball carrier’s legs and improves the defender’s ability to control the disposal.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle
TK-007 – Side-On Entry and Head Placement

title: Evasion Reaction Tackle
primarySkill: Reacting to an evasive movement before tackling
objective: Teach defenders to remain balanced through one evasive movement and complete the tackle only after the ball carrier commits to a direction.
groundSize: Squares approximately 7 metres by 7 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark several 7-metre by 7-metre squares.
One ball carrier and one defender begin approximately 3 metres apart.
Mark an exit gate on the side opposite the attacker.
The attacker may use one controlled sidestep or change of direction.
A third player acts as observer and confirms whether the defender remained balanced.
The ball carrier works at no more than 60 per cent speed.
Both players must remain upright during the tackle.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the ball carrier moves towards the exit gate.
Before reaching the defender, the attacker may make one controlled sidestep.
The defender closes the initial space and establishes a balanced breakdown position.
The defender mirrors the sidestep using active feet.
The defender must not lunge during the first evasive movement.
Once the attacker commits to the new line, the defender closes the final space.
The defender completes a legal side-on shoulder-and-wrap tackle.
The tackler controls the ball carrier upright for one second.
The coach calls “release”.
Players exchange roles after each repetition.
Complete four to six repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Close the initial distance without entering too quickly.
Establish balance before the attacker begins the sidestep.
Watch the attacker’s hips rather than the football.
Move the feet through the evasive action.
Avoid reaching or lunging at the first fake.
Reaccelerate only once the attacker commits to a direction.
Place the near foot close before shoulder contact.
Maintain safe head position and legal tackle height.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders establish balance before the sidestep.
Whether defenders react to the hips rather than guessing.
Whether feet remain active during the change of direction.
Whether the defender avoids reaching.
Whether the final approach is controlled.
Whether legal contact and safe head placement are maintained.

commonErrors.error: Defender lunges during the attacker’s first movement.
commonErrors.correction: Remain balanced and wait until the hips commit.

commonErrors.error: Defender crosses the feet when changing direction.
commonErrors.correction: Use short lateral adjustment steps.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches after being wrong-footed.
commonErrors.correction: Recover the feet before attempting contact.

commonErrors.error: Defender approaches too close before the sidestep.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a small reaction buffer until the attacker commits.

commonErrors.error: Tackler makes high contact while recovering.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the hips and re-establish the legal target before contact.

progressions: Permit two controlled changes of direction.
Increase the attacker’s speed.
Allow a handball fake before the sidestep.
Add a second exit gate so the attacker has a genuine directional choice.
regressions: Predetermine the attacker’s change of direction.
Reduce the attacker to walking speed.
Begin with a two-handed touch rather than a tackle.
Increase the square to 9 metres by 9 metres.
successIndicators: Remain balanced through the attacker’s evasive movement.
Recover defensive position with active feet.
Close the final space after the attacker commits.
Complete a legal and controlled tackle.
matchApplication: Ball carriers commonly use sidesteps, baulks and changes of pace to draw defenders off balance. A patient defender who keeps moving can contain the opponent and tackle after the evasive movement rather than conceding space through an early lunge.

title: Fend-Off Control and Re-Entry
primarySkill: Maintaining tackle position against a controlled fend-off
objective: Develop the ability to absorb or avoid a controlled fend-off, maintain balance and re-enter the tackle without grabbing the opponent’s arm illegally or making high contact.
groundSize: Channels approximately 7 metres long and 4 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Create several 7-metre channels.
The ball carrier begins with the football approximately 3 metres from the defender.
The ball carrier may present one open hand as a controlled fend-off.
The fend-off must contact only the tackler’s upper chest or shoulder and may not contact the face, throat or head.
The defender may deflect the arm, move their head and body line, or recover after initial separation.
A third player observes safety and technique.
Tackles remain upright.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier moves towards the defender at approximately 50 per cent speed.
The defender closes space and prepares to tackle.
The attacker presents one controlled fend-off with an open hand.
The defender keeps the chin clear, protects the head and avoids leaning into the extended arm.
The defender may use the near forearm to guide the fend away without striking or grabbing.
The defender maintains active feet and moves back towards the attacker’s torso.
Once past the fend, the defender makes legal shoulder contact and wraps both arms.
The tackler controls the opponent upright for one second.
The coach calls “release”.
Players rotate roles after two repetitions on each side.
coachingPoints: Keep the eyes open and head upright when the fend is presented.
Avoid leading with the face or throat.
Do not grab, wrench or pull the extended arm.
Use footwork and body angle to move inside or around the fend.
Guide the arm away with an open forearm or hand where appropriate.
Re-establish close body position before attempting the wrap.
Keep the final contact below the shoulders and above the knees.
Maintain control without lifting or rotating the opponent.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the fend-off remains controlled and below the tackler’s neck.
Whether defenders avoid direct facial contact.
Whether players remain balanced after separation.
Whether the defender uses footwork rather than arm wrestling.
Whether re-entry occurs through the legal tackle zone.
Whether the tackle remains upright and controlled.

commonErrors.error: Tackler leads with the face into the fend.
commonErrors.correction: Move the head off-line and approach with the shoulder.

commonErrors.error: Defender grabs and pulls the extended arm.
commonErrors.correction: Guide the arm away and continue moving towards the torso.

commonErrors.error: Tackler stops their feet after the fend.
commonErrors.correction: Keep adjusting until close body position is restored.

commonErrors.error: Defender reaches from outside the fend.
commonErrors.correction: Move the feet past the extended arm before wrapping.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier fends towards the face or neck.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the drill and reset the fend to the upper chest or shoulder only.

progressions: Allow the ball carrier to choose which arm presents the fend.
Increase the ball carrier’s speed slightly.
Allow the defender to choose whether to deflect, evade or absorb the fend.
Permit the ball carrier to attempt a handball after the fend.
regressions: Practise fend avoidance without completing a tackle.
Begin with the attacker stationary.
Use a soft pad instead of a player’s hand.
Predetermine the fend side.
successIndicators: Protect the head and neck from the fend.
Avoid grabbing or wrenching the opponent’s arm.
Continue moving the feet after initial separation.
Re-enter through the legal tackle zone.
matchApplication: Ball carriers frequently use a fend-off to prevent or break tackles. Defenders must protect themselves, remain balanced and continue working towards the opponent’s torso rather than reaching, grabbing the arm or making desperate high contact.
relatedDrills: TK-007 – Side-On Entry and Head Placement

title: Tackle, Spill and Recover
primarySkill: Responding to a football released during a tackle
objective: Teach tacklers to complete legal contact, recognise when the football spills free and release the opponent immediately before competing for the loose football.
groundSize: Squares approximately 8 metres by 8 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark multiple 8-metre by 8-metre squares.
One ball carrier and one tackler begin in the centre of each square.
A feeder stands outside the square.
The ball carrier begins walking or jogging across the area.
During the controlled tackle, the feeder calls either “hold” or “spill”.
On “spill”, the ball carrier releases the football safely into nearby space.
Both players remain upright during the initial tackle.
howTheDrillWorks:
The ball carrier moves across the square at controlled speed.
The defender tracks and completes a legal upright tackle.
The feeder calls “hold” or “spill”.
On “hold”, the tackler maintains legal control until the whistle and then releases.
On “spill”, the ball carrier releases the football 1–2 metres into open space.
The tackler immediately releases the opponent.
Both players turn and compete for the loose football without diving into each other’s legs.
The first player to gain clean possession handballs to the feeder.
The repetition then ends.
Players rotate through ball carrier, tackler and feeder roles.
coachingPoints: Complete the tackle legally before reacting to the coach’s call.
Maintain awareness of where the football is positioned.
Release the opponent immediately when the football is no longer in their possession.
Turn the hips and feet towards the loose football before bending to collect.
Avoid continuing to hold an opponent who no longer has the football.
Approach the loose ball with the head and shoulders protected.
Secure possession before attempting the handball.
Recover balance quickly after contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the initial tackle is legal and controlled.
Whether the tackler recognises the ball spill.
Whether the opponent is released immediately.
Whether both players recover their feet before attacking the loose ball.
Whether players protect their head and body during collection.
Whether the winner completes a clean disposal.

commonErrors.error: Tackler continues holding after the football spills.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and redirect attention to the football.

commonErrors.error: Defender watches the opponent rather than locating the spill.
commonErrors.correction: Scan for the football as soon as possession changes.

commonErrors.error: Players dive head-first towards the loose ball.
commonErrors.correction: Turn, lower through the hips and approach with body protection.

commonErrors.error: Tackler loses balance after releasing.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the feet underneath the body during the tackle.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier throws the football dangerously.
commonErrors.correction: Release the football gently into clear nearby space.

progressions: Allow the ball carrier to attempt a genuine controlled disposal during the tackle.
Add a second loose-ball player entering after the spill.
Vary the direction of the released football.
Require the possession winner to evade passive pressure before handballing.
regressions: Predetermine every repetition as a spill.
Place the football on the ground rather than releasing it live.
Begin with a stationary wrap.
Remove the post-spill contest and allow the tackler to collect unopposed.
successIndicators: Recover balance and locate the football.
Compete safely for the loose ball.
Complete a clean disposal after possession.
matchApplication: Tackles often dislodge the football or force an ineffective disposal. Defenders must stop holding the opponent once possession is lost and react immediately to the next contest. Fast recovery can turn a completed tackle into a possession win or another pressure action.

title: Missed Tackle Recovery Footwork
primarySkill: Recovering after an unsuccessful tackle attempt
objective: Develop the immediate footwork and defensive response required after a tackle attempt is missed or broken.
groundSize: Channels approximately 10 metres long and 6 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark several channels with a central contact gate and two finishing gates.
The attacker begins with a football approximately 3 metres from the defender.
The defender begins in a balanced tackling stance.
The first tackle attempt is represented by a controlled two-handed touch.
The attacker is instructed to evade the initial touch and accelerate towards either finishing gate.
A third player observes the defender’s recovery action.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker approaches the defender at controlled speed.
The defender moves to make a two-handed touch between the shoulders and hips.
The attacker uses a controlled sidestep to avoid the touch.
The defender must immediately recover balance without falling or stopping.
The defender turns through the shortest available path and accelerates after the attacker.
The attacker selects either finishing gate.
The defender attempts to recover goalside and make a second two-handed touch before the attacker crosses the line.
One point is awarded to the defender for a successful recovery touch.
One point is awarded to the attacker for crossing untouched.
Players rotate roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Avoid overcommitting the body during the first attempt.
Keep one foot underneath the body whenever possible.
Recover the eyes to the attacker immediately.
Turn through the shortest path rather than spinning blindly.
Accelerate for the first three recovery steps.
Chase the attacker’s inside or dangerous-side hip.
Continue the defensive effort even when the first attempt fails.
Finish the second approach under control.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders remain on their feet after the missed touch.
How quickly the eyes return to the attacker.
Whether the defender uses an efficient turning path.
Whether the first recovery steps are explosive.
Whether the defender protects the more dangerous exit gate.
Whether the second effort remains controlled.

commonErrors.error: Defender falls or dives during the first attempt.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the feet underneath the body and reach only from balanced range.

commonErrors.error: Player pauses after missing.
commonErrors.correction: React immediately and begin the recovery turn.

commonErrors.error: Defender spins away from the attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the eyes on the opponent and turn through the shortest path.

commonErrors.error: Defender chases the football rather than the hips.
commonErrors.correction: Target the attacker’s dangerous-side hip.

commonErrors.error: Second approach is uncontrolled.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate before the second touch or tackle opportunity.

progressions: Replace the second touch with a controlled tackle.
Allow the attacker a second change of direction.
Increase the length of the recovery chase.
Add a support attacker who may receive a handball.
regressions: Predetermine the attacker’s finishing gate.
Reduce the attacker to jogging speed.
Begin with the defender deliberately stepping past a stationary attacker.
Shorten the recovery distance.
successIndicators: Remain upright after the first failed attempt.
Finish the next pressure action under control.
matchApplication: Not every tackle is completed. Players who remain on the ground, stop moving or react emotionally after a miss allow the opposition to escape. Immediate recovery can create another tackle, force a rushed disposal or allow teammates time to support.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle

title: Tackle Release to Next Threat
primarySkill: Transitioning from a completed tackle to the next defensive action
objective: Teach players to release a completed tackle promptly, scan for the next attacking threat and transition immediately into a second pressure action.
groundSize: Areas approximately 12 metres by 10 metres.
equipment: Tackle bags or controlled partner stations
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Place a tackle bag or controlled ball carrier in the centre of each area.
Position two coloured exit gates approximately 6 metres away.
A second attacker waits between the two gates.
The tackler begins 2 metres from the central contact point.
A feeder stands outside the area with a football.
After the initial tackle, the feeder releases the second attacker towards one gate.
Rotate players through all roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The tackler approaches and completes a legal controlled tackle on the central bag or ball carrier.
The coach blows the whistle once control is established.
The tackler releases immediately.
At the same moment, the feeder handballs to the second attacker.
The second attacker moves towards either exit gate.
The tackler turns, scans and identifies the new threat.
The tackler accelerates to close space and applies a two-handed pressure touch.
The defender scores one point for immediate release and one point for affecting the second attacker before the gate.
Players rotate after each repetition.
Complete four to six defensive repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Finish the first tackle before looking away.
Release immediately on the whistle.
Regain an upright running position quickly.
Scan with the head and eyes rather than turning blindly.
Identify the most immediate attacking threat.
Communicate while transitioning.
Accelerate hard for the first recovery steps.
Arrive under control at the second contest.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the initial tackle is completed legally.
Whether the defender releases immediately.
How quickly the defender regains running posture.
Whether the next threat is identified through scanning.
Whether the defender communicates.
Whether the second approach balances urgency and control.

commonErrors.error: Defender remains attached after the whistle.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and begin the next action.

commonErrors.error: Player turns without locating the new attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Lift the eyes and scan before accelerating.

commonErrors.error: Defender jogs into the second effort.
commonErrors.correction: Produce three urgent recovery steps.

commonErrors.error: Player runs directly past the second attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate before entering pressure range.

commonErrors.error: Defender focuses on the football and loses the opponent.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the attacker’s hips and running line.

progressions: Replace the second touch with a controlled tackle.
Add two possible receiving attackers.
Allow the feeder to fake before selecting the receiver.
Add a third phase after the second pressure action.
regressions: Use a stationary tackle bag for the first action.
Predetermine the second attacker’s gate.
Reduce the distance to the second contest.
Remove the football from the second phase.
successIndicators: Complete and release the first tackle safely.
Accelerate into a repeat defensive effort.
Arrive at the second contest under control.
matchApplication: Australian football requires repeated pressure actions. After a tackle, players must release legally and immediately rejoin play. The next opponent may receive a handball, collect a spill or run past for support, making rapid scanning and repeat effort essential.

title: Corral-or-Commit Decision
primarySkill: Deciding whether to contain or tackle
objective: Develop the defender’s ability to recognise whether the ball carrier can be tackled safely or should be corralled until a better opportunity develops.
groundSize: Areas approximately 10 metres by 8 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark an attacking area with one central scoring gate and two wide escape gates.
The ball carrier begins approximately 6 metres from the gates.
The defender begins 4 metres in front of the ball carrier.
A feeder stands behind the attacker.
Before each repetition, the feeder secretly gives the attacker one of two instructions:
Attack the defender and attempt to break through.
Move laterally and search for a wide escape.
A safety observer stands outside the area.
Contact remains upright and controlled.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder starts the repetition with a handball to the attacker.
The defender closes space while reading the attacker’s speed, body position and available exits.
When the attacker moves directly into tackle range, the defender may commit to a legal controlled tackle.
When the attacker remains outside safe tackle range, the defender must corral and protect the central gate.
The defender scores two points for a legal completed tackle.
The defender scores one point for containing the attacker for five seconds or forcing a wide exit.
The attacker scores two points for crossing the central gate.
The attacker scores one point for escaping through a wide gate.
The repetition stops after a score or completed tackle.
Players rotate through attacker, defender, feeder and observer roles.
coachingPoints: Close space without deciding too early whether to tackle.
Read the attacker’s hips, speed and ball position.
Commit only when the defender can place the near foot close and maintain safe head position.
Corral when the attacker remains outside controlled contact range.
Protect the central and most dangerous space.
Use the boundary or wide gate to reduce attacking options.
Avoid lunging after a late decision.
Reassess continuously as the attacker changes speed or direction.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders delay their decision until useful information is available.
Whether the central gate remains protected.
Whether players recognise safe tackling range.
Whether defenders corral rather than lunge from distance.
Whether committed tackles use correct head and shoulder placement.
Whether defenders adapt when the attacker changes pace.

commonErrors.error: Defender commits from too far away.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain balance and corral until the near foot can arrive close.

commonErrors.error: Defender remains passive when the attacker enters tackle range.
