commonErrors.correction: Recognise the committed running line and close decisively.

commonErrors.error: Defender protects a wide gate and concedes the centre.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise the most dangerous central space.

commonErrors.error: Defender watches only the football.
commonErrors.correction: Read the attacker’s hips, speed and body line.

commonErrors.error: Tackler lunges after being uncertain.
commonErrors.correction: Reset the feet and continue containing rather than reaching.

progressions: Add a support attacker available for a handball.
Reduce the defender’s starting distance.
Allow the attacker unlimited direction changes within a six-second period.
Add a recovering defender approaching from behind.
regressions: Tell the defender whether the repetition requires corral or tackle.
Reduce the attacker to walking speed.
Use two-handed touches rather than tackles.
Remove one wide escape gate.
successIndicators: Recognise whether safe tackle range has been reached.
Commit decisively when the opportunity is available.
Corral patiently when tackling would be reckless.
Maintain balanced footwork throughout the decision.
matchApplication: Defenders should not attempt a tackle simply because they are near the football. At times, containing the ball carrier and protecting the corridor is more valuable than lunging and being beaten. This drill develops the judgement to distinguish between a genuine tackle opportunity and a corral situation.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle

title: Tackling Fundamentals Assessment Circuit
primarySkill: Assessment of introductory tackling fundamentals
objective: Assess whether players can consistently perform the fundamental tracking, approach, contact, control, release and recovery behaviours required for safe introductory tackling.
groundSize: Four stations occupying approximately one-quarter of an oval or an area measuring 35 metres by 30 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Construct four separate assessment stations.
Divide players evenly across the stations.
Station 1 assesses tracking, approach and breakdown position.
Station 2 assesses legal tackle-zone contact on a shield.
Station 3 assesses controlled side-on tackling against a moving partner.
Station 4 assesses corral-or-commit decision making and recovery effort.
Assign a coach or trained observer to each station.
Match players appropriately for size and contact confidence.
Use a consistent scoring scale across all stations.
Rotate groups every five to seven minutes.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, the defender tracks an evasive attacker through a lane without contact.
The observer assesses balance, approach angle, deceleration and ability to remain within effective range.
At Station 2, the player completes three tackle contacts on a shield from each shoulder.
The observer assesses legal target placement, head position, lead-foot distance and arm wrap.
At Station 3, the player completes controlled side-on tackles against a partner moving at approximately 50 per cent speed.
The observer assesses side entry, upright control, foot movement and immediate release.
At Station 4, the defender faces live corral-or-tackle decisions against a ball carrier.
After each repetition, the attacker may release the football or continue moving so the defender must demonstrate recovery.
Each behaviour is scored:
2 points: Consistently demonstrated.
1 point: Demonstrated inconsistently or with correction.
0 points: Not demonstrated or unsafe.
Any unsafe action immediately stops the repetition and requires technical correction.
Players rotate until all four stations are completed.
Coaches record an individual strength, priority improvement and recommended regression or progression for every player.
coachingPoints: Safety takes priority over speed, force and competitive outcome.
Players must remain balanced before making contact.
Contact must remain below the shoulders and above the knees.
Head position must be safely beside or behind the opponent.
Both arms should complete the wrap.
Tacklers must avoid lifting, slinging, rotating or driving opponents into the ground.
Players must release immediately on the coach’s call.
Defenders should recover quickly after a spill, missed tackle or completed action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players maintain effective defensive tracking distance.
Whether approach speed is reduced before contact.
Whether players identify and contact the legal tackle zone.
Whether head placement is consistently safe.
Whether the near foot lands close to the opponent.
Whether both arms wrap securely.
Whether the ball carrier remains upright.
Whether players release immediately.
Whether players make appropriate corral-or-tackle decisions.
Whether players produce a second defensive effort.

commonErrors.error: Player performs well on bags but loses technique against a moving partner.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce partner speed and rebuild the side-on entry sequence.

commonErrors.error: Tackler makes inconsistent high contact.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips earlier and visually identify the legal zone before entry.

commonErrors.error: Head position changes during live movement.
commonErrors.correction: Slow the drill and rehearse the near-foot, shoulder and head sequence.

commonErrors.error: Player reaches instead of closing space.
commonErrors.correction: Continue tracking until the near foot can arrive beside the opponent.

commonErrors.error: Tackler controls contact but fails to release.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce the whistle and release response at every station.

commonErrors.error: Defender repeatedly lunges instead of corralling.
commonErrors.correction: Return to controlled breakdown and mirror work.

commonErrors.error: Player stops after an unsuccessful effort.
commonErrors.correction: Add a mandatory recovery target after each repetition.

progressions: Increase the speed of the moving partner for players who meet all safety standards.
Add a controlled disposal attempt during the tackle.
Introduce a second attacking threat after the initial contact.
Score decision quality as well as technical execution.
Repeat the assessment later in the training cycle and compare results.
regressions: Return players to stationary tackle-bag technique.
Replace live tackling with two-handed touch pressure.
Predetermine the attacker’s movement.
Reduce working speed and contact resistance.
Provide individual technique coaching before reassessment.
successIndicators: Track and approach with balanced footwork.
Identify and contact the legal tackle zone.
Recover into the next defensive action.
Select appropriately between corralling and tackling.
matchApplication: The circuit assesses the full introductory tackling sequence required in Australian football. Players must show that they can approach safely, complete legal contact, control rather than endanger the ball carrier, release correctly and remain involved in the next phase of play.
relatedDrills: TK-005 – Safe Contact Shape with Tackle Bags

title: Moving Ball-Carrier Lane Tackle
primarySkill: Completing a tackle against a moving ball carrier
objective: Develop the ability to match a ball carrier’s movement, close from a safe angle and complete a controlled upright tackle without reaching or diving.
groundSize: Parallel lanes approximately 12 metres long and 4 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark several lanes approximately 12 metres long and 4 metres wide.
Place an attacker’s starting cone at one end and a finishing line at the opposite end.
The defender begins 2 metres behind and one metre to the side of the attacker.
A third player stands outside the lane as a safety observer.
The attacker carries the football at approximately 50–60 per cent speed.
The attacker must remain inside the lane and initially runs in a straight line.
Match players appropriately for size, strength and contact confidence.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the attacker accelerates towards the finishing line.
The defender tracks the attacker’s outside hip and closes the initial distance.
The defender moves fully beside the attacker before initiating contact.
The defender shortens the final steps and places the near foot close to the attacker.
The tackler positions the head safely behind or beside the ball carrier.
The near shoulder contacts inside the legal tackling zone.
Both arms wrap securely around the ball carrier.
The tackler matches the attacker’s movement for no more than two steps.
The coach calls “release” once control is established.
Both players remain upright and separate immediately.
Players rotate through attacker, defender and observer roles.
Complete three repetitions from each chase side.
coachingPoints: Track the attacker’s hip rather than chasing directly at their back.
Accelerate early and reduce speed before contact.
Move beside the attacker before attempting the tackle.
Place the near foot close enough to avoid reaching.
Keep the head behind or safely to the side.
Contact between the shoulders and knees.
Wrap both arms before attempting to control momentum.
Travel with the opponent rather than dragging them backwards.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders take an effective pursuit angle.
Whether the defender reaches the attacker’s side before contact.
Whether the final approach is controlled.
Whether the near foot lands close to the ball carrier.
Whether head placement remains safe.
Whether both arms complete the wrap.
Whether the attacker remains upright throughout the tackle.

commonErrors.error: Defender runs directly into the attacker’s back.
commonErrors.correction: Track the outside hip and move fully beside the opponent before contact.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches from behind with one arm.
commonErrors.correction: Continue running until a two-arm wrap is available.

commonErrors.error: Defender arrives too quickly and collides heavily.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and match the attacker’s speed.

commonErrors.error: Head moves across the attacker’s front.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the head behind the near shoulder and hip.

commonErrors.error: Tackler drags the attacker backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Travel in the same direction and stop applying force when control is established.

progressions: Allow the attacker one controlled change of pace.
Allow the attacker one lateral movement inside the lane.
Increase the attacker’s speed to approximately 70 per cent.
Permit a controlled handball attempt once the tackle begins.
regressions: Begin the defender level with the attacker’s hip.
Reduce both players to walking speed.
Use a moving tackle bag instead of a live ball carrier.
Predetermine the contact side.
successIndicators: Reach a safe side-on tackling position.
Maintain legal shoulder and head placement.
Keep both players upright and release promptly.
matchApplication: Ball carriers are rarely stationary when tackled. Defenders must match movement, choose a safe chase angle and arrive beside the opponent before contact. This technique is essential during transition, boundary pursuits and defensive recovery.
relatedDrills: TK-007 – Side-On Entry and Head Placement

title: Receive-and-Tackle Timing
primarySkill: Timing pressure on a receiving ball carrier
objective: Teach defenders to close space while the football is travelling and tackle the receiver legally after possession has been established.
groundSize: Grids approximately 12 metres long and 8 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Position a feeder at one end of the grid.
Place a receiver approximately 8 metres away.
Position the defender 4 metres to the side of the receiver.
Mark a 4-metre possession zone around the receiver.
A fourth player acts as an observer and disposal target.
The feeder may deliver the football by handball or short kick.
The defender may move once the football leaves the feeder’s hands or foot.
Contact must not occur before the receiver gains possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver leads inside the possession zone.
The feeder delivers the football to the receiver.
Once the football is released, the defender closes space on an appropriate angle.
The defender must avoid contacting the receiver before possession is established.
After the receiver controls the football, they attempt to move towards the observer or complete a disposal.
The defender decelerates and completes a legal upright tackle.
The receiver may attempt one controlled handball after contact.
The defender scores two points for a legal tackle that prevents the handball.
The defender scores one point for forcing an ineffective disposal.
The receiver scores one point for completing a clean handball.
Players rotate through all four roles.
coachingPoints: Read the football’s flight and the receiver’s movement simultaneously.
Accelerate while the football is travelling.
Adjust the approach if the delivery moves the receiver off their line.
Do not contact the player before possession is established.
Shorten the final steps as the receiver gains control.
Target the torso and disposal arm rather than the football alone.
Keep the head to the safe side of the contact.
Finish the tackle without driving the receiver into the ground.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders react when the football is released.
Whether the approach adjusts to the quality and direction of the pass.
Whether defenders avoid premature contact.
Whether deceleration occurs before the tackle.
Whether the defender identifies the receiver’s disposal side.
Whether the tackle affects the disposal legally.

commonErrors.error: Defender waits until the receiver has possession before moving.
commonErrors.correction: Begin closing as soon as the football is released.

commonErrors.error: Defender contacts the receiver early.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain body control and wait until possession is established.

commonErrors.error: Defender runs to the receiver’s starting position.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the line according to the football’s flight and the receiver’s lead.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives upright and reaches.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and lower through the hips.

commonErrors.error: Defender tackles the torso but leaves both arms free.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the wrap to include the likely disposal arm.

progressions: Allow the receiver to lead in any direction.
Vary the feeder’s delivery speed and accuracy.
Add a second receiver so the defender must identify the target.
Permit the receiver to evade after gaining possession.
regressions: Predetermine the receiver’s lead.
Use handball deliveries only.
Reduce the defender’s closing distance.
Replace the tackle with a two-handed touch.
successIndicators: Move while the football is in transit.
Adjust to the receiver’s actual possession point.
Arrive balanced after possession is established.
Complete a legal tackle that affects the disposal.
matchApplication: Defenders frequently close on players receiving short kicks or handballs. Moving while the football travels reduces the receiver’s time, but the defender must remain disciplined enough to avoid front-on or premature contact before possession.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle

title: Lateral Pursuit Tackle
primarySkill: Tackling across a ball carrier’s lateral running line
objective: Develop the ability to intercept a ball carrier moving across the ground and enter the tackle from a safe, controlled lateral angle.
groundSize: Rectangles approximately 12 metres wide and 8 metres deep.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a rectangular working area with an attacker’s starting gate on one side.
Place the finishing gate on the opposite side.
The defender begins near the centre of the rectangle.
The attacker carries the football laterally across the defender’s field of vision.
A third player observes the tackle angle and safety.
The attacker begins at 50–60 per cent speed.
Both players remain upright during contact.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the attacker runs across the rectangle towards the finishing gate.
The defender turns and accelerates towards an interception point rather than chasing the attacker’s current position.
The defender approaches the attacker’s near hip.
The tackler matches speed and shortens the final steps.
The near foot lands beside the attacker’s running line.
The defender positions the head behind the opponent’s near shoulder.
Legal shoulder contact is followed by a two-arm wrap.
The tackler travels with the attacker for one or two steps.
The coach calls “release” once momentum is controlled.
Players rotate roles and repeat from the opposite direction.
coachingPoints: Run towards the interception point, not directly at the attacker’s current location.
Maintain vision of both the opponent and available space.
Approach the near hip from inside the running line.
Match the attacker’s speed before contact.
Place the near foot close without stepping across the opponent’s legs.
Keep the head behind the contact point.
Wrap with both arms and avoid grabbing clothing.
Maintain upright control and travel in the same direction.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders select an efficient interception angle.
Whether the defender avoids chasing behind the attacker.
Whether speed is matched before contact.
Whether the near foot lands safely.
Whether the tackle remains above the knees.
Whether the tackler travels with the attacker instead of twisting them.

commonErrors.error: Defender chases the attacker’s previous position.
commonErrors.correction: Run towards the likely meeting point.

commonErrors.error: Tackler approaches from too far behind.
commonErrors.correction: Take a more direct angle to the near hip.

commonErrors.error: Defender steps across the attacker’s legs.
commonErrors.correction: Land the near foot beside, not across, the running line.

commonErrors.error: Tackler collides at excessive speed.
commonErrors.correction: Match the opponent’s pace before contact.

commonErrors.error: Defender rotates the attacker backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Continue moving laterally and keep the tackle upright.

progressions: Increase the attacker’s speed.
Allow the attacker to change pace.
Add a late change of direction towards a second finishing gate.
Permit a controlled handball attempt during contact.
regressions: Predetermine the meeting point with a cone.
Reduce both players to jogging speed.
Begin the defender closer to the attacker’s path.
Use a two-handed touch before introducing contact.
successIndicators: Maintain safe foot and head placement.
Keep the tackle upright and controlled.
matchApplication: Players often defend opponents moving laterally across half-back, through the corridor or around stoppages. Efficient pursuit angles allow the defender to close space without chasing from behind or creating dangerous contact across the opponent’s legs.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle

title: Boundary Funnel Tackle
primarySkill: Using the boundary to create a tackle opportunity
objective: Teach defenders to protect the inside, funnel the ball carrier towards the boundary and tackle only when the opponent’s escape space has been reduced.
groundSize: Channels approximately 12 metres long and 7 metres wide, positioned beside a boundary line or marked sideline.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Use an existing boundary line or mark one side of the channel as the boundary.
Position the attacker near the inside edge of the channel.
Place the defender 4 metres in front and slightly inside the attacker.
Mark a dangerous central gate and a lower-value boundary gate.
A third player acts as observer and reset feeder.
The attacker attempts to reach either gate.
The defender must prioritise protecting the central gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder starts the attacker with a handball.
The defender closes from an inside starting position.
The defender angles their approach to remove the central gate.
The attacker may attempt to move inside or continue towards the boundary.
The defender corrals until the attacker is within safe tackling range.
Once the boundary restricts the attacker’s movement, the defender completes a legal side-on tackle.
The defender scores two points for a completed tackle before either gate.
The defender scores one point for forcing the attacker through the boundary gate under pressure.
The attacker scores two points for escaping through the central gate.
Players rotate after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Protect the central and most dangerous space first.
Approach from inside the attacker’s line.
Keep enough distance to react to an inside sidestep.
Use the boundary as an additional defender.
Reduce space gradually instead of lunging.
Commit when the attacker’s exit options are limited.
Maintain legal contact and safe head placement.
Avoid pushing the attacker across the boundary after the tackle is controlled.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender protects the central gate.
Whether the approach angle directs the attacker towards the boundary.
Whether the defender remains patient.
Whether the tackle occurs only after space has been reduced.
Whether the defender avoids over-running the attacker.
Whether contact remains controlled near the boundary.

commonErrors.error: Defender approaches from the boundary side.
commonErrors.correction: Start inside and remove the dangerous central exit.

commonErrors.error: Defender commits before the attacker reaches restricted space.
commonErrors.correction: Continue corralling until the boundary reduces the options.

commonErrors.error: Defender becomes too passive and concedes ground.
commonErrors.correction: Close the space in controlled stages.

commonErrors.error: Tackler pushes the opponent over the line.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the tackle and stop applying force once control is established.

commonErrors.error: Defender watches the football and loses inside position.
commonErrors.correction: Track the attacker’s inside hip.

progressions: Allow the attacker to use a fend-off.
Add a support attacker inside the channel.
Reduce the channel width.
Begin the defender in a recovering position behind the attacker.
regressions: Predetermine that the attacker must use the boundary gate.
Use two-handed touch instead of tackling.
Reduce the attacker to jogging speed.
Mark a visible inside lane the defender must protect.
successIndicators: Funnel the attacker towards the boundary.
Recognise the correct moment to tackle.
Complete controlled contact without unnecessary boundary force.
matchApplication: Defenders can reduce an opponent’s options by using the boundary as part of the defensive structure. Protecting the corridor and forcing play wide creates predictable tackle opportunities and lowers the risk of being beaten into dangerous space.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle

title: Ground-Ball Collection Tackle
primarySkill: Tackling an opponent after a ground-ball collection
objective: Teach defenders to apply pressure during a ground-ball contest while delaying contact until the opponent has regained a safe, upright tackling height.
groundSize: Grids approximately 10 metres long and 8 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a feeder at one end of the grid.
Place an attacker and defender side by side approximately 6 metres from the feeder.
Mark a collection zone in the centre.
Place a handball target 5 metres beyond the collection zone.
The feeder rolls the football into the collection zone.
The attacker has first opportunity to collect.
The defender applies pressure but may not tackle while the attacker’s head is down or body is below safe tackling height.
A fourth player acts as observer and target.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football into the collection zone.
The attacker moves to collect the ground ball.
The defender closes space without making contact while the attacker is bent over the football.
The defender uses footwork and body position to block the attacker’s preferred exit.
Once the attacker has secured the football and returned towards an upright position, the defender may tackle.
The attacker attempts to complete a handball to the target.
The defender attempts to control the torso and disposal arm legally.
The repetition stops after a completed tackle, disposal or turnover.
Players rotate through feeder, attacker, defender and target roles.
coachingPoints: Maintain pressure without contacting a player whose head is over the football.
Control the opponent’s exit space while they collect.
Keep the feet moving rather than leaning over the contest.
Identify when the ball carrier has reached a safe tackling height.
Lower the hips to match the opponent’s rising body position.
Target the torso and disposal arm.
Avoid contact below the knees or through the opponent’s back.
Recover immediately if the football spills free.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders avoid unsafe contact during collection.
Whether the defender controls the likely exit path.
Whether the tackle is delayed until the attacker rises.
Whether contact remains within the legal zone.
Whether the defender affects the disposal arm.
Whether both players react appropriately to a loose football.

commonErrors.error: Defender tackles while the attacker’s head is down.
commonErrors.correction: Delay contact and control the exit space until the player rises.

commonErrors.error: Defender stops and waits passively.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the feet active and reduce the attacker’s available space.

commonErrors.error: Tackler contacts below the knees.
commonErrors.correction: Target the torso as the ball carrier returns upright.

commonErrors.error: Defender arrives directly through the opponent’s back.
commonErrors.correction: Approach from the side and protect the likely exit.

commonErrors.error: Tackler continues holding after the ball spills.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and compete for the football.

progressions: Allow the attacker to choose either exit side.
Increase the speed and unpredictability of the roll.
Add a second defender arriving late.
Permit the attacker to use a controlled fend-off after standing.
regressions: Predetermine the attacker’s exit direction.
Use a stationary football.
Replace the tackle with a two-handed touch.
Begin the defender farther away to create more reaction time.
successIndicators: Avoid contact while the opponent is vulnerable over the football.
Maintain active pressure during the collection.
Complete legal contact after the attacker rises.
Release and recover if possession changes.
matchApplication: Ground-ball contests create a significant risk of high or dangerous contact. Defenders must protect the player whose head is over the football while still applying pressure, closing exits and preparing to tackle once the opponent regains an upright position.

title: Handball-Receive Pressure Tackle
primarySkill: Closing and tackling after a handball receive
objective: Develop the defender’s ability to anticipate a handball receive, close while the football is travelling and complete a controlled tackle before the receiver can accelerate or dispose effectively.
groundSize: Rectangles approximately 14 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a feeder with a football near one end of the grid.
Place two potential receivers approximately 8 metres away and 5 metres apart.
Position one defender between the feeder and receivers.
Place a disposal target beyond the receivers.
A fifth player acts as safety observer and return feeder.
The feeder selects either receiver with a handball.
The defender may move when the feeder begins the handball action.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both receivers move within their designated lanes.
The feeder selects one receiver and releases the handball.
The defender reads the feeder’s body position and the handball’s direction.
The defender closes on the selected receiver while the football is travelling.
The non-selected receiver clears away from the contact area.
The receiver gathers the football and attempts to handball to the target.
The defender decelerates and completes a legal tackle after possession is established.
The defender attempts to control the receiver’s disposal arm.
The repetition ends after a tackle, clean disposal or turnover.
Players rotate through all roles.
coachingPoints: Scan both receivers before the handball is released.
Read the feeder’s hips, shoulders and handball action.
Move immediately once the target becomes clear.
Adjust the line if the handball is inaccurate.
Avoid early contact before the receiver controls the football.
Arrive close enough to wrap rather than reach.
Identify the receiver’s preferred handball arm.
Maintain upright control and release promptly.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender scans both potential receivers.
How early the selected receiver is identified.
Whether the approach adjusts to the actual handball.
Whether contact occurs only after possession.
Whether the defender controls the disposal side.
Whether the non-selected receiver clears the contact area safely.

commonErrors.error: Defender guesses before the handball is released.
commonErrors.correction: Stay balanced and read the feeder’s action.

commonErrors.error: Defender reacts too late.
commonErrors.correction: Begin moving as soon as the target becomes clear.

commonErrors.error: Tackler runs to the receiver’s starting point.
commonErrors.correction: Track the football and receiver’s actual movement.

commonErrors.error: Defender contacts the receiver before possession.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate and wait until the football is controlled.

commonErrors.error: Tackler wraps below the arms and concedes a handball.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the legal wrap to include the disposal arm.

progressions: Allow receivers to cross or change lanes before the handball.
Add a second defender.
Permit the feeder to fake before releasing.
Allow the receiver to evade after possession.
regressions: Use only one receiver.
Predetermine the selected receiver.
Reduce the closing distance.
Replace tackling with two-handed touch pressure.
successIndicators: Scan and identify the receiving threat.
Move while the football is travelling.
matchApplication: Handball chains create rapid movement through congestion and transition. Defenders who anticipate the next receiver and move during the handball can close space before the opponent accelerates, disrupting overlap and preventing clean exits.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat

title: Traffic Navigation Tackle
primarySkill: Navigating traffic before completing a tackle
objective: Teach defenders to move through or around nearby players, maintain visual contact with the ball carrier and complete a safe tackle without colliding with non-involved players.
groundSize: Grids approximately 14 metres by 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one ball carrier at one end of the grid and one defender at the opposite end.
Place three or four neutral traffic players inside the area.
Neutral players move slowly along assigned lines and may not deliberately block.
Mark two finishing gates for the ball carrier.
A feeder starts the repetition with a handball to the attacker.
The defender must navigate safely through the moving traffic.
Contact remains upright and controlled.
howTheDrillWorks:
Neutral players begin moving along their assigned paths.
The feeder handballs to the attacker.
The attacker moves towards either finishing gate.
The defender tracks the attacker while scanning the traffic.
The defender chooses whether to move through an available gap or around the traffic.
The defender communicates when passing close to a neutral player.
Once clear, the defender closes and completes a legal tackle.
The attacker scores one point for crossing a gate.
The defender scores one point for forcing a retreat or ineffective disposal and two points for a completed tackle.
Players rotate through attacker, defender, feeder and neutral roles.
coachingPoints: Keep the head up and scan beyond the nearest player.
Maintain visual contact with the ball carrier while navigating traffic.
Select clear running lanes rather than forcing through closing gaps.
Communicate with nearby players.
Avoid using neutral players as uncontrolled screens.
Re-establish balance after changing the pursuit line.
Decelerate before entering contact.
Complete the tackle only when a safe angle is available.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders scan both traffic and the ball carrier.
Whether players choose safe pursuit routes.
Whether communication occurs near neutral players.
Whether the defender regains balance after navigating traffic.
Whether the tackle angle remains legal.
Whether unnecessary collisions are avoided.

commonErrors.error: Defender watches the nearest traffic player and loses the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Scan through the traffic and regularly relocate the attacker.

commonErrors.error: Player forces through a closing gap.
commonErrors.correction: Take the safer outside route when the lane is not clear.

commonErrors.error: Defender uses a neutral player as a screen and collides.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain separation and communicate before passing.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives off balance after changing direction.
commonErrors.correction: Use adjustment steps before entering contact range.

commonErrors.error: Defender tackles from behind after being delayed.
commonErrors.correction: Move to the side or continue corralling until a safe angle develops.

progressions: Increase the speed of the neutral players.
Allow neutral players to change direction on a coach’s call.
Add a second attacker available for a handball.
Introduce a second defender who must communicate responsibilities.
regressions: Use stationary cones instead of moving traffic players.
Predetermine the attacker’s finishing gate.
Reduce the number of neutral players.
Use a two-handed touch rather than a tackle.
successIndicators: Maintain awareness of the ball carrier and surrounding traffic.
Complete a legal tackle from an appropriate angle.
matchApplication: Tackles around stoppages and congestion often require defenders to navigate teammates, opponents and officials. Players must maintain vision, avoid collisions and find a safe path to pressure the ball carrier rather than launching blindly through traffic.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat

title: Two-Defender Close and Secure
primarySkill: Coordinating two defenders around a ball carrier
objective: Develop coordinated defensive movement in which one player applies controlled pressure while the second defender closes escape space and supports the tackle without creating unsafe double contact.
groundSize: Grids approximately 12 metres by 10 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Place one attacker with a football at one end of the grid.
Position the primary defender directly in front of the attacker.
Position the supporting defender 4 metres to one side.
Mark one central and two wide exit gates.
A feeder and safety observer stand outside the grid.
The primary defender is responsible for initial pressure.
The supporting defender closes the most dangerous free space.
Only one defender may deliver significant tackling contact at a time.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker receives a handball from the feeder.
The primary defender closes and protects the central exit.
The supporting defender adjusts to remove the attacker’s most likely escape route.
Both defenders communicate who is pressuring and who is supporting.
If the attacker enters the primary defender’s range, the primary defender completes the tackle.
The supporting defender closes nearby space and may secure a free arm only after the first tackle is established.
The supporting defender must not charge into the ball carrier or drive the player backwards.
If the attacker evades the primary defender, the supporting defender becomes the tackler.
The repetition ends after a tackle, disposal or gate entry.
Players rotate through all roles.
coachingPoints: Establish clear roles before contact.
The nearest balanced defender applies pressure.
The second defender protects the most dangerous escape.
Communicate early and continuously.
Avoid both defenders launching at the same moment.
The supporting defender should arrive under control.
Assistance must remain within the legal tackle zone.
Release immediately when the football is no longer in possession or the whistle sounds.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defenders communicate their roles.
Whether the primary defender protects central space.
Whether the supporting defender closes the correct exit.
Whether only one defender initiates major contact.
Whether support contact remains safe and legal.
Whether responsibilities switch after an evasion.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders charge directly at the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one pressure defender and one space defender.

commonErrors.error: Supporting defender arrives at excessive speed.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate and secure space before assisting.

commonErrors.error: Defenders remain silent.
commonErrors.correction: Require an early “mine” or “support” call.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders approach from the same side.
commonErrors.correction: Create complementary angles around the ball carrier.

commonErrors.error: Supporting defender contacts high while reaching for an arm.
commonErrors.correction: Enter lower and secure only within the legal tackle zone.

progressions: Add a support attacker.
Allow the attacker to use a controlled fend-off.
Begin the defenders from recovering positions.
Continue play after an incomplete disposal.
regressions: Predetermine which defender completes the tackle.
Use two-handed touch pressure.
Reduce the attacker to jogging speed.
Remove the wide gates and focus only on complementary angles.
successIndicators: Switch roles when the attacker changes direction.
matchApplication: Team defence requires more than multiple players chasing the football. Coordinated defenders can remove escape options, prevent handball release and secure tackles without creating high contact, front-on collisions or unnecessary numbers at the contest.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat

title: Tackle, Regain Feet and Rejoin
primarySkill: Recovering into play after a completed tackle
objective: Develop the habit of releasing safely, regaining an effective playing position and rejoining the next phase immediately after completing a tackle.
groundSize: Areas approximately 15 metres by 10 metres.
equipment: Tackle bags or controlled partner stations
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Position a tackle bag or controlled ball carrier in the centre of the area.
Mark three coloured recovery gates 5–7 metres away.
Place a feeder with a football beyond the gates.
Position a moving receiver near the feeder.
The tackler begins 3 metres from the initial contact.
A coach or observer controls the release and recovery call.
Where live partners are used, the tackle remains upright.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defender approaches and completes a controlled tackle on the bag or partner.
The coach blows the whistle when the tackle is secure.
The tackler releases immediately.
The coach calls one of the coloured recovery gates.
The defender regains an upright position and accelerates through the called gate.
As the defender moves, the feeder handballs to the receiver.
The defender scans and applies pressure to the receiver with a two-handed touch.
The defender scores one point for immediate release, one point for reaching the correct gate and one point for affecting the receiver.
Players rotate after each repetition.
Complete four to six defensive repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Complete the first tackle before beginning the recovery.
Release immediately on the whistle.
Regain the feet through a stable base rather than turning the back on play.
Lift the eyes while rising.
Identify the recovery call quickly.
Accelerate through the first three steps.
Scan for the next opponent while moving.
Decelerate before applying the second pressure action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the tackle is released promptly.
Whether the defender regains balance efficiently.
Whether the player lifts their eyes while recovering.
Whether the correct gate is identified.
Whether acceleration is immediate.
Whether the second pressure action is controlled.

commonErrors.error: Tackler remains attached after the whistle.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and create separation.

commonErrors.error: Player turns away from play while recovering.
commonErrors.correction: Rise with the chest and eyes facing the next phase.

commonErrors.error: Defender stands slowly after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Use a wide base and drive through the first recovery step.

commonErrors.error: Player runs through the gate without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Lift the eyes and locate the next receiver while moving.

commonErrors.error: Defender arrives uncontrolled at the second contest.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps before applying pressure.

progressions: Replace the second touch with a controlled tackle.
Add two possible receivers.
Require the defender to communicate the next threat.
Begin the initial tackle from a moving chase.
regressions: Use a stationary tackle bag.
Predetermine the recovery gate.
Remove the second opponent.
Reduce the recovery distance.
successIndicators: Complete and release the initial tackle safely.
Keep vision on the developing play.
Arrive at the next contest under control.
matchApplication: After completing a tackle, defenders must avoid becoming spectators. Rapid release, recovery and scanning allow the player to guard space, pressure a receiver, support a teammate or contest a loose football during the next phase.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat

title: Tackling in Movement Assessment
primarySkill: Assessment of tackling while moving
objective: Assess whether players can apply safe tackling fundamentals while tracking moving opponents, navigating changing space and transitioning into repeat defensive actions.
groundSize: Five assessment stations across approximately one-third of an oval.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Construct five separate assessment stations.
Station 1 assesses moving chase and side-on tackle entry.
Station 2 assesses closing on a receiving player.
Station 3 assesses boundary funnel and tackle timing.
Station 4 assesses ground-ball collection pressure and safe contact timing.
Station 5 assesses tackle release, recovery and repeat pressure.
Assign a coach or trained observer to each station.
Divide players evenly and rotate every five to seven minutes.
Match players appropriately for size and contact confidence.
Use a consistent scoring scale at every station.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, the defender pursues a moving ball carrier through a lane and completes a controlled tackle.
The observer assesses pursuit angle, speed matching, head position and two-arm wrap.
At Station 2, the defender closes while a handball or short kick travels to a receiver.
The observer assesses anticipation, legal timing and disposal control.
At Station 3, the defender protects an inside gate and funnels the attacker towards a boundary tackle opportunity.
The observer assesses positioning, patience and decision timing.
At Station 4, the defender pressures an opponent collecting a ground ball and delays contact until safe tackling height.
The observer assesses player protection, exit control and legal contact.
At Station 5, the defender completes an initial tackle, releases, recovers through a called gate and pressures a second receiver.
Each assessed behaviour receives:
2 points: Consistently demonstrated.
1 point: Demonstrated inconsistently or after correction.
0 points: Not demonstrated or performed unsafely.
Any high, low, reckless or uncontrolled contact stops the repetition immediately.
Coaches record one technical strength, one movement priority and one recommended next step for every player.
coachingPoints: Safety remains the primary assessment standard.
Defenders must use efficient pursuit angles rather than diving from behind.
Closing speed must be reduced before contact.
Contact must occur only after legal possession is established.
Players must protect opponents who are bent over the football.
Tacklers must use safe head placement and a complete two-arm wrap.
Defenders should recognise when to corral rather than tackle.
Release and repeat movement must occur immediately after the contest.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players select effective pursuit and interception angles.
Whether defenders adjust to moving receivers.
Whether approach speed is controlled.
Whether inside and dangerous space is protected.
Whether contact is delayed when an opponent is vulnerable over the football.
Whether head and shoulder placement remain safe.
Whether both arms secure the tackle.
Whether players release immediately.
Whether defenders transition into a repeat action.
Whether decision quality remains stable under movement demands.

commonErrors.error: Defender demonstrates correct stationary technique but loses shape while running.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce approach speed and rebuild the final three steps.

commonErrors.error: Player contacts receivers before possession.
commonErrors.correction: Continue closing but delay contact until control is established.

commonErrors.error: Defender tackles from directly behind.
commonErrors.correction: Improve the pursuit angle and reach the opponent’s side.

commonErrors.error: Player lunges instead of using the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain inside position and reduce space patiently.

commonErrors.error: Defender contacts a player whose head is over the football.
commonErrors.correction: Control the exit and wait until the opponent rises.

commonErrors.error: Tackler completes the first action but fails to recover.
commonErrors.correction: Make release and repeat movement part of every assessed repetition.

progressions: Increase movement speed for players who meet all technical and safety standards.
Add genuine disposal decisions at each station.
Introduce a supporting attacker or defender.
Record station scores across multiple training blocks.
Compare assessment results under fresh and moderately fatigued conditions.
regressions: Return to stationary tackle-bag work.
Use controlled two-handed touch pressure.
Predetermine movement directions.
Reduce the number of decisions at each station.
Reassess individual stations rather than completing the full circuit.
successIndicators: Track and pursue moving opponents efficiently.
Recognise safe and legal contact timing.
Maintain correct head, shoulder and arm technique.
Recover into the next defensive action.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether players can transfer introductory tackling technique into moving football situations. Successful defenders must combine safe contact with pursuit, anticipation, space control, decision making and repeat effort rather than treating the tackle as an isolated action.
relatedDrills: TK-029 – Tackle, Regain Feet and Rejoin

title: Accelerate–Decelerate Tackle Approach
primarySkill: Controlling speed during the tackle approach
objective: Develop the ability to accelerate while closing open space and decelerate into a balanced position before completing a legal tackle.
groundSize: Parallel lanes approximately 14 metres long and 4 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark several lanes approximately 14 metres long.
Place a defender’s starting cone at one end.
Position the ball carrier 8 metres ahead of the defender.
Mark a deceleration zone beginning 3 metres before the expected contact point.
Place a finishing line at the end of the lane.
A third player acts as the safety observer.
The ball carrier moves at approximately 50–60 per cent speed.
Match players appropriately for size and physical maturity.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the ball carrier begins moving towards the finishing line.
The defender accelerates aggressively to reduce the initial gap.
When entering the marked deceleration zone, the defender shortens the stride and lowers the hips.
The defender adjusts towards the ball carrier’s near hip.
The defender places the near foot close to the opponent.
The tackler makes legal shoulder contact with the head safely beside or behind the ball carrier.
Both arms wrap securely around the torso and at least one disposal arm where possible.
The tackler travels with the opponent for no more than two steps.
The coach calls “release” once control is established.
Players rotate through ball carrier, defender and observer roles.
Complete three repetitions from each side.
coachingPoints: Accelerate while the gap is large and the attacker cannot evade immediately.
Begin reducing speed before entering tackling distance.
Use several short steps rather than one large braking step.
Keep the hips low and chest upright during deceleration.
Adjust towards the opponent’s hip rather than running directly at the spine.
Place the near foot close before making contact.
Maintain safe head position and legal tackle height.
Do not allow urgency to create reckless contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders accelerate during the open-space phase.
Whether deceleration begins before contact range.
Whether the defender remains balanced during the final steps.
Whether the approach angle reaches the opponent’s side.
Whether the near foot arrives close enough to prevent reaching.
Whether the tackle remains upright and controlled.

commonErrors.error: Defender approaches at one speed throughout.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate early, then deliberately reduce speed before contact.

commonErrors.error: Player uses one heavy braking step.
commonErrors.correction: Use three or four shorter adjustment steps.

commonErrors.error: Defender becomes upright while decelerating.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the knees and hips while keeping the chest forward.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches because the feet stop too early.
commonErrors.correction: Continue moving until the near foot lands beside the opponent.

commonErrors.error: Defender collides at excessive speed.
commonErrors.correction: Begin deceleration earlier and match the ball carrier’s pace.

progressions: Increase the ball carrier’s running speed.
Remove the visible deceleration-zone cones.
Allow the attacker to change pace once.
Add a controlled handball attempt during the tackle.
regressions: Reduce the starting gap.
Use a moving tackle bag.
Keep both players at jogging speed.
Mark each required short step with flat cones.
successIndicators: Close open space with purposeful acceleration.
Maintain balance throughout the final approach.
Arrive beside rather than directly behind the ball carrier.
matchApplication: Defenders regularly cover several metres before reaching a ball carrier. Effective pressure requires speed, but the defender must convert that speed into a balanced tackle approach. Players who cannot decelerate are more likely to miss, make high contact or be evaded.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle

title: Change-of-Direction Pursuit Gate
primarySkill: Pursuing through repeated changes of direction
objective: Develop the defender’s ability to maintain balance, recover the pursuit line and complete a controlled tackle after multiple changes of direction.
groundSize: Zigzag lanes approximately 14 metres long and 8 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark three staggered gates through each lane.
Place the first gate towards the left, the second towards the right and the final gate centrally.
The attacker begins with the football 2 metres ahead of the defender.
A third player acts as observer and gate caller.
The observer calls which side of each gate the attacker must use.
The attacker works at approximately 60 per cent speed.
A contact zone begins after the final directional gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the attacker and defender enter the lane.
The observer calls the first gate direction.
The attacker changes line and carries the football through the called side.
The defender tracks the attacker’s hips and adjusts without crossing the feet unnecessarily.
The observer calls the second gate direction as the players advance.
The defender recovers the pursuit line after each change.
After the final gate, the attacker accelerates towards the finishing line.
The defender closes from the side and completes a legal controlled tackle.
The tackle remains upright and ends on the coach’s whistle.
Players rotate through attacker, defender and observer roles.
Complete four repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Watch the attacker’s hips rather than the football.
Use short adjustment steps through each change of direction.
Avoid over-running the attacker’s new line.
Recover acceleration immediately after turning.
Maintain a pursuit line towards the near hip.
Do not attempt contact while off balance.
Decelerate again before completing the tackle.
Keep the head behind or beside the opponent during contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders remain visually connected to the attacker.
Whether players cross their feet or lose balance through turns.
Whether acceleration returns immediately after each directional change.
Whether defenders recover to the attacker’s hip line.
Whether the final approach is controlled.
Whether contact technique remains safe after the agility demand.

commonErrors.error: Defender guesses the attacker’s direction.
commonErrors.correction: Stay balanced and react to the attacker’s hips.

commonErrors.error: Player takes wide looping turns.
commonErrors.correction: Use shorter steps and redirect through the nearest efficient line.

commonErrors.error: Defender stops after each gate.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate immediately once the new line is identified.

commonErrors.error: Tackler attempts contact while still turning.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish balance before entering tackle range.

commonErrors.error: Defender reaches after falling behind.
commonErrors.correction: Continue pursuing the hip until a safe side-on position develops.

progressions: Remove the predetermined gate order.
Increase the attacker’s speed.
Allow the attacker to use a baulk before one gate.
Add a handball target beyond the finishing line.
regressions: Use only one directional gate.
Predetermine all gate directions before the repetition.
Replace the tackle with a two-handed touch.
Increase the width between gates.
successIndicators: Track the opponent through repeated directional changes.
matchApplication: Ball carriers frequently change direction around congestion, support runners and defensive traffic. Defenders must recover their line repeatedly without lunging or losing balance before completing the tackle.

title: Overlap Runner Pressure
primarySkill: Pressuring a moving overlap receiver
objective: Teach defenders to identify an overlap runner, leave the initial ball carrier at the correct moment and close the receiving player before clean acceleration can occur.
groundSize: Rectangles approximately 18 metres long and 12 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Place a starting attacker with the football near one end of the grid.
Position an overlap runner 4 metres behind and to the side of the ball carrier.
Place the defender 5 metres in front of the initial ball carrier.
Position a second defender or coach as a passive pressure marker on the initial ball carrier.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
A safety observer stands outside the grid.
The overlap runner must receive by handball before entering the scoring gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The initial ball carrier advances towards the defender.
The overlap runner accelerates past on either side.
The ball carrier may retain possession briefly or handball to the overlap runner.
The defender protects the central scoring line while scanning both attackers.
Once the handball is released, the defender redirects towards the receiver.
The defender closes while the football is travelling.
After the receiver gains possession, the defender completes a legal controlled tackle or forces a rushed disposal.
The receiver scores by crossing the finishing gate.
The defender scores two points for a completed tackle and one for forcing an ineffective disposal.
Players rotate through all roles.
coachingPoints: Maintain vision of both the ball carrier and overlap runner.
Protect the central and most dangerous running lane.
Do not leave the ball carrier before the handball action becomes clear.
Redirect immediately when the football is released.
Run towards the receiver’s likely possession point.
Decelerate as the receiver gathers the football.
Target the torso and likely disposal arm.
Communicate the change of defensive responsibility.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender scans the overlap runner early.
Whether central space remains protected.
Whether the defender moves at the correct moment.
Whether the pursuit line reaches the receiver’s possession point.
Whether contact occurs only after possession.
Whether the tackle affects the next disposal.

commonErrors.error: Defender follows the overlap runner too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold central position until the handball action is clear.

commonErrors.error: Defender remains with the original ball carrier after release.
commonErrors.correction: Redirect immediately once possession transfers.

commonErrors.error: Player runs behind the receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Attack the likely possession point rather than following the current path.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives before the receiver controls the football.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate and delay contact until possession is established.

commonErrors.error: Defender reaches for the football.
commonErrors.correction: Close body space and wrap the receiver’s torso and disposal arm.

progressions: Allow the initial ball carrier to fake the handball.
Add a second overlap runner.
Permit the receiver to return the handball.
Add an active second defender.
regressions: Predetermine which side the overlap runner uses.
Require the initial ball carrier to handball immediately.
Replace the tackle with a two-handed touch.
Reduce the overlap runner’s speed.
successIndicators: Apply legal pressure that affects the next action.
matchApplication: Overlap handball is commonly used to break defensive lines. Defenders must recognise the running receiver, adjust responsibility and close the next possession rather than remaining attached to an opponent who has already released the football.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat

title: Handball Chain Chase Tackle
primarySkill: Chasing through a moving handball chain
objective: Develop the defender’s ability to track possession through consecutive handballs and close the most dangerous receiver rather than following the football from behind.
groundSize: Corridors approximately 22 metres long and 12 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position three attackers in staggered locations through the corridor.
Place one defender 3 metres behind the first attacker.
Position a second defender or coach as a passive central-space protector.
Mark a finishing gate at the far end.
Attackers must use at least two handballs before attempting to cross the gate.
The active defender may tackle only the current ball carrier.
A safety observer stands outside the corridor.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first attacker begins running with the football.
The defender pursues and closes from behind.
The attacker handballs to the second runner.
The defender releases the first opponent and redirects towards the new ball carrier.
The second attacker may carry briefly before handballing to the third runner.
The defender chooses the most efficient line towards the next receiver.
After the final receive, the defender attempts a legal controlled tackle before the finishing gate.
The attackers score one point for crossing the gate with controlled possession.
The defender scores two points for a completed tackle and one for forcing a turnover or ineffective handball.
Players rotate after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Follow the transfer of possession rather than remaining attached to the previous opponent.
Release immediately once the football is handballed.
Use diagonal running lines to reduce distance.
Scan ahead for the next likely receiver.
Protect central space while pursuing.
Communicate each change of ball carrier.
Accelerate after every possession transfer.
Decelerate before the final pressure action.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender releases each previous ball carrier.
Whether the next receiver is identified early.
Whether pursuit lines are direct and efficient.
Whether the defender maintains repeat running effort.
Whether central attacking space is protected.
Whether the final tackle is controlled despite fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Defender continues chasing the previous ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Redirect immediately when possession changes.

commonErrors.error: Player follows the football in a curved line.
commonErrors.correction: Run directly towards the next possession point.

commonErrors.error: Defender watches only the current ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Scan ahead for the next receiver.

commonErrors.error: Player slows significantly after each handball.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate immediately following every transfer.

commonErrors.error: Final tackle is reckless because of fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate and restore technique before contact.

progressions: Add a fourth attacking runner.
Allow attackers to handball backwards or laterally.
Add a second active defender.
Continue play after a spill or turnover.
regressions: Predetermine the handball sequence.
Reduce the corridor length.
Replace the final tackle with a pressure touch.
Allow the defender to begin closer to the second receiver.
matchApplication: Opposition teams use handball chains to move through congestion and exploit defenders who remain focused on the previous contest. Effective defenders repeatedly transfer pressure to the next ball carrier and maintain involvement across several possessions.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat
TK-029 – Tackle, Regain Feet and Rejoin

title: Kick-Receive Closing Tackle
primarySkill: Closing on an opponent receiving a short kick
objective: Teach defenders to close while a short kick is travelling, respect a completed mark and apply immediate legal pressure when the football is played on or not marked.
groundSize: Grids approximately 20 metres long and 12 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a kicker at one end of the grid.
Place a receiver 12–15 metres away.
Position the defender 5 metres to the side of the receiver.
Mark a protected mark zone around the receiver.
Place a disposal target beyond the receiver.
A fifth player acts as observer and return feeder.
The kick may result in a clean mark, dropped mark or play-on call.
The defender must respond according to the outcome.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver leads inside the grid.
The kicker delivers a short kick.
The defender closes while reading the football’s flight.
If the receiver completes a mark, the defender stops outside the protected area and establishes the mark.
The coach may call “play on”, after which the defender closes and applies pressure.
If the mark is dropped or the kick is touched, the defender may continue closing immediately.
The receiver attempts to dispose to the target.
The defender attempts a legal tackle or forces an ineffective disposal.
The repetition ends after a disposal, tackle or turnover.
Players rotate through kicker, receiver, defender, target and observer roles.
coachingPoints: Read the kick’s flight while tracking the receiver.
Close space without entering recklessly underneath the football.
Respect the protected area after a completed mark.
Stop under balance rather than drifting over the mark.
React immediately to a play-on call or dropped mark.
Adjust tackle height to the receiver’s body position.
Avoid front-on contact with a player focused on the football.
Maintain vision and safe head placement.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders move while the kick travels.
Whether players recognise a completed mark.
Whether the defender stops outside the protected area.
Whether reaction to play on is immediate.
Whether the defender avoids dangerous front-on contact.
Whether pressure affects the receiver’s disposal.

commonErrors.error: Defender waits for the receiver to mark before moving.
commonErrors.correction: Close space while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Player enters the protected area after the mark.
commonErrors.correction: Stop under control and establish the mark correctly.

commonErrors.error: Defender relaxes after the mark and misses play on.
commonErrors.correction: Remain balanced and ready for immediate movement.

commonErrors.error: Tackler contacts a receiver exposed under the football.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust the approach and avoid front-on contact.

commonErrors.error: Defender overruns the receiver after a dropped mark.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final steps and track the football’s actual position.

progressions: Allow the receiver to choose whether to play on.
Add a second leading receiver.
Vary the kick’s height and accuracy.
Add a support runner for the receiver.
regressions: Predetermine whether each kick will be marked or dropped.
Use handball instead of kicking.
Reduce the defender’s closing distance.
Replace tackling with two-handed touch pressure.
successIndicators: React quickly to play on or a loose football.
Apply legal pressure to the receiver.
matchApplication: Defenders must close space on short-kick receivers while understanding when contact is permitted. Correct positioning can prevent immediate play on, pressure the next disposal and create a tackle opportunity if the mark is dropped or the player moves off the line.

title: Loose-Ball Win to Moving Tackle
primarySkill: Transitioning from a loose-ball contest into a moving tackle
objective: Develop the ability to react after an opponent wins a loose football, recover defensive position and complete a controlled tackle as the ball carrier exits the contest.
groundSize: Grids approximately 14 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a loose-ball zone in the centre of the grid.
Place two players side by side 4 metres from the zone.
Position a feeder outside the grid.
Mark two exit gates beyond the loose-ball zone.
A fourth player acts as safety observer and disposal target.
The feeder rolls an uneven football towards the contest.
One player is nominated as the initial collector and the other as the recovering defender.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls the football into the loose-ball zone.
The nominated attacker moves to collect.
The defender applies safe pressure without contacting the opponent while their head is over the football.
Once the attacker secures possession and exits the collection posture, they accelerate towards either gate.
The defender recovers towards the attacker’s near hip.
The defender closes the final space and completes a legal side-on tackle.
The attacker attempts to handball to the target before being secured.
The repetition ends after a tackle, disposal or turnover.
Players exchange attacker and defender roles.
Rotate the feeder and target after several repetitions.
coachingPoints: Protect the opponent while their head is over the football.
Stay active and control the likely exit.
React immediately when possession is established.
Accelerate into the pursuit line rather than standing at the contest.
Target the attacker’s near hip.
Decelerate before contact.
Place the head safely behind or beside the opponent.
Release immediately if the football spills.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender avoids unsafe collection contact.
Whether the likely exit is controlled.
How quickly the defender transitions into pursuit.
Whether the defender reaches a side-on tackling angle.
Whether contact remains legal and upright.
Whether the defender reacts correctly if possession changes.

commonErrors.error: Defender contacts the attacker during collection.
commonErrors.correction: Delay contact and control the exit until the player rises.

commonErrors.error: Player stands behind the contest after possession is won.
commonErrors.correction: Transition immediately into the pursuit run.

commonErrors.error: Defender chases directly at the opponent’s back.
commonErrors.correction: Move towards the near hip and reach the side.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches after losing the initial race.
commonErrors.correction: Continue running until safe contact range develops.

commonErrors.error: Defender continues holding after a spill.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and compete for the football.

progressions: Make the loose-ball roll unpredictable.
Allow either player to win possession.
Add a support receiver.
Continue play after the first disposal.
regressions: Use a stationary football.
Predetermine the attacker’s exit gate.
Replace the tackle with a two-handed touch.
Begin the defender closer to the attacker’s exit line.
successIndicators: Apply safe pressure around the loose football.
Identify the ball carrier’s exit quickly.
React appropriately to a spill or disposal.
matchApplication: Players often lose the initial ground-ball contest but can still influence the phase by recovering immediately. Effective transition from contest pressure to pursuit can prevent clean exits and create a turnover after the opponent gains possession.
relatedDrills: TK-029 – Tackle, Regain Feet and Rejoin

title: Give-and-Go Recovery Pressure
primarySkill: Defending a give-and-go possession pattern
objective: Teach defenders to remain involved after an opponent disposes, recognise the return runner and pressure the second possession in a give-and-go movement.
groundSize: Rectangles approximately 18 metres long and 12 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position two attackers 6 metres apart.
Place the first defender near the initial ball carrier.
Position a second defender 4 metres from the support attacker.
Mark a finishing gate beyond the attackers.
The attacking pair must complete a handball and receive a return handball before scoring.
Defenders must communicate when responsibility changes.
A feeder or observer manages resets.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first attacker begins moving with the football.
The first defender closes and applies controlled pressure.
The attacker handballs to the support player and continues running.
The first defender releases immediately and tracks the continuing runner.
The second defender pressures the new ball carrier.
The ball carrier attempts to return the handball to the original attacker.
Both defenders communicate whether to stay, switch or support.
Once the original attacker receives again, the nearest balanced defender attempts a legal tackle.
Attackers score by crossing the finishing gate.
Defenders score by completing a tackle or forcing a turnover.
Players rotate through attacking and defending roles.
coachingPoints: Do not stop after the first opponent disposes.
Track the original attacker’s continuing run.
Communicate the change of ball carrier.
The nearest balanced defender applies pressure.
The supporting defender protects the return lane.
Move while the return handball is travelling.
Avoid both defenders chasing the same player.
Complete the final tackle from balance.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the first defender releases after the handball.
Whether the continuing runner is tracked.
Whether defenders communicate responsibility.
Whether the return passing lane is protected.
Whether defenders avoid duplication.
Whether the final receiver is pressured immediately.

commonErrors.error: First defender watches the football after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue tracking the original attacker’s run.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders pressure the same ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate and protect separate threats.

commonErrors.error: Return handball is conceded through central space.
commonErrors.correction: Position the support defender inside the passing lane.

commonErrors.error: Defender reacts only after the return receive.
commonErrors.correction: Move while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Final tackle is attempted from behind.
commonErrors.correction: Improve the recovery angle and reach the receiver’s side.

progressions: Allow attackers to fake the return handball.
Add a third attacker.
Permit defenders to switch opponents freely.
Continue play after an incomplete handball.
regressions: Predetermine the give-and-go sequence.
Use two-handed touch pressure.
Reduce the working distance.
Nominate which defender completes the final pressure action.
successIndicators: Remain involved after the first disposal.
Pressure or tackle the final receiver.
matchApplication: Give-and-go handball is used to move past a defender who stops after the first disposal. Defenders must continue tracking runners, communicate switches and pressure the return possession to prevent line-breaking movement.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat
TK-036 – Loose-Ball Win to Moving Tackle

title: Inside-Out Defensive Angle
primarySkill: Closing from inside to outside
objective: Develop the ability to approach from an inside position, protect the corridor and force a moving ball carrier towards less dangerous outside space before tackling.
groundSize: Channels approximately 16 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Mark a central corridor lane through the channel.
Mark a wider outside lane towards one boundary.
The attacker begins with the football near the centre.
The defender starts 5 metres away on the inside or corridor side.
Mark a high-value central scoring gate and a lower-value outside gate.
A third player acts as observer and reset feeder.
The defender must remain inside the attacker’s line during the initial approach.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder starts the attacker with a handball.
The attacker moves towards either the central or outside gate.
The defender closes from the corridor side.
The defender positions the body to remove the central lane.
The attacker is encouraged towards the outside lane.
The defender continues reducing space without lunging.
Once the attacker enters safe range near the outside lane, the defender completes a legal tackle.
The defender scores two points for a tackle and one for forcing the outside gate.
The attacker scores two points for entering the central gate.
Players rotate roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Begin inside the ball carrier’s running line.
Protect the corridor before attempting contact.
Angle the hips and shoulders to show outside space.
Maintain a reaction buffer while the attacker can still cut inside.
Reduce space in controlled stages.
Use the outside line as an additional defender.
Commit only from balance.
Avoid pushing the attacker after control is established.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender maintains inside position.
Whether central space is protected.
Whether the body angle influences the attacker’s route.
Whether the defender remains patient.
Whether the tackle occurs from balance.
Whether contact remains controlled near the outside line.

commonErrors.error: Defender approaches directly and leaves the corridor open.
commonErrors.correction: Start inside and angle the attacker towards the outside lane.

commonErrors.error: Defender turns too far sideways.
commonErrors.correction: Remain square enough to react to an inside cut.

commonErrors.error: Player lunges before the attacker reaches restricted space.
commonErrors.correction: Continue corralling until the outside line limits movement.

commonErrors.error: Defender gives excessive ground.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce space steadily while maintaining balance.

commonErrors.error: Tackler drives the opponent over the line.
commonErrors.correction: Stop applying force when the tackle is secure.

progressions: Add a support attacker inside the corridor.
Allow the ball carrier a controlled fend-off.
Begin the defender in a recovery run.
Reduce the outside lane width.
regressions: Predetermine that the attacker uses the outside gate.
Mark a visible inside positioning line for the defender.
Use two-handed touch pressure.
Reduce the attacker’s speed.
successIndicators: Influence the attacker towards outside space.
Recognise the correct moment to tackle.
matchApplication: Defenders are often required to protect the corridor and force the opposition towards the boundary. An inside-out approach reduces dangerous attacking options and creates more predictable tackle opportunities.
relatedDrills: TK-002 – Closing Space and Approach Angle

title: Multi-Lane Tracking and Switch
primarySkill: Switching defensive responsibility between moving opponents
objective: Teach defenders to track moving attackers across adjacent lanes, communicate a switch and apply pressure to the opponent who becomes the immediate ball carrier.
groundSize: Three adjacent lanes, each approximately 18 metres long and 5 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark three parallel lanes.
Place one attacker in each lane.
Position two defenders between the lanes.
A feeder begins with the football at one end.
Attackers may run straight or cross into an adjacent lane at designated crossing zones.
The feeder may handball to any attacker.
Defenders must communicate whether to stay with their original opponent or switch.
Mark a finishing line at the far end.
howTheDrillWorks:
All three attackers begin moving through their lanes.
The feeder releases the football to one attacker.
Attackers may cross lanes only inside marked crossing zones.
