Defenders track the attackers while maintaining vision of the football.
When attackers cross, defenders call “stay” or “switch”.
The nearest balanced defender closes the ball carrier.
The second defender protects the most dangerous support option.
The active defender completes a legal tackle or forces a rushed disposal.
Attackers score by carrying or disposing the football across the finishing line.
Defenders score by completing a tackle or forcing a turnover.
Players rotate between attacking, defending and feeding roles.
coachingPoints: Scan the football and nearby runners continuously.
Communicate before attackers complete the lane crossing.
Switch only when it preserves better defensive position.
The nearest balanced defender pressures the football.
The supporting defender protects the dangerous receiver.
Avoid two defenders following the same attacker.
Move during the disposal rather than after the receive.
Complete contact only from a safe angle.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders scan across multiple lanes.
Whether communication occurs before or during crossing movements.
Whether switches improve defensive position.
Whether one defender takes responsibility for the ball carrier.
Whether the support option is protected.
Whether the final pressure action remains controlled.

commonErrors.error: Defenders communicate after the attackers cross.
commonErrors.correction: Call the switch as soon as the crossing movement develops.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders follow one attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one ball defender and one support-space defender.

commonErrors.error: Defender switches without checking teammate position.
commonErrors.correction: Scan and communicate before changing responsibility.

commonErrors.error: Player watches the football and loses a crossing runner.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain peripheral awareness of both ball and opponent.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives from an unsafe rear angle.
commonErrors.correction: Continue tracking until a side-on position is available.

progressions: Allow unrestricted lane changes.
Add a third defender.
Permit kicks as well as handballs.
Continue play after the first tackle or turnover.
regressions: Predetermine the receiving attacker.
Use only two lanes.
Require attackers to cross at one fixed point.
Replace tackling with two-handed touch pressure.
successIndicators: Maintain coverage of the football and support runners.
Complete a legal tackle from an effective angle.
matchApplication: Defensive switches occur when opponents cross, overlap or change running lanes. Clear communication and role handover prevent attackers from becoming unmarked and allow the nearest balanced defender to pressure the football.

title: Moving Tackle Integration Assessment
primarySkill: Assessment of tackling technique during complex movement
objective: Assess whether players can maintain safe tackle technique while accelerating, changing direction, tracking possession, communicating and responding to moving attacking patterns.
groundSize: Five assessment stations occupying approximately one-third to one-half of an oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Construct five separate movement-based assessment stations.
Station 1 assesses acceleration, deceleration and tackle entry.
Station 2 assesses repeated change-of-direction pursuit.
Station 3 assesses pressure on an overlap or give-and-go receiver.
Station 4 assesses inside-out positioning and boundary funnel technique.
Station 5 assesses defensive switching across multiple moving lanes.
Assign a coach or trained observer to each station.
Divide players evenly and rotate every six to eight minutes.
Match players appropriately for contact activities.
Use the same scoring method at every station.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, the defender closes a large starting gap, decelerates and tackles a moving ball carrier.
The observer assesses speed control, balance, approach angle and safe contact.
At Station 2, the defender tracks an attacker through multiple directional gates before completing a tackle.
The observer assesses footwork, visual tracking and pursuit recovery.
At Station 3, defenders respond to an overlap or give-and-go handball pattern.
The observer assesses scanning, transfer of pressure and tackle timing.
At Station 4, the defender protects the corridor, forces the attacker outside and completes a boundary-side tackle.
The observer assesses positioning, patience and control.
At Station 5, defenders manage lane-crossing attackers and communicate defensive switches.
The observer assesses role clarity, communication and pressure on the correct ball carrier.
Each assessed behaviour receives:
2 points: Consistently demonstrated.
1 point: Inconsistent or demonstrated after correction.
0 points: Not demonstrated or performed unsafely.
Any unsafe contact stops the repetition immediately.
Coaches record one movement strength, one tackling priority and one recommended development drill for each player.
coachingPoints: Technique must remain stable while players move at increasing speed.
Defenders must decelerate before contact.
Pursuit angles should reach the opponent’s hip rather than the back.
Players should move while the football is travelling.
Defenders must recognise the most dangerous attacking option.
Communication should occur before switches and handovers.
Contact must remain below the shoulders and above the knees.
Head placement, two-arm wrapping and immediate release remain non-negotiable.
Fatigue must not be used to excuse poor or reckless technique.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether acceleration is converted into controlled deceleration.
Whether players maintain balance through changes of direction.
Whether pursuit lines reach safe contact positions.
Whether defenders scan multiple attacking threats.
Whether pressure transfers when possession changes.
Whether inside and dangerous space is protected.
Whether communication improves defensive coordination.
Whether tackle technique remains legal under physical and mental load.
Whether players release and rejoin play immediately.
Whether decision quality remains consistent across all stations.

commonErrors.error: Player runs quickly but cannot decelerate safely.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce starting speed and rebuild the final adjustment steps.

commonErrors.error: Defender loses balance after repeated direction changes.
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the turning steps and delay contact until balance is restored.

commonErrors.error: Player reacts after the receiver gains possession.
commonErrors.correction: Begin moving while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Defender chases the football and concedes central space.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the corridor and approach from inside.

commonErrors.error: Defenders fail to communicate during switches.
commonErrors.correction: Require an early and audible role call before the crossing movement.

commonErrors.error: Tackle technique deteriorates under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce work duration and restore head, shoulder and wrap standards.

commonErrors.error: Player completes the tackle but does not rejoin play.
commonErrors.correction: Add release and recovery to the assessment score.

progressions: Increase attacker speed only for players meeting all safety standards.
Allow attackers greater freedom to vary movement patterns.
Add kicks and handballs within the same station.
Introduce scoreboard consequences for team assessment.
Repeat the assessment under moderate football-specific fatigue.
regressions: Assess each movement component separately.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Predetermine attacking movements.
Reduce running distances and decision options.
Return players to TK-020 or TK-030 assessment standards before retesting.
successIndicators: Release and transition into the next defensive action.
matchApplication: This assessment measures whether players can apply safe tackling fundamentals within realistic moving patterns. Effective match defenders must combine pursuit, decision making, communication, space protection and repeat effort while preserving legal contact technique.

title: Live Evasion Tackle Contest
primarySkill: Completing a tackle against live evasion
objective: Develop the ability to remain balanced against unrestricted but controlled evasion and complete a legal tackle when the ball carrier enters a genuine contact window.
groundSize: Squares approximately 8 metres by 8 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark several 8-metre by 8-metre contest squares.
Place one attacker with a football and one defender inside each square.
Mark one scoring gate on each side of the square.
A third player acts as safety observer and timekeeper.
The attacker may use either scoring gate.
The defender begins approximately 3 metres away.
The contest is limited to six seconds.
All tackles remain upright during the introductory version.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the observer’s signal, the attacker attempts to evade the defender and carry the football through either scoring gate.
The defender closes space while tracking the attacker’s hips.
The attacker may change direction, pace or football position.
The defender must remain balanced and avoid lunging at the first movement.
When the attacker enters safe contact range, the defender completes a legal shoulder-and-wrap tackle.
The defender scores two points for a completed tackle.
The defender scores one point for containing the attacker for six seconds.
The attacker scores one point for crossing a gate under control.
If the tackle is missed, the defender must immediately recover and continue pressure.
Players exchange roles after each repetition.
Complete four to six repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Maintain a balanced stance while the attacker retains two movement options.
Watch the hips and trunk rather than the football.
Use short adjustment steps during changes of direction.
Commit only when the near foot can arrive close to the ball carrier.
Keep the head behind or safely beside the opponent.
Contact between the shoulders and knees.
Wrap both arms and control the ball carrier upright.
Recover immediately after a missed attempt.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender remains balanced through the attacker’s first movement.
Whether the defender protects the most dangerous gate.
Whether players recognise genuine tackle range.
Whether the final approach is controlled.
Whether head and shoulder placement remain safe.
Whether defenders produce an immediate second effort after a miss.

commonErrors.error: Defender lunges at the attacker’s first baulk.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain the reaction buffer and wait for the hips to commit.

commonErrors.error: Defender becomes flat-footed.
commonErrors.correction: Keep small adjustment steps active throughout the contest.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches from outside safe range.
commonErrors.correction: Continue closing until the near foot can land beside the opponent.

commonErrors.error: Defender makes high contact after being wrong-footed.
commonErrors.correction: Recover balance and lower through the hips before re-entering.

commonErrors.error: Player stops after a missed tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Turn immediately and continue the pressure effort.

progressions: Increase the contest area to allow greater attacking speed.
Permit the attacker to use a controlled fend-off.
Allow the tackle to continue to a safe ground finish for appropriately coached players.
Add a support attacker available for one handball.
regressions: Restrict the attacker to one change of direction.
Predetermine the scoring gate.
Use two-handed touch pressure.
Reduce the contest to walking or jogging speed.
successIndicators: Delay commitment until safe tackle range develops.
Control the opponent without lifting or slinging.
Recover immediately after an unsuccessful attempt.
matchApplication: Live ball carriers rarely move predictably. Defenders must manage uncertainty, protect space and recognise the correct moment to tackle rather than lunging at every baulk or change of pace.

title: Disposal Window Tackle
primarySkill: Tackling during an opponent’s disposal preparation
objective: Teach defenders to recognise when a ball carrier is preparing to kick or handball and use that moment to close, tackle legally and affect the disposal.
groundSize: Grids approximately 12 metres by 8 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a ball carrier in the centre of each grid.
Place a disposal target 8 metres away.
Position the defender 4 metres from the ball carrier.
A feeder stands behind the defender and signals either kick or handball.
The ball carrier begins stationary before progressing to light movement.
A fourth player acts as target and safety observer.
The defender may move once the ball carrier begins the disposal preparation.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder signals whether the ball carrier should prepare to kick or handball.
The ball carrier begins the appropriate disposal action.
As the football moves away from the protected carrying position, the defender closes space.
The defender targets the torso and disposal arm rather than reaching for the football.
The ball carrier attempts to complete the disposal to the target.
The defender attempts to secure a legal tackle and affect the disposal.
Two points are awarded for preventing the disposal.
One point is awarded for forcing an ineffective disposal.
The ball carrier scores one point for a clean disposal to the target.
Players rotate through all roles.
Complete repetitions against both kick and handball preparation.
coachingPoints: Observe the ball carrier’s hands, hips and disposal preparation.
Close decisively when the football becomes exposed.
Maintain balance and legal tackle height.
Target the opponent’s torso and disposal arm.
Avoid striking or grabbing directly at the football.
Keep the head safely to the side.
Wrap both arms where possible.
Continue pressure through the disposal without making late contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders recognise the disposal preparation.
Whether movement begins at the appropriate time.
Whether the defender arrives before or during release rather than after it.
Whether contact remains within the legal tackling zone.
Whether the disposal arm is controlled legally.
Whether defenders stop contact when the football has already been cleanly disposed.

commonErrors.error: Defender reacts only after the disposal is completed.
commonErrors.correction: Read the preparation and move as the football becomes exposed.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches directly for the football.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the body and disposal arm instead.

commonErrors.error: Defender makes late contact after the kick.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the pressure action once the football has been cleanly released.

commonErrors.error: Player arrives upright and high.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the hips and target the torso.

commonErrors.error: Tackler focuses on one disposal type only.
commonErrors.correction: Train recognition of both kick and handball preparation.

progressions: Allow the ball carrier to fake one disposal before selecting another.
Introduce movement before the disposal.
Add two possible disposal targets.
Allow the ball carrier to evade if the defender commits too early.
regressions: Predetermine the disposal type.
Reduce the defender’s starting distance.
Replace tackling with a controlled arm-and-torso touch.
Slow the disposal preparation.
successIndicators: Close as the football becomes exposed.
Target the body and disposal arm legally.
Affect the disposal without making late contact.
Maintain safe head position and balance.
Adjust to both kick and handball preparation.
matchApplication: Ball carriers often become more vulnerable while preparing to dispose. Defenders who recognise this moment can close before the disposal is completed, create holding-the-ball pressure or force an ineffective kick or handball.

title: Recovery-Line Chase Tackle
primarySkill: Recovering from a defensive disadvantage to tackle
objective: Develop the ability to recover from behind or outside the play, regain a useful defensive line and complete a controlled tackle without diving or making illegal rear contact.
groundSize: Corridors approximately 20 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central corridor and two outside lanes.
Position the attacker with a football near one end.
Place the defender 5 metres behind and outside the attacker’s line.
Mark a scoring gate at the far end.
A support target stands beyond the scoring gate.
A fourth player acts as observer.
The attacker works at approximately 65–70 per cent speed.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the attacker accelerates towards the scoring gate.
The defender begins from the disadvantaged outside position.
The defender sprints diagonally to regain an inside pursuit line.
The defender protects the corridor while closing towards the attacker’s near hip.
The attacker may change pace once.
The defender must reach the attacker’s side before attempting contact.
The tackler decelerates and completes a legal upright tackle.
The attacker attempts to dispose to the support target.
The defender scores two points for a tackle and one for forcing a wide or ineffective disposal.
Players rotate roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Sprint towards the inside recovery line rather than following directly behind.
Protect dangerous central space while closing.
Use early acceleration to reduce the disadvantage.
Read changes in the attacker’s speed.
Avoid desperate reaching or diving from behind.
Move beside the ball carrier before contact.
Decelerate and restore tackling shape.
Continue the effort even if the first tackle opportunity is unavailable.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender selects an effective recovery angle.
Whether inside space is protected.
Whether the defender closes without following directly behind.
Whether the final approach is controlled.
Whether contact occurs from the side.
Whether the defender maintains effort if the tackle cannot be completed immediately.

commonErrors.error: Defender chases directly behind the attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Run diagonally towards the inside hip and scoring line.

commonErrors.error: Player reaches or dives from distance.
commonErrors.correction: Continue running until a safe side-on position is established.

commonErrors.error: Defender recovers outside and concedes the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise inside position before closing fully.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives at maximum speed.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate over the final steps.

commonErrors.error: Defender gives up when the attacker changes pace.
commonErrors.correction: Reaccelerate and continue protecting the dangerous line.

progressions: Increase the attacker’s speed.
Allow the attacker one change of direction.
Add an overlap support runner.
Introduce a second recovering defender.
regressions: Reduce the starting disadvantage.
Predetermine the attacker’s running line.
Replace the tackle with a two-handed touch.
Shorten the corridor.
successIndicators: Avoid diving or illegal rear contact.
Complete a controlled tackle or force a poor disposal.
Maintain repeat effort throughout the chase.
matchApplication: Defenders are regularly caught outside or behind after turnovers. Effective recovery requires an intelligent angle, protection of the corridor and enough discipline to avoid desperate tackles into the back.

title: Front-and-Square Contest Tackle
primarySkill: Tackling the winner of an aerial contest
objective: Teach defenders to position front and square of an aerial contest, identify the player who gains possession and apply legal pressure once that player is safe to tackle.
groundSize: Contest areas approximately 15 metres by 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position two players for a controlled aerial contest.
Place one defender front and square approximately 3–4 metres from the contest.
Position a feeder 15 metres away.
Place two disposal targets outside the contest area.
A sixth player acts as observer and return feeder.
The aerial contest is controlled and players are not permitted to take high-risk marks.
The front-and-square defender may tackle only after possession is clearly established.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks a controlled football to the aerial contest.
The two contest players compete to mark or bring the football to ground.
The defender reads the ball flight and adjusts front-and-square position.
If a player marks, the defender respects the mark and establishes pressure.
If the football spills, the contest players attempt to collect and dispose to a target.
The defender identifies the player who gains possession.
The defender closes and tackles only after the ball winner reaches a safe contact position.
The defender scores two points for a legal tackle and one for forcing an ineffective disposal.
The possession winner scores one point for a clean disposal.
Players rotate through all roles.
coachingPoints: Maintain a front-and-square position relative to the contest.
Read the likely drop zone while preserving vision of both opponents.
Do not enter underneath airborne players.
Respect a completed mark.
Close immediately when a loose football is won.
Avoid contacting a player whose head remains over the football.
Target the torso and disposal arm once safe tackling height is reached.
React to possession rather than guessing the winner.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders maintain effective front-and-square position.
Whether players avoid entering the aerial contest dangerously.
Whether a completed mark is recognised.
Whether the possession winner is identified quickly.
Whether contact is delayed until safe.
Whether the tackle affects the first disposal after the contest.

commonErrors.error: Defender drifts behind the aerial contest.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish front-and-square position before the kick arrives.

commonErrors.error: Player enters underneath airborne opponents.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside the landing space and prepare for the spill.

commonErrors.error: Defender guesses the winner and commits early.
commonErrors.correction: Stay balanced until possession is clear.

commonErrors.error: Tackler contacts the collector while their head is down.
commonErrors.correction: Control the exit and wait for the player to rise.

commonErrors.error: Defender reacts slowly to a clean possession win.
commonErrors.correction: Close immediately once the ball winner is identified.

progressions: Allow the contest players to tap the football deliberately.
Add a second front-and-square defender.
Introduce an attacking support runner.
Continue play after the first disposal.
regressions: Use a coach-directed football spill rather than an aerial contest.
Predetermine which player wins possession.
Replace tackling with two-handed touch pressure.
Reduce the size and speed of the contest.
successIndicators: Remain clear of unsafe aerial contact.
Respect marks and vulnerable collection positions.
Close quickly once tackling is legal.
Affect the first disposal after the contest.
matchApplication: Many tackles occur immediately after marking contests when the football spills or a player gathers at ground level. Front-and-square defenders can pressure the first possession without creating dangerous contact underneath the contest.
relatedDrills: TK-036 – Loose-Ball Win to Moving Tackle

title: Tackle-Induced Spill Transition
primarySkill: Transitioning after a tackle creates a loose football
objective: Develop the ability to complete a tackle, recognise an induced spill and organise the immediate contest for the loose football.
groundSize: Grids approximately 12 metres by 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Place one attacker with a football and one defender in the centre.
Position one supporting attacker and one supporting defender outside the central contest.
Place two disposal targets on opposite sides.
A feeder and observer stand outside the grid.
The central tackle remains upright.
The coach may call “retain” or “spill” once contact is established.
Supporting players may enter only after the call.
howTheDrillWorks:
The central attacker moves across the grid with the football.
The central defender closes and completes a legal tackle.
The coach calls “retain” or “spill”.
On “retain”, the attacker attempts a controlled disposal while the tackle continues.
On “spill”, the attacker releases the football into nearby space.
The tackler immediately releases the opponent.
Both supporting players enter and compete for the loose football.
The tackler regains balance and communicates whether to pressure, protect or support.
The team winning possession attempts to dispose to its target.
The repetition ends after a clean target disposal or turnover.
Players rotate through all roles.
coachingPoints: Complete the initial tackle legally before reacting to the call.
Release immediately when the football spills.
Keep vision on the football and nearby support players.
Communicate who attacks the loose football.
Avoid multiple defenders collapsing on the same ground ball.
Protect the outside release option.
Regain balance quickly after contact.
Transition from tackler to support defender without delay.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the initial tackle is controlled.
Whether the tackler releases immediately after the spill.
Whether supporting players enter at the correct time.
Whether defenders communicate roles.
Whether the tackler regains a useful position.
Whether the loose-ball contest remains safe and organised.

commonErrors.error: Tackler continues holding after the spill.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and redirect towards the next contest.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders attack the loose football.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate one ball player and one support-space defender.

commonErrors.error: Tackler remains behind the original opponent.
commonErrors.correction: Regain the feet and scan for the next threat.

commonErrors.error: Support players enter before the call.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside until possession becomes loose.

commonErrors.error: Players dive recklessly at the spill.
commonErrors.correction: Approach with controlled body position and protect the head.

progressions: Remove the coach’s call and allow the spill to occur naturally.
Add a second supporting player for each team.
Continue play for a second disposal.
Permit the original attacker to rejoin after release.
regressions: Predetermine every repetition as a spill.
Place the football on the ground after the tackle.
Use a tackle bag for the initial contact.
Allow only one supporting player to enter.
successIndicators: Regain balance and rejoin the contest.
Protect both the football and likely outlet.
matchApplication: A strong tackle often creates a spill rather than an immediate stoppage. Teams must react quickly, release legally and organise the next contest to turn pressure into possession.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat
TK-029 – Tackle, Regain Feet and Rejoin
TK-036 – Loose-Ball Win to Moving Tackle

title: Congestion Gate Tackle
primarySkill: Completing a tackle through congested space
objective: Teach defenders to navigate congested space, identify a safe tackle line and apply controlled contact without colliding with nearby players.
groundSize: Grids approximately 14 metres by 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark three narrow movement gates inside the grid.
Place one ball carrier at one end and one defender at the opposite end.
Position four neutral players inside the grid.
Neutral players move along assigned short paths and provide realistic traffic without deliberate blocking.
Mark a scoring gate beyond the traffic.
A feeder begins the repetition with a handball to the attacker.
A safety observer controls player spacing.
howTheDrillWorks:
Neutral players begin moving inside the grid.
The feeder handballs to the attacker.
The attacker selects a route through one of the internal gates.
The defender scans the traffic and selects a safe pursuit route.
The defender communicates when moving close to neutral players.
The defender must avoid tackling through the back of a neutral player or entering a closing gap.
Once a clear angle develops, the defender closes on the attacker’s torso.
The defender completes a legal controlled tackle before the scoring gate.
The attacker scores one point for crossing the gate.
The defender scores two points for a tackle and one for forcing a retreat or turnover.
Players rotate through active and neutral roles.
coachingPoints: Keep the eyes up and scan beyond the nearest body.
Maintain awareness of the ball carrier’s hips.
Choose the safest effective route rather than the shortest blocked route.
Communicate through congestion.
Rebalance after moving around traffic.
Avoid launching through gaps that are closing.
Enter contact only with clear access to the legal tackle zone.
Stop immediately if another player enters the contact line.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders scan both traffic and attacker.
Whether pursuit routes remain safe.
Whether communication occurs.
Whether players avoid blind contact.
Whether balance is restored before tackling.
Whether the ball carrier is pressured before the scoring gate.

commonErrors.error: Defender looks only at the nearest neutral player.
commonErrors.correction: Scan beyond the traffic and relocate the ball carrier continuously.

commonErrors.error: Player forces through a closing gap.
commonErrors.correction: Take the next clear route rather than risking collision.

commonErrors.error: Defender tackles without rebalancing.
commonErrors.correction: Use adjustment steps after clearing traffic.

commonErrors.error: Player approaches blindly from behind another player.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally until the legal tackle zone is visible.

commonErrors.error: Neutral players deliberately block.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce that their role is moving traffic, not screening.

progressions: Allow neutral players to change direction on command.
Add a support attacker.
Add a second defender.
Continue play after the first disposal.
regressions: Replace neutral players with stationary cones.
Predetermine the attacker’s route.
Use a two-handed touch.
Reduce the number of traffic players.
successIndicators: Complete a legal tackle from a clear angle.
matchApplication: Congested tackles occur around stoppages, packs and ground-ball contests. Defenders must navigate bodies safely and resist the temptation to launch blindly at the football.

title: Broken-Tackle Support Defender
primarySkill: Supporting a teammate after a tackle is broken
objective: Develop coordinated support in which a second defender recognises a broken tackle, protects the dangerous exit and completes the next legal pressure action.
groundSize: Grids approximately 14 metres by 10 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position an attacker with a football in the centre of the grid.
Place the first defender 3 metres in front.
Position the support defender 5 metres behind and to one side.
Mark two exit gates beyond the first defender.
A feeder and observer stand outside the grid.
The first defender begins with a controlled tackle attempt designed to be breakable.
The support defender must react to the outcome rather than pre-empting it.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder starts the attacker with a handball.
The first defender closes and attempts a controlled tackle.
The attacker is permitted to break the tackle using movement rather than excessive force.
The support defender scans the contest and protects the most dangerous exit.
Once the first tackle is broken, the support defender becomes the primary tackler.
The first defender immediately recovers and protects the secondary exit.
The support defender closes and completes a legal tackle or forces a disposal.
The attacker scores by crossing an exit gate.
Defenders score two points for a completed second tackle and one for forcing a turnover.
Players rotate through attacker, first defender, support defender, feeder and observer roles.
coachingPoints: The support defender must remain connected without crowding the first tackle.
Protect the dangerous exit before attacking the ball carrier.
React when the first tackle is genuinely broken.
Communicate the role change.
The first defender must recover immediately.
Approach from a complementary angle.
Avoid simultaneous uncontrolled contact.
Finish the second tackle with safe head and arm position.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the support defender maintains useful distance.
Whether the dangerous exit is protected.
Whether the support defender reacts at the correct moment.
Whether the first defender recovers.
Whether defenders avoid converging from the same angle.
Whether the second tackle remains controlled.

commonErrors.error: Support defender joins the first tackle unnecessarily.
commonErrors.correction: Hold supporting position until the tackle is broken.

commonErrors.error: Defender watches the contest and leaves the exit open.
commonErrors.correction: Protect dangerous space while remaining ready to react.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders chase from behind after the break.
commonErrors.correction: Recover to complementary inside and outside angles.

commonErrors.error: First defender stops after being beaten.
commonErrors.correction: Turn immediately and protect the secondary exit.

commonErrors.error: Second defender arrives too quickly.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate before contact and restore tackle shape.

progressions: Allow the attacker to handball after breaking the first tackle.
Add an attacking support runner.
Remove the predetermined broken-tackle outcome.
Continue play after the second pressure action.
regressions: Use two-handed touch for the first attempt.
Predetermine the attacker’s exit.
Reduce the support defender’s starting distance.
Walk through the role exchange before live repetitions.
successIndicators: Recognise when the first tackle is broken.
matchApplication: Broken tackles create dangerous line-breaking opportunities. Effective defensive support ensures that one failed tackle does not remove the entire defensive line from the contest.

title: Two-versus-Two Pressure Chain
primarySkill: Maintaining connected pressure in a two-versus-two contest
objective: Develop coordinated two-player pressure in which defenders protect space, transfer responsibility and tackle the correct ball carrier across multiple possession changes.
groundSize: Grids approximately 14 metres by 12 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Place two attackers and two defenders inside each grid.
Position one feeder outside the grid.
Mark two attacking scoring gates.
Attackers may use handball only.
Defenders begin between the attackers and scoring gates.
A sixth player acts as observer and return feeder.
Contests last a maximum of eight seconds.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder handballs to either attacker.
The nearest balanced defender closes the ball carrier.
The second defender protects the support attacker and dangerous scoring space.
Attackers may carry, evade or exchange handballs.
Defenders communicate each transfer of pressure.
The ball defender may tackle when safe contact range develops.
The support defender may assist only after the first tackle is established.
Attackers score by carrying the football through a gate.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one for containing the attack for eight seconds.
Players rotate after each contest.
coachingPoints: Identify the nearest balanced pressure defender.
The second defender protects space and support options.
Communicate every change of ball carrier.
Move during the handball rather than after the receive.
Avoid both defenders chasing the football.
Support tackles from a safe complementary angle.
Release immediately when possession transfers.
Continue pressure after spills and incomplete disposals.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders establish clear roles.
Whether support space remains protected.
Whether pressure transfers quickly after handballs.
Whether defenders maintain useful separation.
Whether tackles are supported safely.
Whether defenders react immediately to loose footballs.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders chase the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one pressure defender and one support defender.

commonErrors.error: Support attacker becomes free after a handball.
commonErrors.correction: Move during the disposal and communicate the transfer.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stand too close together.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain spacing that covers both attackers.

commonErrors.error: Supporting defender crashes into the tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Arrive under control and secure space or a free arm only.

commonErrors.error: Defenders relax after an incomplete disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue pressure until possession is clearly secured or play stops.

progressions: Permit short kicks.
Add a third attacker and defender.
Remove the time limit.
Continue immediately into transition after a turnover.
regressions: Predetermine the first receiver.
Require attackers to complete only one handball.
Use two-handed touch pressure.
Increase the grid size.
successIndicators: Protect both the ball carrier and support threat.
React quickly to turnovers and spills.
matchApplication: Most match pressure is created by connected defenders rather than isolated tacklers. Two defenders who communicate and protect complementary space can prevent handball exits and create repeat tackle opportunities.

title: Small-Space Pressure Game
primarySkill: Applying tackle pressure in a small-sided contest
objective: Develop collective pressure behaviours in a constrained game where players must decide when to tackle, corral, support or protect the next disposal option.
groundSize: Grids approximately 20 metres by 16 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into teams of four to six.
Mark one scoring gate at each end.
Begin with one football in the centre.
Players may use handball or short kicks.
A team scores by carrying the football through its attacking gate.
Tackles remain controlled and players are not taken forcefully to ground.
The coach restarts play after unsafe contact, a clear stoppage or a score.
Rotate substitute players every two to three minutes where required.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the football into the centre.
Teams compete for possession.
The defending team applies live pressure while protecting its scoring gate.
The nearest balanced defender pressures the ball carrier.
Teammates protect receivers, exits and central space.
Legal tackles are permitted when safe contact range develops.
A completed tackle that prevents disposal creates an immediate turnover to the defending team.
A loose football remains live.
Teams score one point by carrying through the attacking gate.
Award a bonus point for a score created within ten seconds of a tackle or turnover.
Play in blocks of two to four minutes with coaching between blocks.
coachingPoints: The nearest balanced defender applies pressure.
Supporting defenders protect dangerous space and receivers.
Communicate whether to tackle, corral, switch or support.
Move while the football is travelling.
Avoid overcommitting unnecessary numbers to one tackle.
Release immediately after possession changes.
React quickly to spills and turnovers.
Preserve legal tackle height and safe head placement under fatigue.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders identify clear pressure roles.
Whether dangerous central space is protected.
Whether players recognise tackle and corral situations.
Whether pressure transfers after disposals.
Whether defenders avoid crowding the football.
Whether turnovers produce immediate attacking movement.
Whether contact technique remains safe under game pressure.

commonErrors.error: Every defender follows the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain team spacing and protect the next receiver.

commonErrors.error: Players lunge from outside tackle range.
commonErrors.correction: Corral until the near foot can arrive close.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop after the ball is disposed.
commonErrors.correction: Transfer pressure immediately to the next possession.

commonErrors.error: Too many defenders join one tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one tackler and use others to protect exits.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes high under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce work duration and reinforce lower body position.

commonErrors.error: Team wins a turnover but remains stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Spread and attack immediately after possession changes.

progressions: Reduce the grid size.
Introduce a maximum possession time.
Award extra points for consecutive pressure acts.
Allow full match-like ground finishes for appropriately coached players.
Add directional zones that must be defended.
regressions: Increase the grid size.
Use two-handed touch instead of tackling.
Limit attackers to handball only.
Pause after each turnover to reset defensive shape.
successIndicators: Select appropriate tackle or corral actions.
Maintain safe technique under game demands.
Convert defensive pressure into attacking possession.
matchApplication: The game links individual tackling technique with team defence. Players must recognise that effective pressure includes tackling, containing, covering receivers, forcing poor disposals and reacting immediately to turnovers.

title: Pressure and Contest Assessment
primarySkill: Assessment of tackling under live pressure and contest conditions
objective: Assess whether players can maintain safe tackling technique, make effective pressure decisions and remain connected defensively in live contest situations.
groundSize: Five stations occupying approximately one-third to one-half of an oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Construct five separate assessment stations.
Station 1 assesses live evasion and tackle timing.
Station 2 assesses disposal-window pressure.
Station 3 assesses recovery-line chase tackling.
Station 4 assesses contest positioning and reaction to a possession win.
Station 5 assesses connected pressure in a two-versus-two or small-sided game.
Assign a coach or trained observer to every station.
Divide players evenly and rotate every six to eight minutes.
Match players appropriately for contact activities.
Use a consistent scoring system at every station.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, the defender contains a live evasive attacker and tackles when a safe opportunity develops.
The observer assesses balance, patience, tackle timing and recovery effort.
At Station 2, the defender recognises kick or handball preparation and attempts to affect the disposal legally.
The observer assesses recognition, closing speed, arm control and late-contact discipline.
At Station 3, the defender begins from a disadvantaged recovery position and protects the corridor before tackling.
The observer assesses recovery angle, work rate and safe side-on entry.
At Station 4, the defender positions front and square of a contest and pressures the player who wins possession.
The observer assesses contest awareness, player protection and first-disposal pressure.
At Station 5, defenders work together in a two-versus-two or small-sided pressure contest.
The observer assesses communication, role clarity, space protection and turnover reaction.
Each behaviour receives:
2 points: Consistently demonstrated.
1 point: Demonstrated inconsistently or after correction.
0 points: Not demonstrated or performed unsafely.
Any unsafe contact immediately stops the repetition.
Coaches record one technical strength, one pressure-decision priority and one recommended development drill for each player.
coachingPoints: Safe technique remains the first assessment standard.
Players must tackle from balance rather than desperation.
Defenders should recognise when to tackle and when to corral.
Contact must remain below the shoulders and above the knees.
Players must protect opponents who are airborne or bent over the football.
Head placement and two-arm wrapping remain non-negotiable.
Defenders must release immediately when possession changes.
Communication and defensive spacing are assessed alongside individual tackling.
Players must react to spills, broken tackles and turnovers.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players remain balanced against live evasion.
Whether tackle opportunities are recognised accurately.
Whether disposal preparation is read early.
Whether recovery angles protect the corridor.
Whether vulnerable players are protected around contests.
Whether tackle height and head position remain safe.
Whether defenders communicate and support one another.
Whether pressure transfers after disposals.
Whether players react immediately to spills and turnovers.
Whether technique remains stable under fatigue and decision pressure.

commonErrors.error: Player lunges at every evasive movement.
commonErrors.correction: Corral until the attacker enters genuine tackle range.

commonErrors.error: Defender reacts after the disposal is completed.
commonErrors.correction: Read the preparation and close as the football becomes exposed.

commonErrors.error: Player recovers directly behind the attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Use an inside pursuit angle and reach the hip line.

commonErrors.error: Defender contacts an opponent in a vulnerable position.
commonErrors.correction: Control space and delay contact until safe tackling height.

commonErrors.error: Defenders crowd the ball carrier and leave receivers free.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate clear pressure and support roles.

commonErrors.error: Tackle technique deteriorates late in the circuit.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce work duration and restore technical standards before continuing.

commonErrors.error: Player completes contact but fails to react to the next phase.
commonErrors.correction: Include release, scan and recovery in the assessment score.

progressions: Increase attacker freedom and speed for players meeting all safety standards.
Introduce full match-like disposals and transitions.
Add scoreboard and time-pressure consequences.
Repeat the assessment under moderate football-specific fatigue.
Compare individual and team scores across the training cycle.
regressions: Assess each station separately.
Replace live tackles with two-handed touch pressure.
Predetermine attacking movements.
Reduce player numbers and decision options.
Return players to TK-020, TK-030 or TK-040 before reassessment.
successIndicators: Complete legal contact with safe head placement.
Communicate and maintain connected team pressure.
React to spills, broken tackles and turnovers.
Preserve technical quality under physical and mental load.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether players can transfer tackling technique into genuine contest situations. Effective match pressure requires safe contact, intelligent decisions, defensive support, recovery effort and immediate reaction to the next phase.

title: Contact-to-Corral Transition
primarySkill: Transitioning from failed contact into containment
objective: Develop the ability to recover from incomplete tackle contact and immediately corral the ball carrier rather than making a second reckless attempt.
groundSize: Squares approximately 9 metres by 9 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark several 9-metre by 9-metre contest squares.
Position one attacker with a football and one defender inside each square.
Mark one central scoring gate and two lower-value wide gates.
A third player acts as observer and timekeeper.
The defender begins approximately 2 metres from the attacker.
The initial contact is deliberately limited to a controlled shoulder touch and partial wrap.
The attacker is allowed to separate and continue moving.
The contest lasts a maximum of seven seconds.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the observer’s signal, the attacker moves towards any scoring gate.
The defender closes and makes controlled partial contact without fully securing the tackle.
The attacker breaks away and continues moving.
The defender must recover balance immediately.
Rather than lunging again, the defender repositions between the attacker and the central gate.
The defender corrals the ball carrier and reduces the available space.
A second legal tackle may be attempted only when the defender has regained balance and safe contact range.
The defender scores two points for a completed second tackle.
The defender scores one point for forcing a wide exit or containing the attacker for seven seconds.
The attacker scores two points for crossing the central gate and one point for a wide gate.
Players exchange roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Recover the feet immediately after incomplete contact.
Avoid grabbing as the attacker separates.
Re-establish position between the ball carrier and dangerous space.
Use short adjustment steps to regain balance.
Corral when a second safe tackle opportunity is not immediately available.
Watch the attacker’s hips rather than reaching for the football.
Attempt the second tackle only when the near foot can arrive close.
Maintain legal tackle height and safe head position.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders remain upright after incomplete contact.
Whether players avoid desperate grabbing.
Whether central space is protected.
Whether defenders transition into balanced containment.
Whether the second tackle is attempted from safe range.
Whether defenders maintain effort without becoming reckless.

commonErrors.error: Defender reaches while the attacker separates.
commonErrors.correction: Release fully, recover the feet and regain defensive position.

commonErrors.error: Player attempts an immediate second lunge.
commonErrors.correction: Corral until balance and safe contact distance are restored.

commonErrors.error: Defender chases from directly behind.
commonErrors.correction: Recover towards the inside hip and central scoring line.

commonErrors.error: Player becomes passive after the broken contact.
commonErrors.correction: Continue reducing space with active footwork.

commonErrors.error: Second tackle becomes high.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the hips before re-entering contact.

progressions: Allow the attacker to use a controlled fend-off during separation.
Remove the predetermined incomplete-contact requirement.
Add a support attacker outside the square.
Require the defender to communicate the recovery action.
regressions: Replace the first contact with a two-handed touch.
Predetermine the attacker’s escape gate.
Reduce the attacker to jogging speed.
Increase the size of the contest square.
successIndicators: Recognise when safe tackle range returns.
matchApplication: Tackles are often partially broken without completely removing the defender from the contest. Players who recover into containment can prevent further penetration and create another tackle opportunity without conceding a free kick through desperate contact.

title: Boundary Repeat-Pressure Contest
primarySkill: Applying repeated pressure along the boundary
objective: Develop the ability to maintain inside position and produce consecutive pressure efforts as a ball carrier attempts to advance along the boundary.
groundSize: Boundary channels approximately 20 metres long and 7 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Use an existing boundary line or mark one side of each channel as the boundary.
Place the attacker with a football at one end.
Position the defender 4 metres in front and slightly inside.
Mark three five-metre pressure zones along the channel.
Place a receiver beyond the finishing line.
A fourth player acts as observer and reset feeder.
The attacker must remain inside the channel.
The defender must preserve inside position throughout the repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker begins moving along the boundary channel.
The defender closes from the inside and corrals towards the boundary.
In the first pressure zone, the defender attempts a controlled two-handed pressure touch.
The attacker continues into the second zone.
The defender recovers inside position and applies another pressure effort.
In the final zone, the defender may complete a legal upright tackle.
If the attacker disposes to the receiver, the defender must pressure the disposal without making late contact.
The defender scores one point for each effective pressure action and two points for a completed tackle.
The attacker scores one point for reaching the receiver with clean possession.
Players rotate through attacker, defender, receiver and observer roles.
coachingPoints: Maintain inside position throughout the entire channel.
Use the boundary to reduce attacking space.
Recover immediately after each pressure action.
Avoid crossing behind the ball carrier and conceding the corridor.
Apply pressure without forcing uncontrolled contact near the line.
Shorten the final steps before every contest.
Recognise when to corral and when to tackle.
Stop contact immediately after a clean disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender remains between the attacker and central space.
Whether each pressure effort is followed by immediate recovery.
Whether the attacker is directed towards the boundary.
Whether the defender avoids over-running the ball carrier.
Whether the final tackle occurs from balance.
Whether late contact after disposal is avoided.

commonErrors.error: Defender crosses to the boundary side.
commonErrors.correction: Recover inside immediately and continue showing the line.

commonErrors.error: Player stops after the first pressure effort.
commonErrors.correction: Reaccelerate and prepare for the next zone.

commonErrors.error: Defender lunges near the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Corral and shorten the final steps before contact.

commonErrors.error: Tackler drives the opponent across the line.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the tackle and stop force once control is established.

commonErrors.error: Defender contacts after a clean disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Pull out of contact once the football is released.

progressions: Allow the attacker one change of direction towards the inside.
Add an attacking support runner inside the channel.
Remove the marked pressure zones.
Add a second defender entering for the final phase.
regressions: Predetermine the attacker’s running speed.
Use pressure touches only.
Shorten the channel.
Allow a brief reset between pressure zones.
successIndicators: Funnel the attacker towards the boundary.
Avoid unnecessary late or boundary contact.
matchApplication: Boundary defence often requires several efforts rather than one tackle attempt. Defenders must repeatedly recover inside position, reduce space and remain disciplined until a genuine tackle opportunity develops.
relatedDrills: TK-029 – Tackle, Regain Feet and Rejoin

title: Rear-Quarter Awareness Tackle
primarySkill: Closing safely from the rear quarter
objective: Teach defenders to approach from an opponent’s rear quarter, move into the ball carrier’s peripheral vision and complete a controlled side-on tackle without dangerous contact into the back.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 14 metres long and 5 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark several straight lanes.
Place the attacker at one end with a football.
Position the defender 3 metres behind and approximately 2 metres to one side.
Mark a contact zone in the final 6 metres.
A third player acts as observer.
The attacker runs at approximately 60 per cent speed.
The attacker may glance over either shoulder but must remain in the lane.
The defender must move to the side before contact.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the coach’s signal, the attacker accelerates through the lane.
The defender pursues from the rear-quarter starting position.
The defender closes towards the attacker’s outside hip.
Before contact, the defender moves far enough beside the attacker to become visible in peripheral vision.
The defender matches speed and shortens the final steps.
The tackler places the head behind or beside the ball carrier.
The near shoulder contacts inside the legal tackling zone.
Both arms wrap and control the ball carrier upright.
The coach calls “release” after one or two steps.
Players rotate roles and repeat from both rear-quarter sides.
coachingPoints: Pursue the outside hip rather than the centre of the back.
Move beside the opponent before initiating contact.
Reduce the speed difference before tackling.
Avoid placing force through the spine.
Keep the head behind the opponent’s near shoulder.
Wrap both arms rather than reaching around the neck or shoulder.
Maintain contact above the knees.
Travel with the opponent and release promptly.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders pursue the hip rather than the spine.
Whether the tackler moves beside the opponent before contact.
Whether the speed difference is reduced.
Whether head placement remains safe.
Whether contact stays within the legal zone.
Whether the attacker remains upright and controlled.

commonErrors.error: Defender drives directly into the opponent’s back.
commonErrors.correction: Move towards the outside hip and reach the side before contact.

commonErrors.error: Tackler reaches over the shoulder.
commonErrors.correction: Close further and complete a legal torso wrap.

commonErrors.error: Defender arrives with excessive speed.
commonErrors.correction: Match the attacker’s pace before entering contact.

commonErrors.error: Player clips the opponent’s legs.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the tackle target above the knees.

commonErrors.error: Tackler pulls the opponent backwards.
commonErrors.correction: Travel in the same direction and maintain upright control.

progressions: Increase the attacker’s speed.
Allow the attacker one controlled change of pace.
Permit a handball attempt during contact.
Add a nearby support receiver.
regressions: Begin the defender level with the attacker’s hip.
Reduce both players to jogging speed.
Use a moving tackle bag.
Predetermine the tackle side.
successIndicators: Move into a genuine side-on contact position.
matchApplication: Defenders frequently close from behind after transition or an opponent’s breakaway. Safe rear-quarter technique prevents dangerous tackles into the back while still allowing the defender to pressure or stop the ball carrier.

title: Stoppage Exit Pressure
primarySkill: Pressuring the first possession exiting a stoppage
objective: Develop the ability to identify the first ball carrier leaving a stoppage, close the exit lane and apply immediate legal pressure before clean possession can develop.
groundSize: Stoppage circles approximately 8 metres in diameter with a surrounding 15-metre exit area.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central stoppage circle.
Position two inside attackers and two inside defenders around the football.
Place one outside receiver and one outside defender on opposite sides.
A coach stands in the centre with the football.
Mark two exit gates 8 metres from the stoppage.
The coach releases the football by a controlled throw-up or ground roll.
Contact around the initial ball contest remains limited and safe.
Full tackling begins only after a player gains possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the football into the stoppage.
Inside players compete for possession using controlled bodywork.
Once an attacker gains the football, they attempt to exit through either gate or handball to the outside receiver.
The nearest balanced defender closes the ball carrier.
Other defenders protect the exit gates and outside receiver.
A legal tackle may be completed once possession is established.
If the football is handballed outside, the outside defender applies immediate pressure.
Attackers score one point for a controlled exit.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one for forcing a rushed disposal.
Reset the stoppage after each outcome.
Rotate inside and outside roles regularly.
coachingPoints: Begin in a position that allows vision of the football and opponent.
React immediately when possession becomes clear.
The nearest balanced defender pressures the ball carrier.
Supporting defenders protect likely exits.
Avoid diving blindly into the stoppage.
Maintain legal tackle height as the ball carrier rises from congestion.
Communicate whether pressure is inside or outside.
Release and react immediately if the football spills.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders identify the possession winner quickly.
Whether the nearest balanced player applies pressure.
Whether exit gates are protected.
Whether defenders avoid unsafe contact in the initial contest.
Whether tackle timing adjusts to the ball carrier’s body height.
Whether outside receivers are pressured immediately.

commonErrors.error: Defenders watch only the football and lose opponents.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain vision and touch awareness of the direct opponent.

commonErrors.error: Multiple defenders collapse on the first possession.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one ball defender and protect exits with the others.

commonErrors.error: Tackler contacts while the ball carrier’s head is down.
commonErrors.correction: Control the exit and wait until safe tackling height develops.

commonErrors.error: Outside defender reacts after the receiver has accelerated.
commonErrors.correction: Move as soon as the handball is released.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop after a spill.
commonErrors.correction: Release and continue competing for the next possession.

progressions: Add another outside receiver.
Allow either team to transition after a turnover.
Remove the predetermined exit gates.
Introduce a ruck tap rather than a coach release.
regressions: Predetermine which attacker wins possession.
Use handball receives rather than a live stoppage.
Replace tackles with pressure touches.
Reduce the number of inside players.
successIndicators: Transfer pressure to the outside receiver.
matchApplication: Stoppages are often decided by the pressure applied to the first possession. Even when the opposition wins the football, coordinated closing pressure can prevent a clean exit and create a secondary contest.

title: Congestion Escape Tackle
primarySkill: Tackling a ball carrier escaping congestion
objective: Teach defenders to identify the direction of a ball carrier escaping congestion and complete a controlled tackle after the player clears the most dangerous traffic.
groundSize: Grids approximately 14 metres by 14 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central congestion zone approximately 5 metres by 5 metres.
Position one attacker with a football inside the zone.
Place two neutral traffic players nearby.
Position one defender outside the zone.
Mark three exit gates around the outer grid.
A feeder and safety observer stand outside.
Neutral players move slowly and do not deliberately block.
The attacker may escape through any gate.
The defender may not enter the congestion zone recklessly.
howTheDrillWorks:
Neutral players begin moving inside the congestion zone.
The attacker carries the football and searches for an exit.
The defender scans from outside the zone and adjusts to protect dangerous space.
When the attacker commits to an exit, the defender moves towards the likely escape line.
The defender avoids colliding with neutral players.
Once the attacker clears the congestion, the defender decelerates into legal tackle range.
The defender completes a controlled shoulder-and-wrap tackle or forces a rushed disposal.
The attacker scores one point for escaping through a gate.
The defender scores two points for a tackle and one for forcing the attacker back into congestion.
Players rotate through attacker, defender, traffic and observer roles.
coachingPoints: Scan the attacker’s hips and available exit gates.
Protect the most dangerous central or forward exit.
Avoid charging blindly into congestion.
Anticipate the likely escape line.
Move as the attacker commits rather than guessing too early.
Rebalance after navigating traffic.
Complete the tackle after a clear legal contact line develops.
Remain active if the attacker retreats into congestion.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders scan available exits.
Whether the most dangerous gate is protected.
Whether defenders avoid blind entry into congestion.
Whether movement begins when the attacker commits.
Whether a clear contact line is established.
Whether pressure continues if the attacker retreats.

commonErrors.error: Defender enters congestion without a clear path.
commonErrors.correction: Hold outside and protect the likely exit.

commonErrors.error: Player guesses an exit too early.
commonErrors.correction: Remain balanced until the attacker’s hips commit.

commonErrors.error: Defender waits until the attacker is fully clear.
commonErrors.correction: Move as the escape line becomes apparent.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives off balance after avoiding traffic.
commonErrors.correction: Use adjustment steps before contact.

commonErrors.error: Defender stops when the attacker retreats.
commonErrors.correction: Continue containing and reduce the next exit option.

progressions: Increase the speed of neutral traffic.
Add a support attacker outside the congestion.
Add a second defender.
Allow the attacker to handball from inside the zone.
regressions: Predetermine the attacker’s exit.
Replace neutral players with cones.
Use pressure touches rather than tackling.
Reduce the number of exit gates.
successIndicators: Complete a legal tackle or force retreat.
matchApplication: Ball carriers often emerge unexpectedly from packs and stoppages. Defenders must recognise the exit line, remain clear of unsafe traffic and be ready to tackle as soon as a legal contact opportunity appears.

title: Kick-Under-Contact Pressure
primarySkill: Affecting a kick through legal tackle pressure
objective: Develop the ability to pressure a player preparing to kick while avoiding dangerous contact with the kicking leg and preventing late contact after disposal.
groundSize: Grids approximately 15 metres long and 8 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a ball carrier 10 metres from a kick target.
Place the defender 4 metres to the side and slightly behind.
A feeder starts the ball carrier with a handball.
A fourth player acts as target and safety observer.
The ball carrier must take two or three steps before kicking.
The defender may move once the handball is released.
The defender must avoid contact with the extended kicking leg.
Kicks are performed at controlled intensity.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder handballs to the ball carrier.
The ball carrier gathers and prepares to kick to the target.
The defender closes while the football is received.
The defender approaches the torso from the non-kicking or rear-quarter side.
If the defender arrives before the kicking action is committed, a legal tackle may be completed.
If the kicking leg is already extended, the defender must avoid dangerous contact and instead apply legal upper-body pressure where safe.
The defender stops all contact once the kick is completed.
The defender scores two points for preventing the kick and one for forcing an ineffective kick.
The attacker scores one point for hitting the target.
Players rotate through all roles.
coachingPoints: Read the ball carrier’s kicking preparation.
Close early enough to tackle before the kicking action becomes exposed.
Avoid contact with the extended kicking leg.
Target the torso and arms rather than the football or leg.
Maintain safe head position.
Do not push or tackle after the kick has been completed.
Decelerate when arriving late.
Value pressure on the kick even when a tackle is no longer safe.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders recognise the kicking preparation.
Whether players arrive before or after leg extension.
Whether the kicking leg is protected.
Whether contact targets the torso legally.
Whether defenders avoid late force.
Whether the kick is affected through legitimate pressure.

commonErrors.error: Defender dives towards the football or kicking leg.
commonErrors.correction: Target the torso and maintain body control.

commonErrors.error: Tackler contacts after the kick.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the pressure action once disposal is completed.

commonErrors.error: Defender arrives upright and high.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the hips before legal torso contact.

commonErrors.error: Player gives up when a tackle is no longer safe.
commonErrors.correction: Continue with balanced pressure that affects the kick.

commonErrors.error: Defender approaches directly across the kicking leg.
commonErrors.correction: Close from the non-kicking or rear-quarter side.

progressions: Allow the ball carrier to choose between kick and handball.
Add two kick targets.
Increase the ball carrier’s movement speed.
Add an overlap receiver.
regressions: Predetermine the kicking side.
Reduce the defender’s starting distance.
Use a pressure touch rather than a tackle.
Slow the kicking preparation.
successIndicators: Affect the kick without making late contact.
Adjust when a full tackle is no longer available.
matchApplication: Pressure on kicks is essential, but defenders must avoid contacting an exposed kicking leg or arriving late after disposal. Safe pressure can still force a poor kick without requiring a completed tackle.

title: Smother-or-Tackle Decision
primarySkill: Selecting between smother pressure and tackling
objective: Teach defenders to decide whether a ball carrier remains safely tackleable or whether a controlled smother pressure action is the more appropriate defensive response.
groundSize: Grids approximately 12 metres by 8 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position the ball carrier in the centre of the grid.
Place the defender 4 metres away.
Position a disposal target 8–10 metres beyond the ball carrier.
A feeder stands behind the defender.
The feeder signals the ball carrier to either carry for two steps or dispose immediately.
A fourth player acts as target and safety observer.
Smother actions must use open hands and remain directed towards the football path, not the opponent’s body.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder starts the ball carrier with a handball.
The ball carrier follows the hidden instruction to carry or dispose immediately.
The defender closes while reading the ball carrier’s body position.
If the ball carrier remains in possession and safe tackle range develops, the defender completes a legal tackle.
If the disposal action is already committed and tackling would be late or unsafe, the defender uses controlled smother pressure.
For a kick, the defender extends open hands into the expected football path without diving across the kicking leg.
For a handball, the defender closes the release space with open hands.
The defender scores two points for the correct decision and successful pressure.
The ball carrier scores one point for a clean disposal or escape.
Players rotate through all roles.
coachingPoints: Read possession status and body position before committing.
Tackle only while the opponent remains legally and safely tackleable.
Use smother pressure when disposal is already committed.
Keep hands open and directed towards the football path.
Avoid striking, diving or contacting the kicking leg.
Maintain balance through the pressure action.
Do not make secondary contact after disposal.
Continue defending the next phase if the smother creates a spill.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders recognise the ball carrier’s commitment to disposal.
Whether the selected defensive action is appropriate.
Whether smother hands target the football path.
Whether defenders remain balanced.
Whether dangerous leg or late body contact is avoided.
Whether players react to a deflected football.

commonErrors.error: Defender attempts a tackle after disposal is committed.
commonErrors.correction: Convert to controlled smother pressure.

commonErrors.error: Player dives across the kicking leg.
commonErrors.correction: Stay upright and pressure the football path with open hands.

commonErrors.error: Defender chooses a smother while a secure tackle is available.
commonErrors.correction: Close the body space and tackle before disposal begins.

commonErrors.error: Player swats downwards at the football.
commonErrors.correction: Present open hands into the expected release path.

commonErrors.error: Defender stops after a deflection.
commonErrors.correction: Locate the spill and continue the defensive effort.

progressions: Allow the ball carrier to fake the disposal.
Add kick and handball options.
Add a support receiver.
Continue play after a smother or loose football.
regressions: Predetermine the required defensive action.
Reduce movement speed.
Use handball smothers only.
Begin the defender closer to the ball carrier.
successIndicators: Apply legal tackle or smother pressure.
matchApplication: Defenders arriving near disposal must make rapid decisions. Attempting a late tackle can concede a free kick, while failing to smother allows an uncontested disposal. The correct response depends on possession, timing and body position.

title: Three-Defender Pressure Rotation
primarySkill: Rotating defensive pressure between three players
objective: Develop coordinated three-player pressure in which the nearest balanced defender attacks the ball carrier while teammates protect receivers and rotate responsibility after each disposal.
groundSize: Grids approximately 18 metres by 15 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Place three attackers and three defenders inside the grid.
Position one feeder outside.
Mark one scoring gate at each end.
Attackers may use handball and short kicks.
Defenders begin goal side of their direct opponents.
An eighth player acts as observer and return feeder.
Contests last a maximum of ten seconds.
Only the nearest balanced defender applies direct tackle pressure.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder releases the football to any attacker.
The nearest balanced defender closes the ball carrier.
The other two defenders protect the most dangerous receivers and central scoring space.
When the football is disposed, defenders call and rotate pressure roles.
The previous ball defender releases and recovers into support.
The new nearest defender applies pressure to the receiver.
If a legal tackle is completed, supporting defenders protect the likely release points.
Attackers score by carrying the football through a gate.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one for containing the attack for ten seconds.
Players rotate between attacking, defending, feeding and observing roles.
coachingPoints: Identify the nearest balanced pressure defender.
Communicate the pressure rotation early.
Supporting defenders protect dangerous space before chasing opponents.
Move while the football is travelling.
The previous tackler must release and recover immediately.
Maintain connected spacing between defenders.
Avoid three defenders collapsing on one ball carrier.
Protect likely exits around a completed tackle.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders identify pressure roles quickly.
Whether communication occurs before the receiver gains possession.
Whether supporting defenders protect useful space.
Whether the previous ball defender recovers.
Whether defensive spacing remains connected.
Whether tackles are supported without overcrowding.

commonErrors.error: All defenders follow the football.
commonErrors.correction: Assign one pressure defender and two support-space defenders.

commonErrors.error: Defenders rotate after the receiver has already accelerated.
commonErrors.correction: Move and communicate while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Previous tackler remains at the old contest.
commonErrors.correction: Release and recover into the next support position.

commonErrors.error: Defenders become spread too far apart.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain connected spacing that allows support and coverage.

commonErrors.error: Multiple defenders enter the tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one primary tackler and protect exits with the others.

progressions: Add a fourth attacker and defender.
Remove the time limit.
Allow longer kicks.
Continue immediately into attack after a turnover.
regressions: Predetermine the attacking disposal sequence.
Use handball only.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Reduce the grid size and player movement options.
matchApplication: Team pressure depends on repeated rotation rather than one player chasing continuously. Connected defenders must transfer responsibility as the football moves and protect the next attacking option.

title: Turnover-to-Tackle Transition Game
primarySkill: Transitioning immediately into tackle pressure after losing possession
objective: Develop the immediate defensive response required after a turnover by identifying the new ball carrier, protecting dangerous space and applying legal pressure before the opposition can spread.
groundSize: Grids approximately 24 metres by 18 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two evenly matched teams.
Mark a scoring gate at each end.
Begin with one team in possession inside the grid.
Players may use handball and short kicks.
The coach holds spare footballs outside the area.
At any time, the coach may call “turnover” and deliver a new football to the defending team.
The former attacking team must transition immediately into defence.
Tackles remain controlled and upright unless the group is appropriately prepared for match-like ground contact.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins moving the football towards its scoring gate.
The opposing team defends using connected pressure.
The coach calls “turnover” at an unpredictable moment.
The original football becomes dead.
