The coach immediately delivers a new football to a player from the former defending team.
The former attacking team must react and transition into defence.
The nearest balanced player pressures the new ball carrier.
Teammates protect central space and likely receivers.
Teams score one point by carrying the football through their attacking gate.
Award a bonus point for a tackle or turnover created within five seconds of the transition call.
Play in blocks of three to four minutes.
coachingPoints: React immediately when possession changes.
Identify the new ball carrier before sprinting.
The nearest balanced defender applies pressure.
Recover towards dangerous central space.
Communicate direct opponents and free receivers.
Avoid chasing the football from poor angles.
Decelerate before tackling.
Convert defensive pressure into controlled possession after a turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
How quickly players recognise the turnover.
Whether the new ball carrier is identified.
Whether central space is protected.
Whether defenders communicate during transition.
Whether pursuit angles are efficient.
Whether tackle technique remains controlled at high speed.
Whether pressure continues after the first disposal.

commonErrors.error: Players pause after the turnover call.
commonErrors.correction: React immediately and identify the nearest threat.

commonErrors.error: Every defender runs directly towards the football.
commonErrors.correction: Pressure with one player and protect space with the others.

commonErrors.error: Players recover towards the boundary and concede the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Sprint towards central dangerous space first.

commonErrors.error: Defender arrives too quickly and misses the tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate before entering contact range.

commonErrors.error: Team relaxes after forcing one rushed disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue rotating pressure until possession is secured.

progressions: Remove the coach’s turnover call and allow natural turnovers only.
Add scoreboard and time-pressure scenarios.
Expand the grid.
Allow full match-like disposal options.
regressions: Predetermine which player receives after the turnover.
Pause briefly to organise defensive roles.
Use pressure touches instead of tackles.
Reduce player numbers.
successIndicators: Complete legal tackles despite transition speed.
matchApplication: Many scoring opportunities occur immediately after turnovers. The team that reacts fastest can prevent clean transition, create a repeat turnover and stop the opposition before its attacking structure forms.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat
TK-029 – Tackle, Regain Feet and Rejoin

title: Pressure and Contest Block Assessment
primarySkill: Assessment of tackling and pressure in contested football
objective: Assess whether players can maintain safe tackling technique, select appropriate pressure actions and remain defensively connected through contested and transitional football situations.
groundSize: Six assessment stations occupying approximately one-half of an oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Construct six assessment stations.
Station 1 assesses recovery from incomplete contact into containment.
Station 2 assesses repeated boundary pressure.
Station 3 assesses safe rear-quarter tackling.
Station 4 assesses pressure on a stoppage or congestion exit.
Station 5 assesses tackle-or-smother decision making.
Station 6 assesses team pressure and turnover transition.
Assign a coach or trained observer to every station.
Divide players evenly and rotate every six to eight minutes.
Match players appropriately for contact activities.
Apply one consistent scoring system at every station.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, the defender experiences incomplete contact and must recover into a corral or second legal tackle.
The observer assesses balance recovery, patience and tackle judgement.
At Station 2, the defender applies several consecutive pressure efforts along a boundary channel.
The observer assesses inside positioning, repeat effort and controlled finishing.
At Station 3, the defender closes from the rear quarter and must reach a safe side-on position before tackling.
The observer assesses pursuit angle, speed matching and opponent protection.
At Station 4, defenders identify and pressure the first possession leaving congestion.
The observer assesses exit recognition, communication and safe contact timing.
At Station 5, the defender selects between a legal tackle and a controlled smother action.
The observer assesses decision accuracy, late-contact discipline and disposal pressure.
At Station 6, players complete a small-sided turnover transition game.
The observer assesses team reaction, pressure rotation, corridor protection and tackle execution.
Each behaviour receives:
2 points: Consistently demonstrated.
1 point: Demonstrated inconsistently or after correction.
0 points: Not demonstrated or performed unsafely.
Any reckless, high, low or late contact immediately stops the repetition.
Coaches record one technical strength, one pressure-decision priority and one team-defence development requirement for every player.
coachingPoints: Safety remains the primary assessment standard.
Players must recover from failed contact without making reckless second attempts.
Defenders should protect dangerous space before chasing the football.
Repeat effort must not reduce tackle quality.
Rear-quarter contact must become side-on before the tackle is completed.
Vulnerable players in congestion must be protected.
Defenders must distinguish between tackle, corral and smother opportunities.
Communication and team spacing are assessed alongside individual technique.
Turnover reaction should be immediate and organised.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players regain balance after failed contact.
Whether defenders maintain inside position near the boundary.
Whether rear-quarter tackles avoid force through the back.
Whether congestion exits are recognised early.
Whether tackle, corral and smother decisions are appropriate.
Whether late contact is avoided.
Whether defenders communicate and rotate pressure.
Whether central space is protected after turnovers.
Whether technical quality remains stable under repeated effort.
Whether players continue into the next defensive action.

commonErrors.error: Player makes repeated desperate tackle attempts.
commonErrors.correction: Recover balance and corral before attempting contact again.

commonErrors.error: Defender loses inside position during repeat pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Recover towards the corridor side after every effort.

commonErrors.error: Rear-quarter contact remains directly through the back.
commonErrors.correction: Reach the outside hip and move beside the opponent.

commonErrors.error: Defender dives blindly into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the likely exit and wait for a clear contact line.

commonErrors.error: Player attempts a late tackle instead of smother pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Recognise committed disposal and convert to open-hand pressure.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase the football and leave central space open.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one pressure player and protect dangerous space with others.

commonErrors.error: Technique deteriorates under repeated effort.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce work duration and restore approach, head and wrap standards.

progressions: Increase attacker freedom for players meeting all safety standards.
Introduce full match-like transition after every turnover.
Add scoreboard and time-pressure consequences.
Repeat the assessment under moderate fatigue.
Compare individual and team results across the training cycle.
regressions: Assess stations separately.
Replace live tackling with pressure touches.
Predetermine attacking movements and disposal options.
Reduce player numbers and working distances.
Return players to TK-040 or TK-050 before reassessment.
successIndicators: Apply repeated pressure without losing technique.
Protect the ball carrier during rear-quarter and congestion tackles.
Recognise tackle, corral and smother opportunities.
Avoid high, low and late contact.
Transition immediately into the next phase.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether players can apply tackling technique through the full pressure-and-contest phase of Australian football. Effective defenders must combine safe contact with judgement, repeat effort, congestion awareness, team connection and immediate transition after possession changes.

title: Three-Player Pressure Triangle
primarySkill: Coordinating pressure between three defenders
objective: Develop coordinated three-player pressure in which one defender attacks the ball carrier while two supporting defenders protect the nearest release options and rotate responsibility after each disposal.
groundSize: Triangular grids approximately 15 metres along each side.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a triangular grid with one attacking player positioned near each corner.
Position three defenders inside the triangle.
Place one feeder outside the grid with a football.
Nominate one defender as the initial pressure player and two as support defenders.
Attackers may carry for up to three steps before disposing.
Attackers may use handball or short kicks.
A seventh player acts as observer and return feeder where required.
Contests run for a maximum of twelve seconds.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder delivers the football to any attacker.
The nearest balanced defender closes the ball carrier.
The other two defenders position between the ball carrier and the available receivers.
If the football is disposed, the defender nearest the new receiver becomes the pressure player.
The previous pressure defender releases immediately and recovers into a supporting position.
Defenders communicate each pressure rotation.
A legal tackle may be completed when safe contact range develops.
Supporting defenders protect likely handball or kick exits rather than crowding the tackle.
Attackers score one point for completing four consecutive disposals.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing an ineffective disposal.
Players rotate between attacking, defending, feeding and observing roles.
coachingPoints: The nearest balanced defender applies direct pressure.
Supporting defenders position between the football and the nearest receivers.
Communicate the change of pressure responsibility before the receiver gains possession.
Move while the football is travelling.
Release the previous ball carrier immediately after disposal.
Maintain connected defensive spacing without all defenders collapsing on the football.
Support a completed tackle by protecting exits rather than adding unnecessary contact.
Transition into attack immediately after winning possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the nearest balanced defender applies pressure.
Whether supporting defenders protect realistic release options.
Whether defenders communicate before possession transfers.
Whether the previous pressure player recovers promptly.
Whether defensive spacing remains connected.
Whether tackles are supported without overcrowding.
Whether defenders transition quickly after winning possession.

commonErrors.error: All three defenders chase the football.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one pressure defender and two receiver-protection defenders.

commonErrors.error: Defenders rotate after the receiver has already moved.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate and move while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Previous pressure defender remains at the old contest.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and recover into the triangle.

commonErrors.error: Supporting defenders stand too far from receivers.
commonErrors.correction: Position close enough to close during the next disposal.

commonErrors.error: Multiple defenders enter the tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Leave one primary tackler and protect the exits.

commonErrors.error: Defenders win possession but remain congested.
commonErrors.correction: Spread immediately and use the full triangle.

progressions: Allow attackers unrestricted disposal types.
Reduce the size of the triangle.
Add a fourth attacker outside the triangle.
Continue play into a scoring gate after a turnover.
Introduce a twelve-second team-pressure scoring target.
regressions: Predetermine the attacking disposal sequence.
Use handball only.
Replace tackling with two-handed touch pressure.
Increase the triangle size.
Pause after each disposal to organise defensive positions.
successIndicators: Avoid unnecessary numbers at the contest.
matchApplication: Team pressure requires defenders to work as a connected unit. One player pressures the football while teammates remove the easiest release options, allowing pressure to continue across several disposals rather than ending after the first ball carrier releases.
relatedDrills: TK-060 – Pressure and Contest Block Assessment

title: Corridor Squeeze Pressure
primarySkill: Compressing central attacking space
objective: Teach defenders to narrow the corridor, force possession towards less dangerous outside space and create coordinated tackle opportunities.
groundSize: A corridor approximately 30 metres long and 18 metres wide, divided into central and outside lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a central corridor lane approximately 8 metres wide.
Mark an outside lane on each side.
Place an attacking scoring gate at the far end.
Divide players into an attacking team and a defending team.
Begin with equal numbers or one additional attacker.
Position defenders goalside and slightly inside their direct opponents.
Attackers may use handball and short kicks.
The attacking team begins with possession at one end.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team attempts to move the football through the corridor and score through the central gate.
Defenders begin in connected positions that protect the corridor.
The nearest balanced defender closes the ball carrier from an inside-out angle.
Supporting defenders narrow towards central space while remaining capable of closing outside receivers.
Defenders attempt to force the football into an outside lane.
Once possession moves outside, the nearest defender applies direct pressure.
Other defenders slide across to remove the return disposal into the corridor.
Legal tackles are permitted when safe contact range develops.
Attackers score two points for a central-gate entry and one point for an outside-gate entry.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing three consecutive outside disposals.
Reset after a score, turnover or stoppage.
coachingPoints: Protect central space before following direct opponents outside.
Approach the ball carrier from the corridor side.
Maintain connected spacing between defenders.
Slide together when the football moves laterally.
The nearest balanced player pressures the ball.
Supporting defenders remove the return disposal into the corridor.
Avoid overcommitting several defenders to one outside contest.
Convert outside pressure into a legal tackle opportunity.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders begin inside their opponents.
Whether the central lane remains protected.
Whether the defensive unit slides together.
Whether pressure transfers to the outside receiver.
Whether return options into the corridor are removed.
Whether tackles occur from balanced positions.
Whether defenders remain connected after a turnover.

commonErrors.correction: Keep one pressure player and protect the return options.

Add a time limit for the attacking team.
Allow longer kicks.
Add a recovering defender entering from behind.

Increase the width of the outside lanes.
Remove one attacking player.
Replace tackling with two-handed touch pressure.

successIndicators: Slide together as a defensive unit.
matchApplication: Protecting the corridor reduces the opposition’s most dangerous attacking options. Coordinated inside-out pressure forces play towards the boundary, where space is limited and tackle opportunities become more predictable.

title: Wing Trap Pressure
primarySkill: Creating a coordinated pressure trap on the wing

coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:

Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
Position one defender on the ball carrier, one inside the next receiver and one behind the immediate contest.

The attacking team begins with possession near half-back.
Attackers attempt to advance through a forward scoring gate.
Defenders attempt to force possession towards the boundary.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins moving the football along the wing.
The nearest defender approaches from inside and shows the ball carrier towards the boundary.
A second defender positions inside the nearest forward receiver.
A third defender protects the short release behind or beside the ball carrier.
When possession moves closer to the boundary, defenders compress the available space.
The nearest balanced defender applies direct tackle pressure.
Supporting defenders remove the inside handball, forward kick and retreat option.

Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing the football out of bounds under pressure.

Position inside likely forward receivers.
Remove the easy retreat disposal.
Compress space only when the football is near the boundary.
Maintain one primary pressure defender.
Supporting defenders protect exits rather than crashing into the tackle.
Communicate the trap before the ball carrier is fully contained.
Attack through the corridor after winning possession.

Whether the ball carrier is directed towards the boundary.

Reduce the number of attacking receivers.
Use handball only.
Replace live tackling with pressure touches.

matchApplication: Wing traps allow a team to use the boundary as an additional defender. Coordinated positioning can isolate the ball carrier, remove nearby options and create turnovers without every defender chasing the football.

title: Forward-Half Lock-In Pressure

coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into an attacking forward-half team and a defensive exit team.

Place defenders across likely exit lanes.
Mark two wide exit gates and one central exit gate beyond the 50-metre arc.
The attacking team attempts to score.
If the defensive team wins possession, it attempts to exit through any gate.
The original attacking team immediately becomes the pressure team.
Use a coach to restart from varied forward-entry locations.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with a forward entry or possession inside 50.
Play continues until a score, intercept, loose-ball win or turnover occurs.
When the defensive team gains possession, it attempts to exit defensive 50.
The nearest forward applies immediate pressure to the ball carrier.
Other forwards protect the nearest receivers and central exit lane.
Defenders further from the football squeeze towards likely exit options.
Legal tackles are permitted throughout live play.

The nearest balanced player pressures the ball carrier.
Protect the central exit before chasing wide receivers.
Position between the football and the likely next receiver.
Maintain pressure after the first disposal.
Avoid several forwards collapsing on one opponent.
Support tackles by protecting handball and kick exits.
Spread quickly when possession is regained.

Whether forwards react immediately to the turnover.
Whether the ball carrier is pressured before gaining time.
Whether the central exit remains protected.
Whether defenders cover the next receiver.
Whether pressure continues across several disposals.
Whether tackles are completed safely.
Whether regained possession creates a quick scoring attempt.

commonErrors.error: Forwards stop after losing possession.

commonErrors.error: All pressure players chase the ball carrier.

title: Defensive-50 Exit Pressure

objective: Teach a pressure unit to defend an opposition exit from defensive 50 by closing the first receiver, protecting central space and rotating pressure across successive possessions.

coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position an exit team inside defensive 50.
Position a pressure team across the likely short and long exit options.

Mark one central and two wide exit gates beyond the 50-metre arc.
The exit team attempts to move the football through a gate.
The pressure team attempts to force a turnover, boundary outcome or rushed disposal.
Position a coach with spare footballs to vary the starting location.
Maintain realistic positional spacing.
howTheDrillWorks:
The exit team begins with possession inside defensive 50.
The nearest pressure player closes the ball carrier while remaining aware of the mark and protected area where applicable.
Supporting pressure players position inside the likely short receivers.
Deeper defenders protect the central long-kick target.
When the football is disposed, the pressure unit shifts towards the new possession.
The nearest balanced defender closes the receiver.
Legal tackles are permitted once possession is established.
The exit team scores two points for a central exit and one point for a wide exit.
The pressure team scores two points for a turnover inside 50 and one point for forcing a boundary or uncontrolled long kick.

Position inside the nearest short receivers.
Protect the dangerous central long option.
Shift together as the football moves.
The nearest balanced player applies pressure.
Respect marks and protected areas before play on.
Move during the football’s flight.
Attack quickly after forcing a turnover.

Whether short receivers are defended from the inside.
Whether the central long option is protected.
Whether the unit shifts together.
Whether receivers are pressured as possession is established.
Whether defenders respect mark and protected-area rules.
Whether tackles remain controlled.
Whether turnovers create immediate scoring pressure.

commonErrors.error: Pressure player approaches from outside and opens the corridor.

commonErrors.correction: Close space while the football is travelling.

title: Kick-In Receiver Pressure
primarySkill: Pressuring the first receiver from a kick-in
objective: Develop the ability to identify and close the first kick-in receiver while respecting the protected area and preventing immediate attacking continuation.
groundSize: Defensive goal square and an area extending approximately 35 metres from goal.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a designated kicker inside the goal square.
Place three potential receivers across short, wide and central locations.
Assign one defender to each receiver.
Position one deeper defender to protect the long central exit.
Mark the relevant protected areas.
The kicker may select any receiver.
Defenders must begin in legal positions.
A coach observes protected-area compliance and pressure timing.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker begins with the football after a simulated behind.
Receivers move to create short and intermediate options.
Defenders track their opponents while maintaining inside position.

Move while the football is in flight.

Whether defenders track receiver movement.
Whether the likely target is recognised.
Whether defenders close during the kick.
Whether protected areas are respected.
Whether play-on pressure is immediate.
Whether supporting defenders cover the next option.
Whether the central long exit remains protected.

howTheDrillWorks:

title: Repeat-Entry Pressure Chain

title: Team Pressure Foundations Assessment
primarySkill: Assessment of coordinated team pressure

setup:
Construct five team-pressure assessment stations.
Station 1 assesses three-player pressure rotation.
Station 2 assesses corridor squeeze and inside-out positioning.
Station 3 assesses a coordinated wing trap.
Station 4 assesses forward-half lock-in or defensive-50 exit pressure.
Station 5 assesses numerical disadvantage and repeated-entry defence.
Assign a coach or trained observer to each station.
Divide players into balanced groups.
Rotate groups every seven to nine minutes.
Use one consistent assessment scale across all stations.

howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, three defenders rotate pressure against three moving attackers.
The observer assesses role allocation, receiver protection and tackle support.
At Station 2, defenders compress the corridor and force possession towards outside space.
The observer assesses inside positioning, collective movement and tackle creation.
At Station 3, defenders attempt to trap possession near the boundary.
The observer assesses approach angles, exit denial and communication.
At Station 4, players defend an opposition exit or attempt to lock the football inside the forward half.
The observer assesses first-receiver pressure, central-space protection and turnover conversion.
At Station 5, defenders manage a numerical disadvantage before completing several repeated defensive phases.
The observer assesses delay, recovery integration, reset speed and technique under fatigue.
Each assessed behaviour receives:
2 points: Consistently demonstrated.
1 point: Demonstrated inconsistently or after correction.
0 points: Not demonstrated or performed unsafely.
Any high, low, late or uncontrolled contact stops the repetition immediately.
Coaches record one individual pressure strength, one team-structure priority and one recommended development drill for each player.

Tackle technique must remain safe under team and fatigue demands.

Whether outnumbered defenders delay effectively.
Whether players reset between repeated phases.
Whether tackling remains legal under fatigue.
Whether turnovers are converted into controlled attack.

commonErrors.error: All defenders chase the football.

title: Centre-Bounce Exit Pressure

setup:

A coach begins each repetition with a controlled throw-up or ground release.

howTheDrillWorks:

Divide players into balanced positional groups.
Rotate groups every eight to ten minutes.
Use one consistent assessment scale across all stations.
Match players appropriately for controlled contact.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, defenders pressure the first possession and protect stoppage exit lanes.
The observer assesses role clarity, corridor protection and tackle timing.
At Station 2, a pressure unit attempts to prevent a controlled half-back or defensive-50 exit.
The observer assesses receiver positioning, collective shifting and first-receiver pressure.
At Station 3, defenders squeeze central space and create a boundary or zone trap.
The observer assesses inside positioning, team movement and tackle creation.
At Station 4, defenders use a loose player or manage a numerical disadvantage.
The observer assesses threat prioritisation, delay and tackle support.
At Station 5, pressure is transferred across several field zones before a red-time defensive scenario.
The observer assesses pressure handover, recovery, communication and risk management.
Each assessed behaviour receives:
2 points: Consistently demonstrated.
1 point: Demonstrated inconsistently or after correction.
0 points: Not demonstrated or performed unsafely.
Any high, low, late or uncontrolled contact stops the repetition immediately.
Coaches record one individual pressure strength, one structural priority and one recommended progression for every player.
coachingPoints: The nearest balanced defender applies direct pressure.
Supporting defenders protect the most dangerous space and receivers.
Pressure responsibility must rotate as possession moves.
Central space should be protected before lower-value outside options.
Teams must shift together rather than as isolated players.
Loose and recovering defenders must prioritise the greatest threat.
Tackle technique must remain safe under high running loads.
Players must understand scoreboard and time context.
Turnovers should lead to controlled attacking transition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders identify first-possession pressure roles.
Whether corridor and central exits are protected.
Whether receivers are covered during rebound.
Whether the defensive unit shifts together.
Whether boundary and zone traps form at the correct time.
Whether loose defenders identify the greatest threat.
Whether pressure transfers between field zones.
Whether players manage late-game risk appropriately.
Whether tackling remains legal under fatigue.
Whether turnovers are converted into controlled possession.

commonErrors.error: Defenders collapse on the first possession.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one pressure defender and protect receivers with others.

commonErrors.error: Pressure unit follows direct opponents and opens central space.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise the corridor and dangerous forward lanes.

commonErrors.error: Defenders shift after the receiver gains possession.
commonErrors.correction: Move while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Boundary trap forms before the football is committed outside.
commonErrors.correction: Hold connected spacing until the ball carrier enters restricted space.

commonErrors.error: Loose defender follows the football and loses depth.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the greatest scoring threat before joining pressure.

commonErrors.error: Pressure handover fails between field zones.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate responsibility before possession enters the next area.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt reckless tackles late in the scenario.
commonErrors.correction: Corral and protect scoring space when safe contact range is unavailable.

commonErrors.error: Technique deteriorates under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce work duration and restore deceleration, head position and legal wrap.

progressions: Increase attacker freedom and disposal distance.
Remove station boundaries and complete a full-ground assessment.
Add scoreboard and match-time consequences.
Reduce recovery between stations.
Repeat the assessment under moderate match-specific fatigue.
regressions: Assess each station separately.
Predetermine attacking ball movement.
Replace live tackling with pressure touches.
Reduce player numbers and ground size.
Return players to TK-070 before completing the full assessment.
successIndicators: Shift and rotate as a connected unit.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether players can apply tackling and pressure as part of complete team ball movement. Effective AFL defence requires coordinated positioning, pressure rotation, receiver denial, safe tackling and immediate transition across the entire ground.

title: Press-Trigger Recognition
primarySkill: Recognising when to initiate coordinated pressure
objective: Develop the ability to recognise poor disposals, isolated receivers and delayed possession as triggers for coordinated team pressure.
groundSize: A grid approximately 30 metres long and 24 metres wide, divided into three vertical lanes.
equipment: Coloured trigger cards or verbal trigger calls
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into an attacking possession team and a defending pressure team.
Position both teams across the three vertical lanes.
Mark one scoring gate at each end.
The attacking team begins with uncontested possession at one end.
The coach controls the quality and type of attacking disposal through instructions to selected players.
Pressure triggers include a high handball, slow ground-ball gather, receiver facing backwards, poor kick, isolated wide receiver or stationary possession.
Defenders begin in balanced team shape and may not press fully until a recognised trigger appears.
Use controlled tackling throughout the drill.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins moving the football through the grid.
Defenders hold connected positions and protect central space.
The coach creates or calls a pressure trigger during the possession sequence.
The nearest defender calls the trigger and closes the ball carrier.
Supporting defenders move towards nearby receivers and remove easy release options.
The pressure unit attempts to trap the ball carrier or force an ineffective disposal.
Legal tackles are permitted once safe contact range develops.
The attacking team scores one point for moving through the far gate.
The defending team scores two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing a backwards or boundary disposal.
If defenders press without a genuine trigger and lose shape, the attacking team receives one bonus point.
Reset after a score, turnover or stoppage.
coachingPoints: Maintain defensive shape until a genuine trigger develops.
Recognise poor body position, inaccurate disposal and isolated possession.
The nearest defender should call the trigger clearly.
Supporting defenders must press at the same moment.
Close the ball carrier from an angle that removes the easiest disposal.
Protect central space while applying pressure.
Avoid one defender pressing alone without team support.
Decelerate before tackling despite the urgency of the trigger.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify genuine pressure triggers.
Whether the first defender communicates clearly.
Whether supporting defenders react at the same time.
Whether central space remains protected.
Whether receivers are denied before possession arrives.
Whether defenders distinguish between pressing and holding shape.
Whether tackle technique remains controlled.

commonErrors.error: One defender presses without support.
commonErrors.correction: Hold until teammates are connected and call the trigger before moving.

commonErrors.error: Defenders press every possession.
commonErrors.correction: Recognise that pressure should increase only when the opposition is vulnerable.

commonErrors.error: Supporting defenders follow the football rather than receivers.
commonErrors.correction: Remove the nearest release options while the first defender pressures.

commonErrors.error: Central space opens during the press.
commonErrors.correction: Approach from inside and retain corridor protection.

commonErrors.error: Defender arrives too quickly and is evaded.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate before contact and maintain balanced footwork.

commonErrors.error: Players recognise the trigger but do not communicate.
commonErrors.correction: Require an immediate verbal call before the pressure action.

progressions: Remove coach-generated triggers and allow defenders to identify natural cues.
Allow unrestricted attacking ball movement.
Add a scoreboard consequence for failed pressure attempts.
Introduce a spare attacker to increase the importance of trigger selection.
Continue into full transition after a turnover.
regressions: Use one predetermined trigger only.
Pause play when the trigger appears and ask defenders to identify it.
Replace tackling with controlled pressure touches.
Reduce player numbers and grid size.
Allow defenders to nominate the trigger before each repetition.
successIndicators: Create tackles, rushed disposals or turnovers.
matchApplication: Elite pressure is not constant uncontrolled chasing. Teams identify moments when the opposition is vulnerable and increase pressure collectively, creating turnovers while preserving defensive structure.
relatedDrills: TK-080 – Team Pressure and Ball-Movement Assessment

title: Deceptive Ball-Carrier Pressure
primarySkill: Defending against deception before tackling
objective: Develop the ability to remain balanced against ball, handball and kick fakes before committing to a legal tackle.
groundSize: Contest areas approximately 10 metres by 8 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark multiple contest areas with one exit gate and two disposal targets.
Position one ball carrier and one defender approximately 3 metres apart.
A third player acts as observer and one of the disposal targets.
The attacker may use a handball fake, kick fake, shoulder baulk or football transfer.
The attacker may use no more than two deceptive actions.
The defender must remain balanced and protect the scoring gate.
All tackles remain controlled and upright.
howTheDrillWorks:
On the observer’s signal, the attacker begins moving towards the exit gate.
The attacker may use up to two deceptive actions.
The defender closes space without committing to the first ball movement.
The defender tracks the attacker’s hips and supporting foot position.
If the attacker attempts a real disposal, the defender applies legal pressure without making late contact.
If the attacker retains possession and enters tackle range, the defender completes a legal tackle.
The defender scores two points for a completed tackle and one point for forcing an ineffective disposal.
The attacker scores one point for a clean disposal or controlled gate entry.
Players exchange roles after each repetition.
Complete five to seven repetitions per player.
coachingPoints: Read the hips, trunk and supporting foot rather than only the football.
Maintain active feet through every fake.
Avoid leaving the ground or reaching towards a kick fake.
Preserve a reaction buffer until the attacker commits.
Recognise the difference between disposal preparation and actual release.
Close the near foot before completing the tackle.
Control the torso and disposal arm rather than grabbing the football.
Avoid late contact after a completed disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders react to body movement or only football movement.
Whether players remain balanced through repeated fakes.
Whether the scoring gate remains protected.
Whether defenders identify actual disposal release.
Whether the tackle is attempted from close range.
Whether late contact is avoided.
Whether attackers use realistic deception.

commonErrors.error: Defender reaches towards a handball fake.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the hands ready and continue moving the feet.

commonErrors.error: Player jumps at a kick fake.
commonErrors.correction: Stay grounded and read the supporting leg and hips.

commonErrors.error: Defender waits too long after the attacker commits.
commonErrors.correction: Reaccelerate as soon as the movement becomes genuine.

commonErrors.error: Tackler focuses on the football and concedes the exit gate.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the dangerous running line first.

commonErrors.error: Defender makes contact after a clean disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the pressure action once release is complete.

commonErrors.error: Attacker performs unrealistic repeated fakes.
commonErrors.correction: Limit deception to two match-like movements.

progressions: Allow unrestricted deceptive actions within a five-second limit.
Add a support receiver who may move.
Permit the attacker to use a controlled fend-off.
Increase the contest area and approach speed.
Add a second defender arriving late.
regressions: Predetermine the type of fake.
Allow only one deceptive action.
Use two-handed touch pressure.
Reduce attacker speed.
Practise without disposal targets.
successIndicators: Recognise genuine disposal or movement commitment.
Complete legal tackles from close range.
matchApplication: Advanced ball carriers use fakes to make defenders stop, jump or reach. Effective tacklers remain disciplined, continue moving and commit only when the opponent’s movement or disposal becomes genuine.

title: Outnumbered Delay-to-Trap Defence
primarySkill: Delaying an outnumbered attack until a pressure trap can form
objective: Develop the ability to delay an outnumbered attack, direct possession towards a planned pressure area and complete the tackle once defensive support arrives.
groundSize: A grid approximately 28 metres long and 20 metres wide with one designated trap zone.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position three attackers against two starting defenders.
Place one recovering defender 10 metres behind the attacking group.
Mark a central scoring gate and two wide gates.
Designate one wide corner as the defensive trap zone.
The attackers begin with possession.
The starting defenders must protect the central gate and influence play towards the trap zone.
The recovering defender enters on the coach’s signal or after the second attacking disposal.
Rotate roles after each repetition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attackers begin moving towards the scoring gates.
The nearest defender applies controlled corral pressure.
The second defender protects the central gate and most dangerous receiver.
Defenders angle their positioning to encourage possession towards the trap zone.
Attackers may use handball or short kick.
After the second disposal, the recovering defender enters.
Defenders communicate and close the trap around the ball carrier.
The nearest balanced defender attempts a legal tackle.
Supporting defenders remove the inside and backwards releases.
Attackers score two points through the central gate and one through a wide gate.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one for delaying the attack for ten seconds.
coachingPoints: Protect central space while outnumbered.
Delay rather than attempting a low-percentage early tackle.
Influence possession towards the designated trap area.
Maintain separation between the two starting defenders.
Communicate when the recovering defender enters.
Increase pressure only after defensive support is connected.
Remove inside and backwards exits before completing the trap.
Maintain one primary tackler.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders protect the central scoring gate.
Whether the attack is influenced towards the trap zone.
Whether defenders delay without becoming passive.
Whether the recovering player enters through a useful angle.
Whether pressure increases at the correct time.
Whether supporting defenders remove release options.
Whether the tackle remains controlled.

commonErrors.error: First defender charges and is eliminated.
commonErrors.correction: Corral and delay until support arrives.

commonErrors.error: Both starting defenders defend the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one defender protecting the central receiver and gate.

commonErrors.error: Attack is allowed to choose the central route.
commonErrors.correction: Use body angle to direct possession towards the trap area.

commonErrors.error: Recovering defender runs directly behind the play.
commonErrors.correction: Enter through the central or inside defensive line.

commonErrors.error: Defenders tackle before the trap is connected.
commonErrors.correction: Continue delaying until the support defenders remove exits.

commonErrors.error: Multiple defenders crash into the final tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one tackler and use others to close disposal options.

progressions: Delay the recovering defender’s entry.
Allow attackers unrestricted disposals.
Remove the visible trap-zone markers.
Add a fourth attacker and second recovering defender.
Continue play after a defensive turnover.
regressions: Begin with equal numbers.
Predetermine the attacking route.
Use handball only.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Position the recovering defender closer.
successIndicators: Direct possession towards a planned area.
Complete a legal tackle once the trap forms.
matchApplication: When outnumbered, defenders should delay and shape the attack rather than chase immediate tackles. Directing possession towards support or the boundary can convert a disadvantage into a coordinated pressure trap.

title: High-Press Receiver Handover
primarySkill: Handing over receivers within a high defensive press
objective: Develop clear receiver handovers that allow a high defensive press to remain connected while opposition players lead, cross and exchange positions.
groundSize: A forward-half grid approximately 35 metres long and 30 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position an exit team inside the grid with three or four receiving players.
Position an equal number of high-press defenders.
Mark one central and two wide exit gates.
Receivers may lead, cross and exchange lanes.
Defenders begin inside and goalside of their initial opponents.
A designated kicker or feeder begins each repetition.
Defenders must hand over crossing receivers without opening central space.
Tackles are controlled and begin only after possession is established.
howTheDrillWorks:
Receivers begin moving to create exit options.
Defenders track their movement while maintaining press shape.
When receivers cross, defenders call whether to stay or hand over.
The feeder selects a receiver and delivers the football.
The nearest balanced defender closes while the football is travelling.
Other defenders protect the next receiver and central exit.
If the receiver plays on, the closing defender applies legal tackle pressure.
The exit team scores two points for a central exit and one for a wide exit.
The pressure team scores two points for a tackle or turnover and one for forcing a backwards disposal.
Reset after the exit, turnover or stoppage.
Rotate receiver and defender roles.
coachingPoints: Begin inside and goalside of receivers.
Communicate crossing movements before the handover is completed.
Switch only when it preserves the defensive structure.
Maintain corridor protection during every receiver exchange.
Move towards the selected receiver while the football travels.
The nearest balanced defender applies pressure.
Other defenders protect the next options.
Avoid following one opponent through multiple zones when a handover is available.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders maintain starting position.
Whether crossing receivers are communicated.
Whether handovers occur before separation develops.
Whether central space remains protected.
Whether the selected receiver is pressured quickly.
Whether supporting defenders cover the next option.
Whether defenders avoid duplicated responsibility.

commonErrors.error: Defenders follow receivers across the entire grid.
commonErrors.correction: Hand over when a teammate has the better defensive position.

commonErrors.error: Communication occurs after receivers cross.
commonErrors.correction: Call the movement early and confirm the handover.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders take the same receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Use clear “stay” or “switch” language.

commonErrors.error: Central exit opens during a handover.
commonErrors.correction: Preserve inside positioning before changing responsibility.

commonErrors.error: Closing defender waits for possession.
commonErrors.correction: Move while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Supporting defenders watch the tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Cover the next receiver and likely release option.

progressions: Increase receiver movement freedom.
Allow switches of play.
Add a spare exit player.
Continue into transition after a turnover.
Remove assigned direct opponents and defend zonally.
regressions: Use only two crossing receivers.
Predetermine the crossing pattern.
Pause at the handover point.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Reduce the grid width.
successIndicators: Close the selected receiver during the football’s flight.
Maintain coverage of the next option.
matchApplication: High presses are vulnerable when receivers cross and defenders lose responsibility. Clear handovers allow the pressure unit to remain connected and close receivers without creating open central exits.

title: Repeat-Tackle Fatigue Wave
primarySkill: Maintaining safe tackling technique under repeated fatigue
objective: Develop the ability to complete several consecutive pressure and tackle efforts while preserving legal contact, safe head position and immediate recovery behaviour.
groundSize: A central defensive area approximately 18 metres by 18 metres with four entry gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one active defender in the centre.
Place four attackers outside separate entry gates.
Each attacker has a football or receives one from a feeder.
A coach controls the order and timing of entries.
The defender completes one pressure or tackle action per attacker.
Tackle bags may replace live players during early repetitions.
Limit each work period to 20–30 seconds.
Provide full recovery between sets.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach calls the first entry gate.
The attacker enters with the football.
The defender accelerates, decelerates and completes a controlled tackle or pressure touch.
The coach calls “release” immediately after control.
The defender regains balance and returns towards the centre.
A second attacker enters from a different gate.
The defender repeats the process for three to five attacking entries.
The final attacker may use one controlled evasive movement.
The defender receives one point for each technically correct effort.
Any unsafe contact ends the set immediately.
Rotate defenders and complete two to four sets.
coachingPoints: Technique takes priority over completing every repetition.
Accelerate early and decelerate before contact.
Keep the head safely beside or behind the opponent.
Maintain legal tackle height.
Wrap both arms before attempting control.
Release immediately and recover through the centre.
Communicate fatigue or loss of technique.
End the set when safe standards cannot be maintained.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether deceleration quality changes under fatigue.
Whether tackle height rises late in the set.
Whether head position remains safe.
Whether arm wrapping becomes incomplete.
Whether players recover promptly between entries.
Whether communication and awareness remain effective.
Whether the coach stops sets when technique deteriorates.

commonErrors.error: Defender arrives faster with each repetition.
commonErrors.correction: Control the final steps regardless of fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Tackle height rises late in the set.
commonErrors.correction: Lower through the hips or end the set.

commonErrors.error: Head position moves in front of the opponent.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and restore side-on entry.

commonErrors.error: Player reaches instead of wrapping.
commonErrors.correction: Continue foot movement until close enough for a two-arm tackle.

commonErrors.error: Defender remains at the previous contest.
commonErrors.correction: Release and recover towards the centre immediately.

commonErrors.error: Coach rewards completion despite unsafe technique.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the set as soon as technical standards are lost.

progressions: Increase the number of attacking entries to a safe maximum.
Vary entry speed and angle.
Add disposal attempts.
Introduce two active defenders who communicate alternating responsibilities.
Complete the final repetition as a live evasion contest.
regressions: Use tackle bags for all entries.
Reduce the set to two or three actions.
Increase recovery between entries.
Use pressure touches rather than tackles.
Predetermine the entry order.
successIndicators: Maintain technique through the final repetition.
matchApplication: Players frequently complete several pressure efforts within one passage. Conditioning is useful only when tackling technique remains safe, controlled and effective despite repeated running demands.
relatedDrills: TK-029 – Tackle, Regain Feet and Rejoin
TK-080 – Team Pressure and Ball-Movement Assessment

title: Comeback Pressure Scenario
primarySkill: Applying aggressive but controlled pressure while trailing
objective: Develop the pressure decisions required when trailing late in a match and needing to create a turnover without conceding an easy scoring opportunity.
groundSize: Approximately half an oval with attacking and defensive scoring gates.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into a possession team protecting a narrow lead and a pressure team trailing by one or two scores.
Set a countdown between 60 and 120 seconds.
The possession team begins with the football in its defensive half.
The pressure team positions in an aggressive but connected press.
Mark a central and two wide exit gates for the possession team.
The pressure team attacks goals after winning possession.
Restart the scenario from varied field positions.
Tackles remain legal and controlled.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts the clock.
The possession team attempts to retain the football and exit through a gate.
The pressure team identifies when to hold shape and when to press.
On a poor disposal or isolated receive, defenders initiate coordinated pressure.
The nearest balanced defender attacks the ball carrier.
Supporting defenders remove backwards and short release options.
If the pressure team wins possession, it attempts to score immediately.
The possession team scores one point for each controlled exit or thirty-second retention period.
The pressure team scores two points for a turnover and additional points for the resulting score.
The scenario ends when time expires, a score occurs or the possession team secures a full exit.
Review pressure decisions before resetting.
coachingPoints: Understand the score and time before pressing.
Increase pressure without abandoning the most dangerous opposition receiver.
Recognise poor disposals and isolated possession as pressing triggers.
Remove backwards and safe retention options.
Avoid high-risk lunges that allow the opposition to escape.
Maintain legal tackling technique despite urgency.
Attack quickly but clearly after winning possession.
Communicate remaining time and required score.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players understand the match situation.
Whether pressure increases at appropriate moments.
Whether the press remains connected.
Whether safe opposition exits are removed.
Whether tackle attempts remain balanced.
Whether the team attacks quickly after turnovers.
Whether players communicate score and time.
Whether excessive risk creates easy opposition scores.

commonErrors.error: Defenders press continuously without structure.
commonErrors.correction: Hold shape until a genuine turnover opportunity develops.

commonErrors.error: One defender charges and is bypassed.
commonErrors.correction: Press collectively and protect the next receiver.

commonErrors.error: Backwards possession remains unguarded.
commonErrors.correction: Remove the safe release to force a riskier disposal.

commonErrors.error: Tacklers lunge because of time pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain balance and legal contact standards.

commonErrors.error: Team wins possession but attacks without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the best scoring option before disposing.

commonErrors.error: Players do not know the time remaining.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate a leader to call the clock and required score.

progressions: Reduce the available time.
Increase the deficit.
Add an opposition spare.
Begin from a boundary throw-in or kick-in.
Continue after the first score if time remains.
regressions: Increase the available time.
Begin with equal numbers.
Predetermine the pressing trigger.
Replace live tackling with pressure touches.
Pause after turnovers to organise the attack.
successIndicators: Convert regained possession into scoring attempts.
matchApplication: Teams trailing late must increase turnover pressure without becoming disorganised. Effective comeback pressure removes safe possession, forces risk and creates fast scoring opportunities while avoiding reckless free kicks or easy opposition exits.

title: Last-Line Goal-Saving Tackle
primarySkill: Completing a goal-saving tackle as the last defender
objective: Develop the composure and positioning required for a last defender to delay the ball carrier, protect the goal line and complete a legal goal-saving tackle.
groundSize: A forward area approximately 25 metres from goal and the width of the goal square.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position an attacker with the football 20–25 metres from goal.
Place the last defender 4–6 metres goal side and slightly inside.
Position a feeder outside the area.
Mark one boundary-side escape lane.
A fourth player acts as observer and rebound target.
The attacker may run towards goal, attempt a shot or move towards the boundary.
The defender must protect the direct path to goal.
Tackles remain controlled and upright unless safe ground contact has been formally introduced.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder releases the attacker into the scoring area.
The defender retreats or adjusts while remaining between the attacker and goal.
The defender closes the direct shooting line.
If the attacker remains outside tackle range, the defender corrals towards the boundary side.
If the attacker prepares to shoot, the defender closes the disposal window.
When safe contact range develops, the defender completes a legal tackle.
The attacker scores two points for a goal and one point for reaching the goal square under control.
The defender scores two points for a tackle and one point for forcing a wide or rushed shot.
If the defender wins possession, they dispose to the rebound target.
Players rotate through attacker, defender, feeder and target roles.
coachingPoints: Remain goal side and protect the direct scoring line.
Avoid charging too early and allowing the attacker to run around the defender.
Use the boundary side as the lower-risk escape.
Read whether the attacker intends to run, evade or shoot.
Close quickly as the ball becomes exposed for a shot.
Avoid contact with an extended kicking leg.
Complete the tackle from a balanced side-on position.
Secure possession and exit safely after winning the football.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the defender remains between the attacker and goal.
Whether direct scoring space is protected.
Whether the attacker is influenced towards the boundary.
Whether the defender recognises the shot preparation.
Whether contact avoids the kicking leg.
Whether the tackle occurs from balance.
Whether the defender completes a safe rebound disposal.

commonErrors.error: Defender charges and is evaded.
commonErrors.correction: Delay and maintain goal-side position until the attacker commits.

commonErrors.error: Player protects the boundary and concedes the direct goal line.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise the shortest path to goal.

commonErrors.error: Defender attempts contact from too far away.
commonErrors.correction: Corral until the near foot can arrive close.

commonErrors.error: Tackler dives across the kicking leg.
commonErrors.correction: Close the torso from the side and use smother pressure if the kick is committed.

commonErrors.error: Defender wins possession but turns it over centrally.
commonErrors.correction: Use the safest rebound target.

commonErrors.error: Player becomes passive near goal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue reducing space while preserving balance.

progressions: Add an attacking support runner.
Add a recovering defender.
Allow the attacker unrestricted shot and handball choices.
Begin from a turnover with both players moving.
Introduce scoreboard and late-game context.
regressions: Predetermine the attacker’s running line.
Use a scoring gate instead of goals.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Reduce attacking speed.
Begin the defender closer to the attacker.
successIndicators: Influence the attacker towards lower-value space.
Complete a legal goal-saving tackle or force a rushed shot.
matchApplication: Last-line defenders must balance urgency with patience. Protecting the goal, delaying the attacker and tackling at the correct moment can prevent a certain score without conceding a free kick or being eliminated by an early commitment.

title: Advantage-Call Recovery Pressure
primarySkill: Responding to play continuing after a free kick or advantage call
objective: Teach defenders to distinguish between a stopped free kick and continued advantage, then recover immediately into legal pressure when play remains live.
groundSize: A grid approximately 20 metres by 16 metres with two scoring gates.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide players into two small teams.
Mark a scoring gate at each end.
Begin with live possession in the centre.
The coach carries a whistle and uses clear calls for “free kick”, “advantage” and “play stopped”.
On some whistle calls, play stops and the player receiving the free kick must be protected.
On advantage calls, play continues immediately.
Defenders must respond according to the call.
Controlled tackling remains active during live play.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins as a small-sided possession contest.
The coach blows the whistle during a disposal or contest.
The coach immediately calls either “advantage” or “play stopped”.
On “play stopped”, all defenders disengage and establish legal mark positions.
On “advantage”, defenders continue playing and identify the new ball carrier.
The nearest balanced defender applies pressure.
Supporting defenders protect the most dangerous receivers and scoring gate.
Teams score one point by moving through the attacking gate.
Award the defending team two points for a legal tackle or turnover following an advantage call.
Penalise any player who tackles after play is stopped or stops competing during advantage.
Reset after each score or stoppage.
coachingPoints: Listen beyond the whistle for the controlling call.
Stop contact immediately when play is declared stopped.
Continue competing when advantage is called.
Identify the new ball carrier rather than focusing on the original contest.
Recover towards dangerous central space.
Communicate whether play is live.
Avoid retaliatory or late contact.
Re-establish balanced pressure before tackling.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players react correctly to the whistle and call.
Whether contact stops immediately during a dead-ball situation.
Whether defenders continue during advantage.
Whether the new ball carrier is identified.
Whether central scoring space is protected.
Whether players communicate live or stopped status.
Whether tackles remain legal after the transition.

commonErrors.error: Players stop automatically at every whistle.
commonErrors.correction: Listen for the advantage or stopped call before reacting.

commonErrors.error: Tackler continues contact after play is stopped.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and move to a legal mark position.

commonErrors.error: Defenders watch the original free-kick contest during advantage.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the new ball carrier and next receiver.

commonErrors.error: Players argue with the call instead of recovering.
commonErrors.correction: Respond to the current phase and review decisions later.

commonErrors.error: Defender sprints directly at the football without balance.
commonErrors.correction: Recover the angle and decelerate before contact.

commonErrors.error: Teammates do not communicate that play remains live.
commonErrors.correction: Require an immediate “live” or “stopped” call.

progressions: Remove the clear verbal call and use umpire-style signals.
Add uncertain ball spills around the free-kick moment.
Introduce scoreboard consequences.
Continue into a full-ground transition.
Allow rapid advantage after marking or out-of-bounds simulations.
regressions: Walk through each call separately.
Predetermine whether advantage will be paid.
Use pressure touches rather than tackles.
Reduce player numbers.
Pause briefly after the whistle before giving the call.
successIndicators: Listen to the full officiating call.
Stop contact when play is dead.
Continue immediately when advantage is paid.
Apply legal pressure without late contact.
matchApplication: Players must respond correctly when a whistle does not automatically stop play. Misreading advantage can concede uncontested territory, while failing to release during a stopped phase can result in further penalties.
relatedDrills: TK-018 – Tackle Release to Next Threat
TK-029 – Tackle, Regain Feet and Rejoin

title: Chaos-Ball Pressure Game
primarySkill: Maintaining pressure through unpredictable possession changes
objective: Develop adaptable pressure behaviours when possession, direction, player numbers and football location change unpredictably.
groundSize: A grid approximately 30 metres by 24 metres with four scoring gates.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two evenly matched teams.
Mark one coloured scoring gate on each side of the grid.
Begin with one live football and keep spare footballs with the coach.
The coach may change the attacking direction, introduce a new football, remove the current football or add a temporary neutral player.
Teams must identify possession, direction and pressure responsibilities after every change.
Tackles remain controlled and legal.
Play in short blocks of two to four minutes.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins play with one team in possession.
Teams attack the designated scoring gate.
The nearest balanced defender pressures the ball carrier.
Supporting defenders protect the nearest receivers and central space.
At unpredictable moments, the coach may call a new gate colour, release a second football or declare a turnover.
When a new football becomes active, the previous football becomes dead.
Players must release any completed contact and identify the new live phase.
Legal tackling resumes once the new ball carrier is identified.
Teams score one point through the correct gate.
Award one bonus point for creating a score within ten seconds of a pressure turnover.
Stop immediately for unsafe confusion or contact.
coachingPoints: Scan continuously for possession, direction and player numbers.
Confirm which football is live before applying contact.
Release immediately when the current phase becomes dead.
The nearest balanced defender applies pressure.
Protect central space during every transition.
Communicate the new direction and ball carrier.
Avoid chasing blindly when the phase changes.
Preserve legal tackle technique under uncertainty and fatigue.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
How quickly players identify the live football.
Whether new attacking direction is communicated.
Whether defenders release dead-ball contact.
Whether pressure responsibility is allocated quickly.
Whether central space remains protected.
Whether players remain balanced during sudden transitions.
Whether tackle safety is maintained under confusion and fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Players continue contesting a dead football.
commonErrors.correction: Stop, scan and locate the new live phase immediately.

commonErrors.error: Defender tackles before confirming possession.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the active ball carrier before applying contact.

commonErrors.error: Team runs towards the new football and opens the centre.
commonErrors.correction: Recover through central space and allocate one pressure player.

commonErrors.error: Communication disappears during rapid changes.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate calls for colour, ball and opponent.

commonErrors.error: Tacklers arrive recklessly after a direction change.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate and restore tackle shape before contact.

commonErrors.error: Players become confused by too many simultaneous changes.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the number and frequency of coach interventions.

progressions: Introduce two live footballs for a short controlled period.
Change attacking direction more frequently.
Add temporary numerical advantages.
Include scoreboard and time-pressure consequences.
Expand into a larger field area.
regressions: Use direction changes only.
Give a clear pause before introducing a new football.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Reduce player numbers.
Use only two scoring gates.
successIndicators: Identify the active football and direction.
Release contact when play becomes dead.
Convert turnovers into fast scoring opportunities.
matchApplication: Matches contain unpredictable spills, umpire calls, deflections, turnovers and changing numbers. Players must adapt rapidly without losing defensive structure or tackling discipline.

title: Advanced Pressure Decision Assessment
primarySkill: Assessment of advanced pressure decision making
objective: Assess whether players can recognise advanced pressure cues, maintain defensive structure and execute safe tackles across complex match-like scenarios.
groundSize: Six assessment stations occupying approximately one-half to a full oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Construct six advanced assessment stations.
Station 1 assesses press-trigger recognition.
Station 2 assesses defence against ball-carrier deception.
Station 3 assesses outnumbered delay and pressure-trap formation.
Station 4 assesses receiver handovers within a high press.
Station 5 assesses repeat tackling under fatigue.
Station 6 assesses scoreboard, advantage and chaos-pressure decisions.
Assign a coach or trained observer to each station.
Divide players into balanced groups and rotate every seven to nine minutes.
Use one consistent assessment scale across all stations.
Match players appropriately for contact activities.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Station 1, defenders identify natural or coach-created pressure triggers.
The observer assesses cue recognition, communication and collective pressing.
At Station 2, defenders respond to kick fakes, handball fakes and evasive movements.
The observer assesses patience, footwork and tackle timing.
At Station 3, defenders manage a numerical disadvantage and direct possession towards a trap.
The observer assesses delay, space protection and recovery integration.
At Station 4, defenders hand over crossing receivers while maintaining a high press.
The observer assesses communication, structural discipline and receiver pressure.
At Station 5, players complete repeated pressure actions under controlled fatigue.
The observer assesses deceleration, head position, wrap quality and recovery.
At Station 6, players respond to scoreboard, advantage and unpredictable phase changes.
The observer assesses match awareness, communication and tackle discipline.
Each behaviour receives:
2 points: Consistently demonstrated.
1 point: Demonstrated inconsistently or after correction.
0 points: Not demonstrated or performed unsafely.
Any reckless, high, low or late contact immediately stops the repetition.
Coaches record one technical strength, one decision-making priority and one recommended advanced drill for every player.
coachingPoints: Pressure should increase when genuine opposition vulnerability is recognised.
Defenders must remain balanced against deception.
Outnumbered players should delay and protect dangerous space.
Receiver handovers must preserve team structure.
Fatigue must not reduce legal tackle height or safe head placement.
Scoreboard and time context should influence pressure risk.
Players must distinguish live play from dead phases.
Team communication is assessed in every scenario.
Turnovers should lead to controlled attacking transition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify pressing opportunities accurately.
Whether defenders resist deceptive movements.
Whether outnumbered players protect dangerous space.
Whether pressure traps form after support arrives.
Whether crossing receivers are handed over cleanly.
Whether tackling technique remains safe under fatigue.
Whether players understand scoreboard and advantage situations.
Whether live football and direction changes are identified.
Whether communication remains clear.
Whether turnovers create effective attacking transition.

commonErrors.error: Players press without a genuine trigger.
commonErrors.correction: Hold shape until the opposition becomes vulnerable.

commonErrors.error: Defender reacts to every fake.
commonErrors.correction: Track the hips and remain grounded until genuine commitment.

commonErrors.error: Outnumbered defender attempts an early tackle.
commonErrors.correction: Delay and direct possession until support arrives.

commonErrors.error: Receiver handovers are late or unclear.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate before the crossing movement is completed.

commonErrors.error: Tackle height rises under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce workload and restore lower body position.

commonErrors.error: Players ignore scoreboard or time context.
commonErrors.correction: Require a clear scenario call before each repetition.

commonErrors.error: Defenders continue after play becomes dead.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and identify the new live phase.

commonErrors.error: Chaos changes create reckless contact.
commonErrors.correction: Slow, scan and confirm the ball carrier before tackling.

progressions: Increase attacking freedom at every station.
Reduce decision and recovery time.
Combine stations into a continuous match simulation.
Add scoreboard consequences to all scenarios.
Repeat the assessment under moderate match-specific fatigue.
regressions: Assess stations separately.
Predetermine pressure cues and attacking movements.
Replace live tackling with controlled pressure touches.
Reduce player numbers and field dimensions.
Return players to TK-080 before repeating the complete assessment.
successIndicators: Respond correctly to advantage and chaos.
Convert pressure into turnovers and controlled attack.
matchApplication: Advanced pressure requires more than effort. Players must recognise cues, manage risk, communicate changing responsibilities and execute safe tackles within complex and unpredictable match situations.
relatedDrills: TK-080 – Team Pressure and Ball-Movement Assessment

title: Broken-Play Pressure Reorganisation
primarySkill: Reorganising pressure after defensive structure breaks down
objective: Develop the ability to rapidly rebuild connected pressure after a deflection, missed disposal, unexpected turnover or positional breakdown disrupts the original defensive structure.
groundSize: A grid approximately 30 metres long and 24 metres wide with central and outside scoring gates.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two evenly matched teams.
Mark one central scoring gate and two outside gates at each end.
Begin with one team in structured possession.
Position defenders in a connected shape.
The coach keeps several footballs outside the grid.
At unpredictable moments, the coach creates a broken-play event by calling a deflection, turnover, loose ball or new possession location.
The original football becomes dead when a new football is introduced.
Players must immediately identify the live phase and reorganise.
howTheDrillWorks:
One team begins moving the football through the grid.
The defending team applies connected pressure.
The coach creates an unexpected broken-play event.
Players release all dead-ball contact and locate the new live football.
The team without possession identifies the nearest balanced pressure defender.
Other defenders recover towards the corridor and most dangerous receivers.
Defenders communicate new opponents and pressure roles.
Legal tackles are permitted once the new ball carrier is clearly identified.
The possession team scores two points through the central gate and one point through an outside gate.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover within six seconds of the broken-play event.
Play continues until a score, stoppage or secure possession.
Reset from a different initial structure.
coachingPoints: Confirm which football and direction are live.
Release previous opponents immediately when the phase changes.
Recover through dangerous central space before searching widely.
The nearest balanced defender pressures the ball carrier.
Supporting defenders identify receivers and close easy exits.
Communicate role changes early.
Avoid sprinting blindly towards the football.
Restore balance before attempting contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
How quickly players recognise the broken-play event.
Whether dead-ball contact is released.
Whether defenders recover through central space.
Whether the correct player applies pressure.
Whether opponents and receivers are reassigned.
Whether communication remains clear.
Whether tackle technique remains controlled during confusion.

commonErrors.error: Players continue competing for the dead football.
commonErrors.correction: Stop, scan and identify the new live phase immediately.

commonErrors.error: Every defender runs directly towards the new ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one pressure player and protect receivers with the others.

commonErrors.error: Defenders recover towards the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Recover through the corridor before spreading to opponents.

commonErrors.error: Players retain old opponent responsibilities.
commonErrors.correction: Reassign opponents based on the new football position.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives recklessly after the phase change.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate and confirm legal contact range before tackling.

commonErrors.error: Communication stops during confusion.
commonErrors.correction: Require immediate calls for ball, opponent and direction.

progressions: Create two consecutive broken-play events.
Change the attacking direction as the new football is introduced.
Add a temporary numerical advantage.
Remove coach calls and use physical deflections to create natural chaos.
Continue into full-ground transition after a turnover.
regressions: Predetermine the new football location.
Pause briefly after the broken-play call.
Use pressure touches instead of tackles.
Reduce player numbers.
Use only one scoring direction.
successIndicators: Identify the live football and direction.
Create a tackle or turnover before structure fully resets.
matchApplication: Defensive structure frequently breaks down after smothers, deflections, poor disposals and unexpected turnovers. Teams that reorganise quickly can prevent broken play from becoming an uncontested scoring opportunity.

title: Interchange-Side Pressure Communication
primarySkill: Maintaining pressure near the interchange area
objective: Develop clear defensive communication and opponent handover when players enter or leave the field near the interchange side.
groundSize: A wing channel approximately 40 metres long and 22 metres wide, including a marked interchange zone.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a wing channel beside a designated interchange area.
Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
Place one substitute player from each team inside the interchange zone.
The coach controls when players exchange.
Mark one forward gate and one boundary release gate.
