The attacking team begins with possession.
Defenders must maintain pressure while identifying players entering and leaving the field.
Tackles remain controlled and legal.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins moving the football along the wing.
Defenders establish inside position and protect the forward gate.
The coach calls an interchange for one or both teams.
Players leaving the field move towards the interchange zone.
Incoming players enter and immediately take up an attacking or defensive role.
Defenders communicate opponent handovers involving the outgoing and incoming players.
The nearest balanced defender continues direct pressure on the ball carrier.
Supporting defenders protect the corridor and new receiver options.
Attackers score one point for entering the forward gate.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing a boundary stoppage.
Reset after a score, turnover or completed interchange sequence.
coachingPoints: Maintain focus on the live football during interchange movement.
Clearly identify which player is leaving and which player is entering.
Communicate opponent handovers before the incoming player becomes free.
Do not follow an outgoing opponent beyond the playing area.
Preserve inside and corridor position.
The nearest balanced defender continues pressuring the football.
Incoming defenders must scan before joining pressure.
Avoid congestion around the interchange line.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players recognise interchange movement.
Whether outgoing opponents are released appropriately.
Whether incoming players are identified.
Whether opponent handovers are communicated.
Whether the live ball remains pressured.
Whether central space remains protected.
Whether players avoid crowding the interchange area.

commonErrors.error: Defender follows an opponent towards or beyond the interchange line.
commonErrors.correction: Hand the player over and return attention to the live field.

commonErrors.error: Incoming attacker enters unopposed.
commonErrors.correction: Identify and communicate the new receiver before entry.

commonErrors.error: Incoming defender runs directly at the football.
commonErrors.correction: Scan opponents and team structure before applying pressure.

commonErrors.error: Defenders lose inside position during the interchange.
commonErrors.correction: Preserve corridor protection while roles change.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd the interchange gate.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain clear entry and exit lanes.

commonErrors.error: Pressure stops while players communicate.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one defender actively pressuring the ball carrier.

progressions: Conduct simultaneous interchanges.
Allow the incoming attacker to become an immediate receiver.
Add a switch-of-play option.
Continue into full-ground transition.
Remove the coach’s interchange warning.
regressions: Interchange one player at a time.
Pause briefly during the first rehearsals.
Predetermine the incoming player’s position.
Use pressure touches instead of tackles.
Reduce the channel width and player numbers.
successIndicators: Maintain pressure on the live football.
Complete safe tackles near the boundary.
matchApplication: Interchange movement can create temporary confusion and unmarked players. Clear communication allows teams to maintain pressure and defensive structure while personnel changes occur beside live play.

title: Slow-Possession Squeeze
primarySkill: Increasing pressure against slow opposition possession
objective: Teach defenders to recognise when slow opposition ball movement allows the defensive unit to compress space and create a coordinated pressure trap.
groundSize: A grid approximately 32 metres long and 24 metres wide with central and boundary lanes.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into possession and pressure teams.
Mark one central lane and two outside lanes.
The possession team begins at one end.
The coach may call “slow” to require a player to hold possession for two to three seconds before disposing.
Defenders begin in connected shape.
Slow possession acts as the trigger for the pressure unit to compress space.
The possession team attempts to move through the far scoring gate.
Tackles remain controlled.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins moving the football.
Defenders protect central space without overcommitting.
When a ball carrier is delayed, stationary or facing backwards, the nearest defender calls the press.
The ball defender closes the opponent’s easiest disposal side.
Supporting defenders move closer to nearby receivers.
Deeper defenders squeeze forward while protecting the long central option.
The possession team attempts to escape the pressure through a disposal or carry.
Defenders attempt to complete a legal tackle or force a rushed disposal.
The possession team scores one point for escaping through the far gate.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing possession backwards.
Reset after a score, turnover or stoppage.
coachingPoints: Maintain shape while the opposition moves the football quickly.
Increase pressure when possession becomes slow or stationary.
The nearest defender calls and initiates the squeeze.
Supporting defenders remove short release options.
Deeper defenders move forward without abandoning the long threat.
Approach from an angle that forces the ball carrier towards pressure.
Avoid pressing individually.
Maintain tackle balance as space closes rapidly.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders identify slow possession.
Whether the press call is immediate.
Whether supporting defenders compress together.
Whether nearby receivers are denied.
Whether deeper defenders maintain useful coverage.
Whether the ball carrier is forced backwards or wide.
Whether the eventual tackle remains controlled.

commonErrors.error: Defenders remain passive during slow possession.
commonErrors.correction: Recognise the delay as a trigger to compress space.

commonErrors.error: One defender presses without support.
commonErrors.correction: Call the squeeze and wait for teammates to move.

commonErrors.error: Supporting defenders chase the football.
commonErrors.correction: Close receivers and disposal lanes instead.

commonErrors.error: Deeper defender moves too close and concedes the long kick.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain enough depth to protect the dangerous long option.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives upright and high.
commonErrors.correction: Decelerate and lower through the hips.

commonErrors.error: Team squeezes while the opposition is moving quickly.
commonErrors.correction: Hold shape until possession genuinely slows.

progressions: Remove the coach’s “slow” call and use natural possession cues.
Reduce the grid size.
Add an attacking spare.
Allow longer kicks.
Continue into attack after a turnover.
regressions: Predetermine which possession becomes slow.
Pause play at the press trigger.
Use handball only.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Reduce player numbers.
successIndicators: Force backwards, wide or rushed disposal.
matchApplication: Slow opposition possession gives defenders time to compress space and remove exits. Teams that recognise this opportunity can turn passive containment into coordinated turnover pressure.

title: Mark-and-Play-On Trap
primarySkill: Pressuring an opponent who plays on after a mark
objective: Develop the ability to legally establish the mark, recognise play on and rapidly close the ball carrier while teammates remove the immediate disposal options.
groundSize: A grid approximately 22 metres long and 16 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position a kicker at one end of the grid.
Place a receiver in the centre with a direct defender.
Position two supporting attackers and two supporting defenders nearby.
Mark the protected area around the expected mark location.
The receiver may hold, play on immediately or fake play on.
Defenders must remain legal until play on is called or clearly initiated.
Mark a scoring gate beyond the receiver.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker delivers a controlled pass to the receiver.
The receiver completes the mark.
The direct defender establishes the mark outside the protected area.
Supporting defenders position to close likely handball and short-kick options.
The receiver chooses whether to hold or play on.
Once play on is called or clearly initiated, the direct defender closes immediately.
Supporting defenders remove the easiest release options.
The ball carrier attempts to cross the scoring gate or dispose to a teammate.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing the player back over the mark or towards the boundary.
Attackers score one point for a clean exit.
Rotate all roles.
coachingPoints: Respect the mark and protected area.
Establish balanced body position while standing the mark.
Watch the player’s hips and movement rather than guessing.
React immediately when play on begins.
Approach from the side that removes the easiest disposal.
Supporting defenders close likely receivers before the play-on movement.
Avoid contact before play on.
Complete the tackle without carrying momentum into late contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders remain outside the protected area.
Whether the player standing the mark stays balanced.
Whether play on is recognised immediately.
Whether supporting defenders cover likely receivers.
Whether the pressure angle influences the ball carrier.
Whether early or late contact is avoided.
Whether the trap remains connected.

commonErrors.error: Defender enters the protected area.
commonErrors.correction: Hold the legal mark position until play on is called.

commonErrors.error: Player standing the mark becomes flat-footed.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain balanced readiness without moving illegally.

commonErrors.error: Defender guesses play on and contacts early.
commonErrors.correction: React only to clear movement or the official call.

commonErrors.error: Supporting defenders watch the mark rather than receivers.
commonErrors.correction: Close the likely release options before play on.

commonErrors.error: Ball defender approaches directly and is evaded.
commonErrors.correction: Close from an angle that removes the preferred side.

commonErrors.error: Defender makes late contact after disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the tackle action once the football is cleanly released.

progressions: Allow the receiver to fake play on.
Add more support runners.
Use different mark locations, including boundary positions.
Continue play after the first disposal.
Introduce scoreboard and time-pressure scenarios.
regressions: Predetermine that the receiver will play on.
Use one support receiver only.
Slow the play-on movement.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Pause at the mark to organise positions.
successIndicators: Force retreat, boundary movement or turnover.
matchApplication: Players often attempt to escape pressure by playing on quickly after a mark. Defenders must remain legal, anticipate the likely options and react together when play resumes.

title: Spoil-to-Tackle Pressure
primarySkill: Applying immediate tackle pressure after an aerial spoil
objective: Teach defenders to transition from an aerial spoil into organised ground-level pressure on the player who collects the loose football.
groundSize: Contest areas approximately 18 metres by 16 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position one attacker and one defender for a controlled aerial contest.
Place two ground-level players from each team around the contest.
Position a kicker 18–25 metres away.
Mark two disposal targets outside the contest area.
The defender’s initial aim is to spoil safely.
Ground-level players compete after the football reaches the ground.
Full tackling begins once a player gains possession and reaches safe contact height.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker delivers the football to the aerial contest.
The aerial defender attempts a controlled spoil towards a designated safe area.
Ground-level players read the football’s drop.
The nearest player attempts to gain possession.
Defenders identify the ball winner immediately.
The nearest balanced defender closes and applies legal tackle pressure.
Other defenders protect the nearest disposal targets.
If the football remains loose, players continue competing safely.
The possession team scores one point for a clean disposal to a target.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing an ineffective disposal.
Rotate aerial and ground-level roles.
coachingPoints: Spoil away from the most dangerous attacking space where possible.
Land safely and regain balance before re-entering play.
Ground-level defenders should position front and square.
Identify the player who wins possession.
Avoid tackling while the player’s head remains over the football.
Close the disposal side as the collector rises.
Supporting defenders protect the outlet options.
Release immediately if the football spills.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the spoil is controlled and directed.
Whether aerial players land safely.
Whether ground-level defenders hold useful positions.
Whether the possession winner is identified quickly.
Whether contact is delayed until safe tackling height.
Whether outlet targets are covered.
Whether defenders react correctly to another spill.

commonErrors.error: Spoil is directed into dangerous central space.
commonErrors.correction: Aim towards the boundary or supporting defenders where possible.

commonErrors.error: Aerial defender falls into the ground contest.
commonErrors.correction: Land, regain balance and then re-enter.

commonErrors.error: Ground players stand behind the aerial contest.
commonErrors.correction: Establish front-and-square positions.

commonErrors.error: Defender tackles while the collector’s head is down.
commonErrors.correction: Control the exit and wait until the player rises.

commonErrors.error: All defenders attack the collector.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one pressure player and protect outlets with others.

commonErrors.error: Tackler continues holding after another spill.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and contest the football.

progressions: Allow the attacker to mark if the spoil is ineffective.
Add a second aerial attacker.
Continue live play after the first disposal.
Vary the kick’s height and direction.
Introduce a scoring target near goal.
regressions: Use a coach-directed spoil or ball drop.
Predetermine the ground-ball winner.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Reduce the number of ground-level players.
Use shorter kicks.
successIndicators: Apply legal pressure at safe height.
Create tackles, turnovers or ineffective disposals.
matchApplication: A spoil is only the first defensive action. Teams must organise immediately at ground level to prevent the opposition collecting and exiting cleanly after the aerial contest.

title: Press Recovery After Kick Over the Top
primarySkill: Recovering pressure after the defensive press is beaten
objective: Develop the ability to recover and rebuild pressure after an opposition kick travels over or through the first defensive line.
groundSize: Approximately half an oval from one wing to the opposite forward line.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position an attacking team inside its defensive half.
Position a high defensive press ahead of the football.
Place one or two deeper defenders behind the press.
Mark an attacking scoring gate beyond the deeper defenders.
The coach instructs the possession team to use a long kick over the first pressure line during selected repetitions.
Pressing defenders must turn and recover.
Deeper defenders delay the receiver until support arrives.
Tackles remain controlled.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins moving the football against the high press.
Defenders apply pressure and cover short receivers.
The possession team delivers a long kick over the first pressure line.
Deeper defenders move towards the receiver while protecting the direct scoring route.
Pressing defenders turn and recover through central space.
The nearest deeper defender corrals or pressures the receiver.
Recovering defenders close the next disposal options.
Once support reconnects, the nearest balanced defender attempts a legal tackle.
Attackers score two points for reaching the scoring gate and one point for retaining possession for ten seconds.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for delaying the attack until support arrives.
Reset from different kick locations.
coachingPoints: Recognise immediately when the first line has been beaten.
Turn and recover through the corridor.
Deeper defenders delay rather than charging recklessly.
Protect the direct scoring line.
Communicate the arrival of recovering support.
Close the receiver’s easiest forward option.
Increase tackle pressure once the defensive unit reconnects.
Avoid desperate rear contact.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
How quickly the first line turns and recovers.
Whether recovery routes protect central space.
Whether deeper defenders delay effectively.
Whether the receiver is prevented from attacking directly.
Whether support defenders close disposal options.
Whether pressure increases after reconnection.
Whether tackles occur from safe side-on positions.

commonErrors.error: Pressing defenders watch the kick instead of recovering.
commonErrors.correction: Turn immediately and sprint through central space.

commonErrors.error: Deeper defender charges and is evaded.
commonErrors.correction: Delay and protect the direct scoring route.

commonErrors.error: Recovering defenders run outside the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Recover inside the ball and protect the corridor.

commonErrors.error: Defender dives from behind.
commonErrors.correction: Continue recovering until a side-on position develops.

commonErrors.error: Support arrives but pressure remains passive.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate the reconnection and increase controlled pressure.

commonErrors.error: Several defenders chase the receiver and leave outlets free.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one ball defender and cover the next options.

progressions: Add an attacking overlap runner.
Allow the receiver to play on immediately.
Increase the kick distance.
Continue into full match transition.
Begin from an unexpected turnover.
regressions: Predetermine the kick target.
Reduce the distance behind the press.
Use pressure touches instead of tackles.
Begin with more deeper defenders.
Pause after the kick to identify recovery roles.
successIndicators: Recognise when the press is beaten.
Complete a legal tackle after support arrives.
matchApplication: Aggressive presses will occasionally be beaten by a kick over the top. Effective teams recover immediately, delay the receiver and rebuild pressure rather than allowing one disposal to create an uncontested scoring chain.

title: Shepherd-Release Defensive Handover
primarySkill: Maintaining pressure when a ball carrier is protected by a shepherd
objective: Teach defenders to avoid illegal contact through a shepherd, communicate a defensive handover and continue pressure on the ball carrier from a safe angle.
groundSize: Lanes approximately 18 metres long and 10 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one ball carrier and one supporting attacker at one end of the lane.
Place two defenders between the attackers and the scoring line.
The supporting attacker may provide a legal controlled shepherd.
The shepherd must remain within legal distance and may not make high or forceful contact.
Defenders must communicate whether to fight around, switch or hand over.
A feeder and observer stand outside the lane.
Tackles remain controlled and upright.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder starts the ball carrier with a handball.
The supporting attacker moves into a legal shepherding position.
The nearest defender reads the shepherd and chooses a safe route around it.
The second defender communicates whether to switch onto the ball carrier.
If the first defender is delayed, the second defender becomes the primary pressure player.
The released defender recovers to the supporting attacker or next disposal option.
The nearest balanced defender completes a legal tackle when safe range develops.
Attackers score one point for crossing the scoring line.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing a backwards disposal.
Rotate all roles after each repetition.
coachingPoints: Recognise the shepherd before entering contact.
Avoid charging directly through the supporting player.
Communicate whether to stay, switch or hand over.
The defender with the clearest path pressures the ball carrier.
The delayed defender recovers to the support attacker.
Maintain vision of the ball carrier while navigating the shepherd.
Re-establish balance before tackling.
Keep all shepherd and tackle contact legal and controlled.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders identify the shepherd early.
Whether direct collision with the shepherd is avoided.
Whether communication occurs before the ball carrier escapes.
Whether responsibility transfers cleanly.
Whether the delayed defender recovers to a useful opponent.
Whether the tackle is completed from balance.
Whether the shepherd remains legal.

commonErrors.error: Defender runs directly into the shepherd.
commonErrors.correction: Move around the body and communicate a handover.

commonErrors.error: Both defenders attack the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate one pressure defender and one support-opponent defender.

commonErrors.error: Delayed defender stops after being blocked.
commonErrors.correction: Recover to the shepherd or next receiver.

commonErrors.error: Switch call occurs too late.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate as soon as the shepherding line develops.

commonErrors.error: Tackler arrives off balance after changing route.
commonErrors.correction: Use adjustment steps before contact.

commonErrors.error: Shepherd contacts high or moves outside legal position.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce speed and reinforce legal shepherding technique.

progressions: Allow the shepherd to change sides.
Add a second support attacker.
Remove predetermined defender roles.
Continue play after the first disposal.
Introduce a boundary-side shepherd scenario.
regressions: Walk through the shepherd and switch pattern.
Predetermine which defender takes the ball carrier.
Use passive shepherd positioning.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Reduce lane length.
successIndicators: Maintain pressure on the ball carrier.
Complete legal tackles from balanced positions.
matchApplication: Shepherds are used to create space for ball carriers. Defenders must communicate and transfer responsibility rather than allowing one block to remove all pressure from the possession chain.
relatedDrills: TK-096 – Press Recovery After Kick Over the Top

title: Last-Five-Minutes Full-Field Press
primarySkill: Applying a full-ground press late in a match
objective: Develop a coordinated full-ground press for a team trailing late and needing to create possession without conceding an uncontested scoring transition.
groundSize: Full oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two match-positioned teams.
Set one team two to three goals behind with five minutes remaining.
The leading team begins with possession in its defensive half.
The trailing team establishes an aggressive full-ground press.
Use normal match disposal and positional rules.
Contact is match-like but must remain legal and appropriately supervised.
The coach controls restarts after scores, stoppages and out-of-bounds outcomes.
Rotate which team protects the lead.
howTheDrillWorks:
The match clock begins with the leading team in possession.
The leading team attempts to retain possession, exit defence and reduce time.
The trailing team protects central space and denies short safe receivers.
The nearest balanced defender applies pressure to the ball carrier.
Supporting defenders press likely receivers while maintaining coverage behind the ball.
On slow possession, poor disposal or isolated reception, the trailing team increases pressure.
Legal tackles and match-like contests continue throughout the scenario.
If the trailing team wins possession, it attacks goal immediately.
If the leading team exits the press, it attempts to score at the opposite end.
Continue until the clock expires.
Review the balance between aggressive pressure and defensive security.
coachingPoints: Understand score, time and required scoring rate.
Protect central and forward space.
Remove short possession options.
Identify genuine pressing triggers.
Maintain a spare or safety defender where possible.
Avoid every player chasing the football.
Preserve legal tackling technique under extreme urgency.
Attack directly but intelligently after winning possession.
Reset the press quickly after a score or stoppage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players understand the scoreboard requirement.
Whether the full-ground press remains connected.
Whether short receivers are denied.
Whether central space is protected.
Whether pressure increases on genuine triggers.
Whether defenders preserve coverage behind the press.
Whether tackles remain legal at match speed.
Whether turnovers are converted into scoring attempts.
Whether the press resets after stoppages.

commonErrors.error: Every player moves ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain enough coverage to defend an opposition escape.

commonErrors.error: Defenders press without a trigger.
commonErrors.correction: Hold structure until possession becomes vulnerable.

commonErrors.error: Short receivers are left uncontested.
commonErrors.correction: Position tighter and inside the safest options.

commonErrors.error: Players chase wide possession and open the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Protect central and forward space first.

commonErrors.error: Tacklers become reckless because of the clock.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain legal approach and contact standards.

commonErrors.error: Turnover is followed by a low-percentage disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the best scoring route before releasing the football.

commonErrors.error: Press does not reset after a stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish roles before the restart.

progressions: Reduce the time remaining.
Increase the scoreboard deficit.
Begin from a kick-in or boundary stoppage.
Give the possession team an additional spare.
Continue through multiple scores without pausing.
regressions: Use half an oval.
Reduce player numbers.
Predetermine the first pressing trigger.
Use controlled contact rather than full match-like tackling.
Increase the remaining time.
successIndicators: Complete legal tackles at match speed.
Reset pressure after stoppages and scores.
matchApplication: Late in a match, a trailing team may need to sacrifice conservative positioning to create turnovers. The challenge is increasing pressure without allowing one opposition disposal to break the entire defensive structure.

title: Elite Chaos Pressure Match Simulation
primarySkill: Applying complete pressure principles in unpredictable match play
objective: Challenge players to maintain safe tackling, connected team pressure and tactical decision making through unpredictable match-like changes in possession, numbers, direction and scoreboard context.
groundSize: Full oval or approximately three-quarters of an oval.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two match-positioned teams.
Begin with normal match play from a selected restart.
The coach holds spare footballs and scenario cards.
During play, the coach may introduce turnovers, numerical changes, altered scoring direction, reduced time, advantage calls or new restart locations.
Only one football is live unless the coach explicitly conducts a short two-ball awareness phase.
Contact is match-like but must remain legal.
Stop immediately for unsafe confusion or uncontrolled contact.
Use short match blocks with structured review between them.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from a stoppage, kick-in or centre restart.
Teams apply normal attacking and defensive structures.
The coach introduces an unexpected scenario change.
Players identify the live football, direction, score and player-number situation.
The defending team allocates one immediate pressure player.
Supporting defenders protect dangerous space and receivers.
Pressure rotates as possession changes.
Players select between tackling, corralling, smothering, delaying or supporting.
Turnovers remain live and teams transition immediately.
Goals and scoring outcomes are recorded.
Play continues for three- to five-minute blocks.
Between blocks, coaches review one pressure success and one structural breakdown.
coachingPoints: Identify the current phase before acting.
Maintain legal tackle standards regardless of confusion.
The nearest balanced defender pressures the ball carrier.
Supporting defenders protect dangerous space.
Communicate possession, direction and role changes.
Recognise whether the situation requires press, delay, corral or retreat.
Release immediately when play becomes dead.
Convert turnovers into controlled attack.
Rebuild structure quickly after every disruption.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
How quickly players process scenario changes.
Whether the live football and direction are identified.
Whether pressure roles are allocated.
Whether central and scoring space remain protected.
Whether defenders select appropriate pressure actions.
Whether communication remains effective under fatigue.
Whether tackling stays legal at match speed.
Whether turnovers create organised attack.
Whether team structure can be rebuilt after chaos.

commonErrors.error: Players act before identifying the new phase.
commonErrors.correction: Scan and confirm ball, direction and possession first.

commonErrors.error: Every defender reacts directly to the football.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one pressure player and protect space with others.

commonErrors.error: Players tackle during a dead-ball change.
commonErrors.correction: Release immediately and await the live restart.

commonErrors.error: Defenders continue pressing when delay is required.
commonErrors.correction: Recognise numerical disadvantage and protect dangerous space.

commonErrors.error: Communication becomes individual and unclear.
commonErrors.correction: Use consistent team language for pressure, switch, hold and recover.

commonErrors.error: Contact becomes reckless under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce block length and restore legal technique standards.

commonErrors.error: Turnovers are followed by rushed decisions.
commonErrors.correction: Secure first possession and identify the best transition route.

progressions: Reduce rest between blocks.
Increase scenario-change frequency.
Add complex scoreboard requirements.
Introduce temporary two-ball phases.
Allow captains to control tactical adjustments without coach instruction.
regressions: Use half an oval.
Limit scenario changes to one type per block.
Use controlled contact rather than match-like tackling.
Pause briefly after each scenario change.
Reduce player numbers and tactical options.
successIndicators: Apply pressure principles without constant coach direction.
matchApplication: High-level matches contain unpredictable changes that cannot be rehearsed exactly. Elite pressure depends on players independently reading the situation, communicating and applying the correct defensive response.
relatedDrills: TK-080 – Team Pressure and Ball-Movement Assessment

title: Elite Pressure Systems Assessment
primarySkill: Assessment of elite tackling and team-pressure systems
objective: Assess whether players can independently apply safe tackling and coordinated pressure systems across advanced tactical, transitional and match-scenario challenges.
groundSize: Full oval with five tactical assessment zones.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Construct five advanced assessment zones or scenarios.
Zone 1 assesses press-trigger recognition and slow-possession squeezing.
Zone 2 assesses stoppage, aerial-contest and ground-ball pressure.
Zone 3 assesses receiver handover, shepherd response and defensive reorganisation.
Zone 4 assesses recovery after the press is beaten and numerical-disadvantage defence.
Zone 5 assesses full-ground late-game and chaos-pressure systems.
Assign a lead coach and supporting observer to each zone.
Divide players into positional groups and rotate every nine to eleven minutes.
Use one consistent scoring system across all zones.
Contact is match-like only for physically prepared players.
howTheDrillWorks:
At Zone 1, defenders identify natural pressure triggers and compress slow possession.
Observers assess cue recognition, communication and collective movement.
At Zone 2, players pressure the first possession after a stoppage, spoil or ground-ball contest.
Observers assess opponent safety, tackle timing and outlet coverage.
At Zone 3, defenders manage receiver crossings, shepherds and unexpected structural breakdowns.
Observers assess handover quality, role reassignment and tackle support.
At Zone 4, defenders recover after a kick over the press or while outnumbered.
Observers assess delay, corridor protection and reconnection.
At Zone 5, teams complete late-game and chaos match simulations.
Observers assess tactical adaptation, full-ground pressure and turnover conversion.
Each behaviour receives:
2 points: Consistently demonstrated without coach assistance.
1 point: Demonstrated inconsistently or after prompting.
0 points: Not demonstrated or performed unsafely.
Any illegal or uncontrolled contact immediately stops the repetition.
Coaches record one technical strength, one tactical priority, one communication priority and one recommended progression for each player.
coachingPoints: Players should identify pressure triggers without coach direction.
The nearest balanced defender applies direct pressure.
Supporting defenders protect the most dangerous space and receivers.
Pressure must reorganise rapidly after broken play.
Receiver handovers and switches require early communication.
Outnumbered defenders should delay and direct rather than overcommit.
Match context should influence defensive risk.
Legal tackle height, safe head placement and immediate release remain mandatory.
Team leaders should organise pressure across the ground.
Turnovers should create controlled attacking transition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether players identify natural pressure triggers.
Whether pressure is coordinated across multiple defenders.
Whether vulnerable opponents are protected.
Whether stoppage and aerial-contest exits are pressured.
Whether receiver handovers occur early.
Whether shepherds are managed without illegal collision.
Whether defensive structure is rebuilt after breakdowns.
Whether outnumbered players delay effectively.
Whether full-ground pressure remains connected.
Whether match context influences decisions.
Whether tackle technique remains legal under fatigue.
Whether leadership communication reduces coach dependence.

commonErrors.error: Players wait for the coach to call the press.
commonErrors.correction: Require on-field leaders to identify and communicate triggers.

commonErrors.error: Pressure defenders act without receiver support.
commonErrors.correction: Connect the nearest defenders before increasing pressure.

commonErrors.error: Tacklers compromise safety around aerial or ground-ball contests.
commonErrors.correction: Delay contact until legal and safe tackling height develops.

commonErrors.error: Receiver handovers occur after separation.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate before the movement crosses defensive zones.

commonErrors.error: Defenders charge through shepherds.
commonErrors.correction: Move around, switch or hand over responsibility.

commonErrors.error: Players chase after the press is beaten.
commonErrors.correction: Recover through central space and delay until support reconnects.

commonErrors.error: Late-game pressure becomes reckless.
commonErrors.correction: Match aggression to scoreboard need while preserving legal technique.

commonErrors.error: Team structure disappears during chaos.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish ball pressure, corridor protection and receiver coverage in that order.

commonErrors.error: Turnovers produce rushed attacking disposals.
commonErrors.correction: Secure first possession and identify the highest-value transition option.

progressions: Complete all zones as one continuous full-ground simulation.
Remove most coach-generated prompts.
Add opponent-specific tactical patterns.
Increase scoreboard and time complexity.
Repeat the assessment under controlled match fatigue.
Use player-led review after each scenario.
regressions: Assess each zone separately.
Reduce contact from match-like to controlled.
Predetermine pressure triggers and attacking movements.
Reduce player numbers and field dimensions.
Return players to TK-080 or TK-090 before reassessment.
successIndicators: Protect dangerous space and vulnerable opponents.
Adapt to scoreboard and time context.
Complete legal tackles at match speed.
Convert turnovers into controlled attacking opportunities.
Lead pressure systems with minimal coach intervention.
matchApplication: The assessment measures whether players can independently apply advanced tackling and pressure systems at match intensity. Successful teams combine safe individual technique with collective positioning, communication, tactical adaptation and leadership across the entire oval.
relatedDrills: TK-080 – Team Pressure and Ball-Movement Assessment
TK-096 – Press Recovery After Kick Over the Top

title: On-Field Pressure Leadership Calls
primarySkill: Organising team pressure through player-led communication
objective: Develop on-field leaders who can identify the pressure situation, assign defensive roles and organise teammates without relying on coach instructions.
groundSize: A grid approximately 35 metres long and 28 metres wide with central and outside scoring gates.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into an attacking possession team and a defending pressure team.
Nominate one defensive leader for each repetition.
Mark one central scoring gate and two outside gates.
The attacking team begins with possession at one end.
The coach varies attacking numbers, starting positions and available space.
The defensive leader must organise the press before and during play.
Coaches remain silent during each live repetition.
Rotate the leadership role every two to three repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins moving the football towards the scoring gates.
The defensive leader identifies the immediate threat.
The leader calls who pressures the ball carrier.
The leader assigns supporting defenders to central space and nearby receivers.
Defenders adjust their positions according to the call.
Pressure responsibility rotates after each disposal.
The leader continues communicating switches, holds, recoveries and pressing triggers.
Legal tackles are permitted when safe contact range develops.
Attackers score two points through the central gate and one point through an outside gate.
Defenders score two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing a backwards disposal.
After each repetition, teammates rate the clarity and timing of the leadership calls.
coachingPoints: Identify the greatest attacking threat first.
Use short, consistent and specific calls.
Assign one direct pressure player.
Protect the corridor and next receiver.
Communicate before teammates need to act.
Continue organising after the first disposal.
Adjust the call when the situation changes.
Leaders should direct rather than chase every contest themselves.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether the leader scans before communicating.
Whether calls identify specific players or spaces.
Whether teammates respond immediately.
Whether pressure roles remain clear after disposals.
Whether central space stays protected.
Whether the leader adapts when the initial plan breaks down.
Whether communication improves team tackling opportunities.

commonErrors.error: Leader gives several conflicting instructions.
commonErrors.correction: Use one priority call at a time.

commonErrors.error: Calls occur after the receiver gains possession.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate while the football is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Leader follows the football and loses awareness.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a position that allows scanning of the full structure.

commonErrors.error: Pressure player is not identified.
commonErrors.correction: Name or point to the nearest balanced defender.

commonErrors.error: Teammates ignore the call.
commonErrors.correction: Establish common team language and require verbal acknowledgement.

commonErrors.error: Leader stops communicating after the first contest.
commonErrors.correction: Continue organising until possession is secured or play ends.

progressions: Remove the nominated leader and require leadership to emerge naturally.
Add scoreboard and time-pressure scenarios.
Change attacking numbers during live play.
Allow the attacking team unrestricted kicks and switches.
Require different players to lead each field zone.
regressions: Give the leader several seconds to organise before play begins.
Predetermine the first attacking disposal.
Reduce player numbers.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Allow the coach to prompt the first leadership call.
matchApplication: Pressure systems fail when players wait for coaches to organise them. On-field leaders must identify threats, allocate roles and maintain defensive connection throughout live play.

title: Opposition Exit Pattern Recognition
primarySkill: Recognising and countering repeated opposition exit patterns
objective: Teach defenders to recognise repeated opposition ball-movement patterns and adjust positioning to pressure the intended receiver or exit lane.
groundSize: Defensive 50 and an area extending approximately 30 metres beyond the arc.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position an exit team inside defensive 50.
Position a pressure team across likely short, wide and central options.
Select three opposition-style exit patterns:
Short kick followed by handball overlap.
Boundary kick followed by corridor switch.
Long kick to a central target.
Do not initially tell the pressure team which pattern will be used.
Repeat each pattern several times before allowing live variation.
Mark central and wide exit gates.
Rotate attacking and defending roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The exit team begins with possession near goal.
The attacking group executes one selected exit pattern.
Defenders apply normal pressure and observe the movement.
After several repetitions, defenders briefly discuss the cues identifying each pattern.
Play restarts without announcing the selected pattern.
Defenders attempt to recognise the pattern earlier.
The nearest defender pressures the first receiver.
Supporting defenders adjust towards the expected second or third possession.
Legal tackles are permitted after possession is established.
The exit team scores two points for a central exit and one point for a wide exit.
The pressure team scores two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for disrupting the intended pattern.
coachingPoints: Observe starting positions and early receiver movement.
Identify repeated cues rather than guessing.
Communicate the likely pattern as soon as evidence appears.
Pressure the current ball carrier while preparing for the next possession.
Avoid abandoning direct responsibilities too early.
Adjust positioning without opening a more dangerous alternative.
Move while the football is travelling.
Continue pressure if the opposition abandons the expected pattern.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether defenders recognise repeated starting cues.
Whether players communicate the likely exit.
Whether the first receiver is pressured.
Whether supporting defenders anticipate the next possession.
Whether the defensive adjustment remains connected.
Whether players adapt when the attacking team changes the pattern.
Whether tackle opportunities increase through anticipation.

commonErrors.error: Defenders memorise the pattern but stop reading live play.
commonErrors.correction: Use cues as information, not as a fixed prediction.

commonErrors.error: Player leaves a direct opponent too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold responsibility until the pattern is confirmed.

commonErrors.error: Defenders identify the pattern but do not communicate.
commonErrors.correction: Require an immediate team call.

commonErrors.error: Pressure focuses only on the final receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Affect the first and second possessions to disrupt timing.

commonErrors.error: Team over-adjusts and concedes another exit.
commonErrors.correction: Preserve central and dangerous space while adapting.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop when the opposition changes the pattern.
commonErrors.correction: Return to normal pressure principles immediately.

progressions: Allow the exit team to disguise one pattern as another.
Add a fourth exit pattern.
Introduce opponent-specific match footage before the drill.
Remove pattern repetition and use fully random selection.
Continue play into full-ground transition.
regressions: Announce the pattern before each repetition.
Walk through receiver movements.
Reduce the number of attacking options.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Pause after the first disposal for defensive adjustment.
successIndicators: Adapt when the opposition changes its movement.
matchApplication: Teams frequently use rehearsed exits and ball-movement patterns. Recognising these cues allows defenders to arrive earlier, pressure intended receivers and disrupt the opposition’s preferred method of transition.

title: Ruck-Tap Follow-Up Tackle
primarySkill: Pressuring the first possession from a ruck tap
objective: Develop the ability to read a ruck tap, identify the likely receiver and apply immediate legal tackle pressure to the first possession.
groundSize: A stoppage circle approximately 10 metres in diameter with four exit gates 10 metres beyond it.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position two rucks for a controlled contest.
Place two or three midfielders from each team around the stoppage.
Mark four exit gates representing front, back, inside and outside clearance directions.
Nominate several possible tap zones.
The rucks may tap to any zone.
Midfield defenders begin in realistic accountable positions.
Full tackling begins after possession is established.
Rotate ruck and midfield roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach throws the football up for the ruck contest.
Rucks compete and direct the tap towards a chosen zone.
Midfielders read the ruck body position and football direction.
The possession winner attempts to exit through a gate or handball to a teammate.
The nearest balanced defender applies immediate pressure.
Supporting defenders protect the nearest receiver and dangerous exit.
Legal tackles are permitted once possession is established.
The possession team scores two points for a clean front or central exit and one point for a wide or backwards exit.
The defending team scores two points for a tackle or turnover and one point for forcing a secondary stoppage.
Reset after an exit, turnover or stoppage.
Repeat with different ruck and midfield starting positions.
coachingPoints: Read the ruck’s body angle and likely tap direction.
Maintain awareness of direct opponents.
React on the tap rather than waiting for full possession.
The nearest balanced defender pressures the receiver.
Supporting defenders protect the next handball and dangerous exit.
Lower tackle height as the receiver gathers from below waist level.
Avoid contacting a player before possession is established.
Continue pressure if the football spills.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Observe:
Whether midfielders read ruck cues.
Whether defenders maintain opponent awareness.
Whether movement begins on the tap.
Whether the possession winner is pressured immediately.
Whether the next receiver is covered.
Whether tackle height remains legal.
Whether a spill produces continued pressure.

commonErrors.error: Defender watches only the ruck contest.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain awareness of the direct midfield opponent.

commonErrors.error: Player reacts after the receiver has accelerated.
commonErrors.correction: Move as soon as the tap direction becomes clear.

commonErrors.error: Several defenders collapse on the first possession.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one pressure defender and protect exits with others.

commonErrors.error: Tackler contacts before possession.

commonErrors.error: High contact occurs on a low gather.

commonErrors.error: Defenders stop after the football spills.
commonErrors.correction: Release and continue the ground-ball contest.

Add outside midfield receivers.
Continue play into a forward entry.
Use boundary throw-ins and ball-ups.
Add scoreboard consequences for clean central clearances.
regressions: Predetermine the tap direction.
Use a coach-directed tap.
Reduce the number of midfielders.
Replace tackling with pressure touches.
Pause after the tap to identify responsibilities.
successIndicators: Move before possession is fully established.
